roster.name: Aaron Rodgers
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Ashton Jeanty
roster.reason: The Aug 23 ankle sprain was a non-issue for the Sept 13 opener — Jeanty was off the injury report entirely and delivered a workhorse Week 1 in Las Vegas' game vs. Miami: 23 carries for 102 yards plus 6 catches for 45 yards and 2 receiving TDs (27 touches, 2 total TDs). Confirmed as the clear lead back over rookie Mike Washington Jr., who saw no meaningful role in Week 1. Reaffirmed the workhorse role with 25 total touches (21 carries/48 yards, 4-of-7 targets/15 yards) in the Raiders' 26-14 upset of the Chargers in Week 2, but had a late-game injury scare (returned to finish the game) and dropped 3 passes — worth a brief watch, not yet a designation change (CBS Sports, NBC Sports). NEW (10/8): downgraded to a limited practice participant Thursday with a foot issue layered on top of the ankle he's been managing since exiting Week 4's loss to Kansas City (hobbled off in the 3rd quarter, returned in the 4th). Raiders haven't signaled real concern about Sunday's game vs. New England and one outlet still expects him active, but worth tracking given the back-to-back-day downgrade (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, Newsweek, 10/8). CLEARED (10/12): played through the ankle/foot combo with no reported setback in Sunday's Week 5 loss at New England (Patriots won 45-17); specific carry/yardage totals for the game could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update. Remains the clear lead back in Las Vegas' (now 3-2) backfield.

roster.name: Blake Corum
roster.reason: RB2 behind Kyren Williams in a ~65:35 split that has been fluid through camp. Carried a near-even Monday-night workload alongside Kyren Williams (combined 164 rush yards) in the win over the Giants — the split continues to run closer to 50/50 than a clean Williams-lead role (CBS Sports/RotoWire).

roster.name: Malik Nabers
roster.reason: CLEARED: the shoulder that "popped out" (and back in) during Week 2's loss at the Rams came back with clean X-rays; Nabers was a full practice participant that Thursday and the ESPN status flipped from Questionable to Active ahead of Week 3 at Tennessee. Told reporters: "Good result. I'm smiling, I'm out there, playing, catching the ball, so good results... I'll be fine" (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Giants.com, 9/24). UPDATE: played Week 3 and led the Giants with 5 catches on 6 targets for 26 yards (27% target share) in a 12-7 win over Tennessee — a quiet, low-yardage line but with no ill effects reported from the shoulder (NBC Sports, CBS Sports/RotoWire, 9/27-28). The bigger Week 4 storyline is the QB change, not the shoulder: starter Jaxson Dart is out with a knee injury and Jameis Winston is set to start at QB going forward, which beat writers flag as a likelier drag on Nabers' target quality/fantasy ceiling than the now-resolved shoulder issue (CBS Sports, 9/29-30). NEW (10/8): flipped to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington after not practicing Wednesday with a knee issue (Giants' official injury report, giants.com, 10/7) -- notable given his 2025 season ended with a torn ACL/meniscus in the same knee, though no beat writer has reported a new tear or setback. Treat as a practice-report flag to watch through Friday, not a confirmed re-injury. CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington -- no setback reported from the knee soreness that had him DNP Wednesday (the knee is the same one that ended his 2025 season with a torn ACL/meniscus, but no new tear or setback has been reported). HC/beat coverage from the Giants was cautiously upbeat all week (bolavip, Newsweek, 10/7-9).

roster.name: Tetairoa McMillan
roster.reason: 2025 AP Offensive Rookie of the Year (70/1,014/7); profiles as a safe WR2 (~WR18-20) capped by Carolina's low-volume passing offense, with Jalen Coker now adding real target competition.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Puka Nacua
roster.reason: Missed Monday Night Football vs. the Giants (9/21) with a hip/groin issue and stayed OUT all last week; HC Sean McVay confirmed there's no hernia involved. CONFIRMED: sat out Week 3's 30-26 loss at Denver (9/27) as expected off the DOUBTFUL tag — his second straight missed game with the groin/hip issue. UPDATE (9/28-29): McVay said the Rams are "hopeful" Nacua can return for Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia, but has since tempered that to "to be determined" and confirmed Nacua will again be limited in practice this week. The team still views it as a short-term issue and believes he's capable of playing now, just not at full explosiveness — no new setback or structural diagnosis, and surgery/IR remain off the table for now (CBS Sports, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, 9/28-29). Keeping Short-Term Injury tag; Davante Adams remains the clear top target in his absence. UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia. Nothing new medically — this reflects the calendar reaching the week HC Sean McVay has targeted since Week 2. McVay called himself "hopeful" Nacua plays (9/28), described the injury as "almost like pre-hernia" soreness, and said there's "no consideration" of IR; Adam Schefter reports the Rams don't believe surgery will be needed. A follow-up read was more guarded ("to be determined"), so treat this as genuinely 50/50 with a slight lean toward playing, final call likely Friday practice status (NBC Sports, ESPN, CBS Sports, 9/28-29). Davante Adams remains the top target if he sits again. CLEARED TOWARD PLAYING (10/1-2): logged a full practice Thursday after a limited Wednesday session, with McVay firmly expecting him to play Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia; surgery is not currently expected (SI, NBC Sports, 10/1). SEPARATE STORYLINE — Personal Conduct Policy: Nacua remains under an active NFL conduct-policy review tied to a civil lawsuit (alleging a bite and an antisemitic remark) and has begun steps toward a diversion program on related misdemeanor charges. He has not been placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List and ESPN's Adam Schefter says there's a real chance he plays out the season with no discipline, but the league can still act at any point since there's no decision deadline — a background risk to monitor, separate from the groin injury (CBS Sports, Fox News/Outkick, 10/1-2). CLEARED (10/3): officially off the injury-worry list -- full practice participant all week and HC Sean McVay firmly expects him to play Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia with no game-time-decision framing anymore; surgery was never on the table. Downgrading tag from Short-Term Injury to Healthy. Separate conduct-policy review (civil suit) remains unresolved and worth continued background monitoring, but is no longer tied to his on-field availability. CONFIRMED (10/4-5): played a full workload at Philadelphia in Week 4, posting 14 catches, 199 yards and a rushing TD (our stats database has this at 27.7 fantasy points) despite the Rams' loss (ESPN gameId 401772839). The hip/groin issue (variably described as hip vs. groin, unrelated to his earlier psoas issue) did not limit his role at all -- team-leading target share in the loss, with no lingering concern reported as of 10/5. Upgrading tag from Healthy to include WR1 Lock given the workload. Note: the separate NFL conduct-policy review (civil suit) remains open and unrelated to his on-field availability -- continue monitoring in the background. UPDATE (10/13): put up a monster line in the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday Night Football (10/12) -- 17 catches (a career-high 24 targets) for 138 yards and a TD. The Rams fell to 2-3 despite the huge game, partly because K Harrison Mevis missed two field goals, including a potential game-winner in overtime (see his note) -- therams.com, Deseret News, AP/Boston Globe.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.reason: Dislocated his left (non-throwing) elbow — the same joint's 2nd dislocation within under a year — late in the first half of Washington's 37-20 Week 2 loss to Dallas (Sun 9/20); X-rays showed no fracture. Ruled out for Week 3 vs. Seattle, with Marcus Mariota named starting QB (Dan Quinn, 9/22 presser). NEW (AP, ~9/23): imaging and multiple specialist opinions found NO ligament damage, and Daniels will NOT need surgery; the Commanders are not placing him on IR "for now" (FOX Sports/AP, NBC Sports/PFT, ProFootballRumors) — a real upgrade from Tuesday's total-uncertainty read. Still no firm return timetable — HC Dan Quinn has declined to commit to one, with re-evaluation expected to continue toward Washington's Week 7 bye. Mariota remains the starter in the interim, and the recurring nature of the injury (2nd dislocation of the same elbow in <1 year) keeps real season-long variance in play even without surgery. UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Week 4 (in London vs. Indianapolis). He returned to practice this week and traveled with the team, and per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz told teammates he's foregoing surgery and felt he "owed it to them" to return as fast as possible (RotoWire, Washington Times, Hogs Haven, 9/28). HC Dan Quinn said he isn't sure yet if Daniels plays "in six days" but that he "isn't far off" and will practice "in some form" this week. Read this as soft/early-stage QUESTIONABLE, not a real lean toward playing — nearly every outlet still has Marcus Mariota as the presumptive Week 4 starter pending how practice reps go Wed-Fri. CONFIRMED OUT (10/2-3): ruled out for Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Colts in London -- ESPN's Adam Schefter does not believe Daniels will be active despite making the trip and practicing in some form. Marcus Mariota remains the favorite to start unless Daniels takes the bulk of first-team reps, which hasn't happened (CBS Sports, RotoBaller, Commanders.com, 10/1-3). No surgery still planned this season; recurring elbow dislocation keeps real multi-week variance in play. CONFIRMED (10/5): did not play Week 4 vs. the Colts in London; Marcus Mariota started for a second straight game and Washington won 17-16 (Colts.com). Per Adam Schefter, Daniels will "eventually need surgery" on the elbow (this is the THIRD dislocation of the same non-throwing elbow within under a year) but is deferring it to the offseason and will likely play in a brace whenever he returns -- no practice/return timeline has been given as of 10/5 (NBC Sports). Given the recurring nature of the injury and no near-term surgical or return plan, upgrading tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury; Mariota remains the starter indefinitely. IMPROVING, REVISED (10/7): real progress this week -- HC Dan Quinn said Daniels is set for a full Wed-Thu-Fri practice week with the goal of starting Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants, wearing the elbow brace (ESPN, TSN). Added urgency: backup Marcus Mariota suffered his own MCL sprain vs. the Colts, making 7th-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis the emergency option if Daniels can't go. Some practice-report aggregators still show a "limited" tag, so treat this as a real but not fully resolved Questionable rather than a lock. Revising tag down from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch given the firm full-practice/start-Sunday trajectory -- no longer an open-ended absence. CLEARED (10/8): officially flipped from Questionable to Active ahead of Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants after a full Wednesday practice; per Jay Glazer, Washington plans to start Daniels in the elbow brace, and Tom Pelissero reports the team remains hopeful he returns to the starting role (ESPN, CBS Sports, 10/7-8). Backup situation is in flux -- Marcus Mariota aggravated the same MCL he had surgically repaired in 2022 and is doubtful/out, which only reinforces that Washington needs Daniels back now. CONFIRMED HEALTHY RETURN (10/12): started Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants in the elbow brace and delivered a big dual-threat performance in a 27-27 overtime tie -- 17-of-25 passing for 199 yards with no interceptions (despite 5 sacks), plus 103 rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns on 9 carries. No setback to the surgically-pending elbow reported. Washington lost a late chance to win in OT after a Daniels scramble ran out the clock instead of spiking it.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.reason: Ranked QB11 for 2026 — with Etienne now gone to New Orleans, more of the offense funnels through Lawrence's arm and legs; expected to throw 30+ TDs for the first time. UPDATE: threw 3 TD passes (including to Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers) in Jacksonville's 35-6 rout of New England in Week 3 (9/27) — a strong bounce-back performance for the passing game (Jaguars.com, SI/OnSI).

roster.name: Bhayshul Tuten
roster.reason: Illness that sent him home from a Sept 2 practice was a non-issue by kickoff — logged a full workload in Jacksonville's Week 1 win over Cleveland with 15 carries for 66 yards plus a catch for 22 yards. UPDATE: posted a season-high 73 yards on 15 touches with 5 broken tackles in Jacksonville's 35-6 rout of New England in Week 3 (9/27) — a clear positive trendline heading into Week 4 (Jaguars.com, SI/OnSI).

roster.name: Carnell Tate
roster.reason: Took a hard hit in Monday practice and missed Wednesday's session with dizziness/stiffness — evaluated but not diagnosed with a concussion, has since returned to practice with no Week 1 concern. Rookie WR with rising fantasy stock as the direct beneficiary any time Wan'Dale Robinson is banged up. 2026 1st-round pick (No. 4 overall, Ohio State) — Tennessee's top rookie weapon for Cam Ward alongside slot man Wan'Dale Robinson. NEW (10/8): added to Tennessee's injury report Thursday with a back issue, downgraded to limited after a full practice Wednesday -- a new ailment unrelated to the August practice-collision stiffness. Comes right after his best game of the season (9 catches, 145 yards in the Week 4 loss at Baltimore), so a limited Sunday vs. Houston would be a real hit to Cam Ward's passing game (Yahoo Sports/Titans beat, 10/8). QUESTIONABLE heading into the weekend; no final Friday designation found yet. CLEARED (10/12): HC Robert Saleh's 'good to go' read on the back tightness held up -- Tate played through it with no setback or in-game exit reported in Sunday's 26-3 Week 5 loss at Houston (Titans fall to 0-5). Specific Week 5 catch/yardage totals could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update; revisit once a box score source becomes available. No new injury concern entering Week 6.

roster.name: Dalton Kincaid
roster.reason: Sleeper-caliber TE1 upside (80/1,000/10 pace) after a 7 TD, 14.6 YPC 2025 — durability is the real question, but camp reports have his snap share trending up even with Knox/Hawes healthy. The breakout thesis showed up in real games: 7 catches on 8 targets for 95 yards and a TD in Thursday night's win over Detroit, his best game of the young season. PLAYED THROUGH IT (10/18): exited Sunday's 33-30 win at Las Vegas in the 3rd quarter with a rib injury and was briefly questionable to return, but came back in the 4th quarter and helped close out the win -- finished with 7 catches for 38 yards (had a TD nullified by a holding penalty) on a day Buffalo improved to 5-1 (CBS Sports, NBC Sports, DraftKings Network, 10/18). Today's QUESTIONABLE tag reflects that rib soreness still being managed, but Buffalo is on its Week 7 bye (next game isn't until Nov. 1 vs. Baltimore), so he has two full weeks to heal. Keeping Health Watch given he played through it with no larger setback. BYE-WEEK RESET (10/21): today's QUESTIONABLE-to-ACTIVE flip is procedural -- Buffalo is on its Week 7 bye (confirmed Fox Sports/NBC Sports bye-week lists), so there's no game this week for any designation to attach to. The rib injury that had him questionable to return in the Week 6 win over Las Vegas (10/18) has not been described as a long-term issue by any outlet found; he has two full weeks before Buffalo's next game (Nov. 1 vs. Baltimore) to heal. No new setback reported.

roster.name: Seahawks D/ST
roster.reason: Reigning Super Bowl champs and the #1-ranked defense in 2026 projections — led the NFL in scoring defense and led the league with 7 defensive/ST TDs in 2025. Elite, high-floor DST1. Worth monitoring: starting QB Sam Darnold left the Sept 9 opener with a hip injury; a Sept 10 MRI ruled out major structural damage but he's still expected to miss Week 2 at Arizona — a Drew Lock-led offense for that game could mean tougher field position/offensive support for the defense.

roster.name: Jordan Mason
roster.reason: Placed on injured reserve Sept 16 after further evaluation of the sore thumb from Minnesota's Week 1 win over Green Bay revealed a fracture requiring surgery — HC Kevin O'Connell said the exact moment of the break is unclear, but it escalated from what first looked like a bruise. IR's mandatory 4-game minimum rules him out through Week 5 (vs. Bears, at Bucs, vs. Dolphins, at Saints); O'Connell called the recovery "not expected to be long-term" beyond that window, putting a realistic return at Week 6 or later with no hard date confirmed. Minnesota promoted RB DeeJay Dallas from the practice squad and signed Jerome Ford to the practice squad as depth behind Aaron Jones.

roster.name: Jordyn Tyson
roster.reason: Hamstring injury in an August joint practice vs JAX; placed on IR with a return designation — out at least the first 4 games.

roster.name: Jonathon Brooks
roster.reason: CONFIRMED: officially placed on injured reserve Wednesday 9/23 after re-aggravating a groin/core-muscle injury late in Carolina's 34-3 Week 2 win over Atlanta (9/20) (Panthers.com; AP via Washington Post/US News) — the earlier "week-to-week, seeking opinions" framing has resolved into a hard IR move. AP source reporting: Brooks will undergo surgery to repair the core-muscle injury and is expected to miss a minimum of six weeks (IR floor is 4 games); a return later this season is still expected. Carolina signed S Isaiah Simmons off the practice squad to fill the vacated 53-man spot. Backfield touches now run through Chuba Hubbard (clear-cut RB1, no longer sharing the load) and AJ Dillon (RB2/short-yardage) — Rico Dowdle signed with Pittsburgh in the offseason and is NOT part of Carolina's backfield picture.

roster.name: C.J. Stroud
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.reason: Widely projected as the 2026 fantasy #1 overall pick — back-to-back 1,400+ rush-yard seasons plus 60+ catches gives him a McCaffrey-type dual-threat ceiling. The camp hold-in is fully resolved: signed a 3-year, $75M extension ($51M guaranteed) with Atlanta in early August 2026, ending the contract-driven absence before the season started (NFL.com). Backed up the elite billing with a dominant Thursday-night Week 3 performance in the 35-14 win over Green Bay: 29 carries for 194 yards and 2 rushing TDs, plus 2 catches for 19 yards — 213 total yards from scrimmage (CBS Sports, 9/24).

roster.name: Chase Brown
roster.reason: Top-5, arguably top-3 PPR RB potential — posted 7 top-12 weekly finishes even through Burrow's 2025 absence; Samaje Perine remains mild committee/handcuff risk. Backed up a strong Week 1 with 20 carries for 80 yards plus 3 catches on 5 targets in Cincinnati's 20-6 win over Houston in Week 2 — 42-of-60 snaps, 36 carries and 11 targets through two games confirms bell-cow usage (Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports).

roster.name: Christian Watson
roster.reason: No PUP/injury drama to open 2026 — signed a 4-year, $110.5M extension in June and entered the season atop Green Bay's WR depth chart, fully healthy. Delivered as the Packers' clear outside WR1 in the Week 1 win at Minnesota: 6 catches for 147 yards and 2 TDs on 8 targets, well ahead of Matthew Golden in target share. Kept it up in Thursday night's Week 3 loss at Atlanta (35-14): led the team with 7 catches on 10 targets for 96 yards and a TD (4-yard grab that opened the scoring) — remains Green Bay's clear top target earner even in a blowout loss (RotoWire/CBS Sports, 9/24).

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.reason: The groin injury was fully resolved for Week 1 — played through it with no setback, catching all 5 targets for 63 yards vs. Carolina. UPDATE: caught an 8-yard TD from Case Keenum in Chicago's 27-7 Week 3 upset of Philadelphia (Monday Night, 9/28) — his first score of the season, with Keenum starting in place of the injured Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.reason: Missed Week 1 (meniscus trim surgery in early September) and Week 2 at the Chargers, then came down to a Sunday game-time call for Week 3 vs. New Orleans. CLEARED AND DELIVERED: officially active roughly 2 hours before kickoff and made a monstrous 2026 season debut in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Saints — 10 catches on 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown (CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 9/27), instantly re-establishing himself as Las Vegas' clear top receiving option. No re-aggravation reported after the workload; Michael Mayer moves back to a clear TE2 role now that Bowers has cleared and produced in the same game. UPDATE (10/8): Bowers has carried a QUESTIONABLE tag in each of the last two weeks -- an illness (not his earlier knee issue) was the reported cause ahead of Week 4 vs. Kansas City, and the Raiders expected him to play (ESPN's Adam Schefter, 10/4); he's QUESTIONABLE again for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. New England, though the specific reason behind this week's tag hadn't been reported by beat writers as of Wednesday. CLEARED (10/8): upgraded from limited to a full practice participant Thursday on the knee, trending toward playing Sunday's Week 5 game vs. New England -- no setback reported from the illness-related QUESTIONABLE tag he carried into Week 4 (Yahoo Sports/Raiders beat, 10/8). NEW DESIGNATION (10/16): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag for the first time this week, but it's the same knee the Raiders have been proactively managing in practice all season, not a new injury -- limited Wednesday, upgraded to a full practice Thursday (10/14-10/15). FantasyPros projects him at 94% to play Sunday vs. Buffalo (10/18); this matches his standard early-week rest pattern rather than a real setback. CLEARED (10/17): logged back-to-back full practices Thursday and Friday and carries NO injury designation into Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Buffalo -- officially off the injury report entirely (NBC Sports, 10/16). Remains the overall TE1 play this week.

roster.name: Jalen Coker
roster.reason: Caught 8-of-9 targets in EACH of Carolina's first two games (Week 1: 8/138 yds/2 TD vs. Chicago; Week 2: 8/66 yds vs. Atlanta) with Bryce Young — became just the 3rd undrafted player since 1967 to reach 15+ catches, 200+ receiving yards and 2+ TDs through a team's first two games (Yahoo Sports/Heavy, 9/23). No longer just a presumptive WR2 behind McMillan — now viewed as a legitimate 1A/1B. UPDATE: played through the ankle issue that had triggered a Week 3 Questionable tag, but exited Sunday's 21-18 loss to Cleveland early with a new quad strain, finishing limited to 2 catches for 18 yards. Monday follow-up tests found nothing overly significant on the quad — described as a relatively minor strain. He's Questionable for Week 4 vs. Detroit, with his Wednesday-Friday practice activity set to determine availability (SI/OnSI, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 9/28-29). Downgrading tag from a standalone injury tier to Health Watch given the "relatively minor" framing and no ruled-out signal yet. WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/5): downgraded from QUESTIONABLE to OUT today -- the quad strain suffered vs. Cleveland in Week 3 (originally called "relatively minor" by Ian Rapoport) has not resolved on the Wed-Fri practice ramp-up as hoped. No multi-week timeline has been disclosed, but Carolina has an IR transaction history on this same quad earlier in the season, raising some risk the team manages it conservatively. Bumping tag from Health Watch to standard Injury given the confirmed missed game and recurrence on the same body part. REVISED TO LONG-TERM, CORRECTED (10/7): Carolina placed Coker on IR, and ESPN's David Newton reported an expected 4-to-6 game absence -- HC Dave Canales called it a "serious quad strain," a firmer and worse timeline than the earlier "relatively minor" read. Revising tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury given the confirmed 4+ game IR window. IMPORTANT CONTEXT: the Panthers are on their Week 5 BYE, so there is no Week 5 game/opponent for him either way -- today's QUESTIONABLE roster status is a placeholder, not a game-week designation. He's now inside his 21-day practice window (eligible to return from IR) but has not yet been designated to return; realistic target is Week 6 or later, post-bye. CLEARED (10/16): practiced in full Wednesday (10/14) with no designation on Carolina's injury report, ending the IR stint -- HC Dave Canales called him "on track" to play Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Philadelphia (10/18) (NBC Sports/Sharp Football, 10/13-14). Softening tag from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch; expect his workload eased in his first game back before he reclaims a full target share.

roster.name: Panthers D/ST
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Spencer Shrader
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.reason: Locked in as the top overall fantasy QB — top-9 in passing yards 5 of the last 6 years, top-7 in passing TDs every year, with real rushing/scramble equity on top. Historic Week 2 Thursday-night performance in a 41-31 win over Detroit: 317 total yards and 5 total TDs (3 pass, 2 rush), over 40 fantasy points — per ESPN, only the 3rd player in NFL history with 9 total TDs and 0 turnovers through a team's first 2 games (Mahomes 2018, Manning 2013 the others). NEW: banged up late in Week 3's win over the Chargers — took a helmet to the outside of his left knee in the 4th quarter and was seen favoring the leg postgame. No formal diagnosis announced, but medical analysts (Dr. David Chao) describe him as "more hurt than injured," floating a possible grade 1-2 MCL sprain that could range from full Week 4 availability to a 1-3 week absence (Buffalo Rumblings, SI, Yahoo Sports, 9/28-29). Officially Questionable entering Week 4 vs. New England and likely limited in practice early in the week — worth checking the Friday injury report before locking him in. UPDATE (9/30): the left knee scare from Week 3 is a non-issue — Allen practiced in full Wednesday with no brace or visible limitation, and HC Joe Brady said "I'm not concerned with Josh." He is NOT listed on the Week 4 injury report at all ahead of Sunday's game vs. New England (Buffalo Rumblings, CBS Sports, RotoWire, 9/30). Week 4 final (10/4): the knee was a total non-issue, but Buffalo lost its first game of the season, 29-26 at home to New England (fell to 3-1). Allen went 23/33 for 253 yards and 1 passing TD (34-yd to Keon Coleman) plus 5 carries for 4 yards and a rushing TD -- but threw a game-sealing INT with 1:14 left. He also became Buffalo's all-time TD leader on the score. No health concerns entering Week 5 (ESPN, Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 10/4).

roster.name: Tre Tucker
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: David Montgomery
roster.reason: Trade acquisition from DET leads the Houston backfield, and Joe Mixon's release clears out the only other real competition — but Woody Marks still holds real passing-down/receiving touches, so it remains a genuine committee, not a clear lead back. NEW (10/13): suffered a groin injury early in the 2nd quarter of Sunday's Week 5 win over Tennessee (26-3), exiting after just 5 carries for 11 yards (Houston Chronicle, RotoWire, ESPN, 10/11-12). HC DeMeco Ryans called it "week-to-week" Monday with no hard return date, matching today's flip to DOUBTFUL -- picking the standard Injury tier given the genuinely uncertain timeline. Woody Marks (see his note) took over as the lead back the rest of the game and is confirmed to handle the workload if Montgomery sits further; Ryans said Marks "will carry the load for us." UPDATE (10/15): no fresher practice-report confirmation found beyond HC DeMeco Ryans' Monday (10/12) "week-to-week" comments -- no official Wed/Thu Week 6 designation located via search yet. 4for4's analysis says he's "very likely" to miss Week 6, and flags that Houston's upcoming bye week could extend the absence further before a firm return estimate emerges. Woody Marks (see his note) is confirmed as the Week 6 lead back regardless. CONFIRMED OUT (10/16): officially ruled out for Sunday's Week 6 game at Jacksonville in London (10/18) with the groin injury suffered late in the Week 5 win over Tennessee, after zero practice reps Wednesday or Thursday. HC DeMeco Ryans calls it "week-to-week," with reporting (NBC Sports, National Football Post) pointing to a Week 7 vs. the Giants target return -- Houston's bye isn't until Week 8, so there's no extra cushion this week. Upgrading tag to Short-Term Injury given the firm ~1-week target; Woody Marks remains the clear lead back in the meantime. UPDATE (10/22): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip lines up with the new Week 7 practice-report cycle (Houston hosts the Giants Sun 10/25), but no independent beat reporting confirming his actual Wednesday practice participation was found as of this update -- one outlet speculates he could target a Week 7 return but explicitly flags that as unconfirmed, not an official report. Keeping the Short-Term Injury tier from last week's ~1-week target rather than overclaiming a confirmed recovery; recheck Thursday/Friday's report. Woody Marks remains the lead back in the meantime.

roster.name: Michael Mayer
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.reason: Clear backup, not a starter — Breece Hall re-signed and remains the workhorse; Allen competes with Isaiah Davis for change-of-pace touches. UPDATE (9/30): Breece Hall (thigh/quad) will not play Week 4, and Allen is set to start in his place — he flashed in relief during Week 3's loss to Detroit (4 carries for 14 yards and a TD) after Hall exited. Treat as the clear lead-back option for as long as Hall is out (CBS Sports, NBC Sports, SI/OnSI, 9/28). Week 4 final (10/4): took every single Jets RB carry in the 23-12 loss to Chicago -- 14 carries for 59 yards (4.2 YPC) plus 2 catches for 8 yards. Volume was capped by the Jets' anemic 32 offensive plays, not a snap-share concern. With Breece Hall still out (see his note, remains week-to-week with no firm return date), Allen looks like the clear every-down back rather than a committee piece -- upgrading tag from Depth Chart Battle to Depth Chart Secured (NBC Sports, NYJets.com, CBS Sports, 10/4-5). Week 5 final (10/11): career-best game with Breece Hall again out -- 24 carries for 116 yards (4.8 YPC) and the game-winning 22-yard TD run on 3rd down in a 17-12 win over Cleveland, playing 60 of 70 snaps (85.7%). Added 1 catch on 4 targets for 0 yards. Remains the clear lead back as long as Hall is out.

roster.name: Keon Coleman
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
roster.reason: Wasn't the clear lead back in Week 2 — White out-snapped him 36-23 in the Dallas loss (9/20) as the Commanders leaned on White's receiving in a trailing game script. Treat this as a genuine 2-man committee rather than a locked-in CM1 role, even after his confirmed Week 1 lead-back role vs. Philadelphia. NEW (10/8): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag in this week's injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants; specific injury type was not confirmed by beat writers as of Wednesday -- recheck once Washington's Thursday/Friday reports post. Still working as part of a 2-man committee with Rachaad White. CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants -- no setback reported from this week's unspecified issue. Still in a backfield mix with Rachaad White (also cleared, see his note); Washington waived depth piece Kaytron Allen this week, slightly simplifying the committee (RotoBaller, 10/8-9). Dropping the Health Watch tag now that he's cleared. NEW (10/15-16): a groin injury (recurring from Week 5) kept him off the practice field entirely both Thursday and Friday ahead of Monday night's Week 6 game at San Francisco (10/19) -- ESPN's John Keim flagged the Thursday absence as a real watch item. Re-adding the Health Watch tag given the back-to-back DNPs; no severity or ruled-out/doubtful designation confirmed yet, recheck Saturday's report. Rachaad White would see the bulk of the backfield work if he sits. CONFIRMED OUT (10/18, final): HC Dan Quinn confirmed Saturday that Croskey-Merritt is out for tonight's Monday Night Football Week 6 game at San Francisco (10/19) with the same recurring groin injury -- he did not practice at all this week (SI/Yahoo Sports Commanders injury reports, 10/17-18). Rachaad White (shoulder, cleared) and Austin Ekeler (chest, cleared) are set to handle the bulk of Washington's backfield work in his absence -- see White's note. PLACED ON IR (10/19-21): officially moved to injured reserve with a groin reinjury (first hurt in preseason, reaggravated in the Week 5 tie vs. the Giants) -- HC Dan Quinn called it a reinjury, and per Ian Rapoport he's out at least through Week 10 (NFL Network, RotoBaller, TSN, 10/19). Across 5 games this season he had 67 carries for 239 yards and 2 TDs in a committee with Rachaad White. Washington's backfield now projects as a White/Austin Ekeler/Jeremy McNichols (activated off IR Monday) committee in his absence. Upgrading tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury given the official IR move and the ~4-game minimum absence.

roster.name: Tyreek Hill
roster.reason: Suffered a severe left knee injury (dislocation with torn ACL/MCL/PCL and patella damage) on Sept 29, 2025 vs. New England, requiring surgery; Miami released him in February 2026 as expected. Remains an unsigned free agent as of Sept 2026 — has not retired, but has also not signed with any team. Publicly says his recovery "timeline looking real good" but has also said he still has "no power" in the left leg; agent Drew Rosenhaus has indicated doctors want to hold off on a comeback attempt until at least October 2026. Not rostered by any NFL team — unplayable/bench for now; monitor for a signing or workout announcement. UPDATE (10/13): still unsigned -- agent Drew Rosenhaus called the free-agency situation "fluid," telling reporters "I think a deal could happen anytime" and naming the Chiefs as a plausible contender fit given Hill's stated preference to sign only with a Super Bowl-caliber team needing WR help (RotoBaller, CBS Sports, 10/13). No team has signed him as of this update. Today's in-system flip from OUT to QUESTIONABLE does not correspond to any real NFL game-status designation since he isn't on any team's roster -- treat it as a data artifact, not real news. Remains unplayable/bench.

roster.name: Patrick Mahomes
roster.reason: The lingering "knee" injury-report notation from his offseason ACL/LCL recovery was a non-factor in Kansas City's Week 1 win over Denver — went 15/27 for 184 yards and 2 passing TDs (1 INT) and added 7 carries for 23 yards and a rushing TD.

roster.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
roster.reason: No lingering back/hamstring issue — exploded for 29 carries, 156 yards and 2 TDs plus 5 catches for 30 yards in Sunday's opener, the clear workhorse with Montgomery gone and Isiah Pacheco on IR. Ground game was quiet in Thursday night's loss to Buffalo (52 yards on 16 carries), but 6 catches and a receiving TD kept his fantasy floor strong — a reminder his receiving work is what makes him a true 3-down workhorse even on an off day rushing.

roster.name: Javonte Williams
roster.reason: New 3-yr/$24M deal after a career year: 252 att, 1,201 yds, 11 TD. Backups Davis, Blue, and Mafah are unproven; Dallas' history of a 2-RB rotation still leaves him high touch security.

roster.name: Chris Olave
roster.reason: Played through the minor hamstring issue with no setback — caught 8 of 10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-17 win over Baltimore, giving him an 18-268-1 line on 23 targets through two games as the Saints' clear top downfield target. Torched Detroit for 10/182 in the Week 1 opener; the Thursday-emergent hamstring tag never became a real threat — Adam Schefter and Saints beat reporters expected him to play all week, and that's exactly what happened. NEW (10/8): showed up on New Orleans' Thursday injury report as limited -- the Saints' own report ties it to a veteran rest day, while other outlets describe a lingering foot/knee issue; reporting is inconsistent on the cause. He remains the Saints' clear top target (18 targets through 2 full games, torched Detroit for 10/182 in the opener) and isn't expected to miss Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Minnesota, but worth confirming Friday's final designation (Yahoo Sports/Saints beat, 10/8). CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Minnesota -- the limited-practice issue from Thursday (reporting was split between a vet rest day and a lingering foot/knee issue) resolved without missing a game. Remains New Orleans' clear top target earner; downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. NEW (10/16): missed back-to-back practices Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15) with an illness -- not a new soft-tissue injury -- ahead of Sunday's Week 6 game at the Giants (10/18). RotoWire (10/16) expects no worse than a Questionable tag if he can't practice Friday; illness-based absences typically clear by gameday. Downgrading from Healthy to Health Watch pending final confirmation. WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): the illness that limited his practice Wednesday/Thursday was a non-issue by gameday -- caught an 18-yard TD from Tyler Shough in New Orleans' 34-27 win over the Giants (NFL.com, PFF, 10/18), remaining the Saints' clear top target earner. Downgrading tag back to Healthy.

roster.name: Michael Wilson
roster.reason: Broke out as the overall WR10 in PPR last year (78/1,006/7); locked in as the Z-receiver in new OC Mike LaFleur's scheme with projected 110-120 targets — camp reports have him looking sharper than Marvin Harrison Jr. so far. UPDATE (10/16): with Marvin Harrison Jr. now traded to Houston (see his note), beat reporting (KOLD, KSAT, Fox10 Phoenix) frames Wilson as Arizona's new top receiving option, with Kendrick Bourne as the secondary outside piece (see his note). Expect a real target-share bump starting Week 6 vs. the Rams (10/18), though it's not yet reflected in a box score.

roster.name: Colston Loveland
roster.reason: Moore's departure opens a big target vacuum; Bears leaning into more 13-personnel — projected ~78 rec/918 yds/7 TD after closing his rookie year red-hot. 2025 1st-round pick (10th overall, Michigan). UPDATE: Chicago's passing game is now working through journeyman Case Keenum after Caleb Williams' hamstring injury (out at least through Week 5) and Tyson Bagent's own unavailability — Keenum threw for 247 yards and 2 TD in Week 3's 27-7 upset of Philadelphia (9/28). Monitor target share/efficiency with a backup-caliber passer under center for the next several weeks.

roster.name: Josh Jacobs
roster.reason: Pleaded no contest Sept 10 to misdemeanor battery and criminal-damage charges from the May incident — fined $1,000 plus costs, with the damage charge to be dismissed after a 12-month deferred agreement. The legal resolution does NOT end his NFL absence: he remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List (can't practice, play, or be on the 53-man roster, though he's paid and can attend meetings/individual workouts) while a separate personal-conduct-policy review continues. Sources still peg the likely suspension range at 4-6 games once announced, with games missed on the exempt list expected to count toward it. Pleaded no contest Sept 10 in Brown County to the misdemeanor battery charge (found guilty, $1,000 fine + costs) with a 12-month deferred-judgment agreement on the property-damage charge. As of 9/26, the NFL STILL has not announced an official suspension length — reporting indicates the league is navigating legal barriers (a court-ordered bar on releasing video evidence) before finalizing discipline, with the standard 6-game domestic-violence-related baseline still the working estimate (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, ProFootballRumors, 9/24-26). Green Bay has already hedged, trading a 2028 6th-round pick to Pittsburgh for RB Kaleb Johnson as depth-chart insurance — a real sign the team isn't banking on a quick Jacobs return. Treat him as unplayable/bench for now. UPDATE (10/6): still no change -- the NFL has NOT announced an official suspension length. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List (confirmed still inactive for Green Bay's Week 4 game vs. Tampa Bay on 10/4). Speculation on the eventual suspension length now ranges from 4-6 games (ESPN's Jeremy Fowler) up to as many as 8 games (NFL Network's Ian Rapoport), still unconfirmed either way. The video-evidence dispute delaying the league's review is still unresolved -- a judge recently declined to permanently seal the incident video on procedural grounds (NBC Sports/PFT, ~10/1-2) -- and Jacobs' next court hearing isn't until Nov. 17, well past several more game weeks. Any time already spent on the Exempt List would count toward an eventual suspension. Green Bay's Kaleb Johnson depth-chart plan is unchanged; still unplayable/bench. UPDATE (10/13): still no official suspension length announced. HC Matt LaFleur said ahead of Green Bay's Week 6 game at Dallas that he has no word from the league on timing. Reporting still pegs a likely 4-6 game range (6-game baseline for a first battery offense, reducible for mitigating factors), with exempt-list time possibly counting toward it (ProFootballRumors, Yahoo Sports, 10/9-10). Still unplayable/bench. UPDATE (10/14): still no suspension length officially announced -- HC Matt LaFleur reiterated he has no word yet from the league on timing (AcmePackingCompany/Yardbarker, 10/12-13). This remains a Personal Conduct Policy matter (a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery/criminal damage to property stemming from a May domestic incident), not a PED case. A court fight over releasing police video/records from that incident is reportedly ongoing and may be delaying the league's final ruling (Rolling Out, 10/14). He'll miss a 6th straight game Sunday vs. Dallas. Green Bay's backfield without him: MarShawn Lloyd leads with 40 carries/112 yards/2 TD this season, with Kaleb Johnson (27/106) and Chris Brooks also involved -- Green Bay's run game ranks last in the NFL in his absence. UPDATE (10/16): filed a civil suit Wednesday (10/15) seeking to restrict public access to records tied to the May incident, as the Commissioner's Exempt List review continues -- no suspension length has been announced yet, and this remains a Personal Conduct Policy matter, not a physical injury (our roster feed's "DAY_TO_DAY" status field reflects the exempt-list/legal situation, not an actual injury). Still unplayable/bench; MarShawn Lloyd remains Green Bay's lead back for Sunday Night Football vs. Dallas (10/18). EXEMPT LIST LIFTED (10/16-19): the NFL announced it is removing Jacobs from the Commissioner's Exempt List effective Monday (10/19), clearing him to practice and play again starting with Green Bay's Week 7 game (Sun. 10/25) -- missing the first six games of the season in the process. The Personal Conduct Policy investigation into his misdemeanor battery/property-damage case continues separately, and the league has not ruled out an eventual suspension, but for now he is expected to be available to the Packers (AP, Newsweek, NY1, 10/16-19). MarShawn Lloyd has been Green Bay's lead back in his absence and figures to continue sharing work even once Jacobs is back; still a wait-and-see Depth Chart Battle until he actually suits up.

roster.name: Vikings D/ST
roster.reason: Through 2 games: 8 sacks (tied for most in the NFL), 4 takeaways, and the league's highest pressure rate (50.6%) — ranked the No. 6 fantasy defense entering Week 3 (Yahoo Sports/PFN, Sportsnaut, ~9/2026). Held Chicago to 297 total yards and zero TDs in Week 2, with 4 sacks and 2 takeaways — a second straight game with that exact sack/takeaway line. Minor injury watch: DL Jalen Redmond (elbow) and DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (oblique) were limited in Week 3 practice, but no starters were ruled out as of this week's report (SI/OnSI, 9/23).

roster.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
roster.reason: Veteran incumbent, Houston's clear starting kicker with no camp competition reported.

roster.name: Jared Goff
roster.reason: No injury designation — fully healthy through 3 games (Fox Sports injury tracker). Week 3 vs. NYJ (31-24 win): 25/32 for 269 yards and 2 TD (4-yard to Amon-Ra St. Brown, 11-yard game-winner to Jahmyr Gibbs in the final two minutes), plus 4 carries for 6 yards (CBS Sports, FantasyPros, RotoWire, 9/27). Roughly 802 yards, 8 TD, 0 INT on the season — solid, mistake-free form and a straightforward streaming/starter option.

roster.name: Juwan Johnson
roster.reason: Newly added off waivers — has emerged as New Orleans' clear TE1 in Kellen Moore's up-tempo offense, out-snapping backup Noah Fant 76-37 in Week 2. Ranks TE7 in fantasy points per game through 2 weeks (10.6+ PPR points in each game): 3/54/1 TD in the Week 1 OT loss to Detroit, then 4 catches in Week 2 — a 12.2% target share with 4 red-zone targets (FantasyData, RotoBaller, FantasyPros). Comes off a strong 2025 finish (77 catches/889 yards/3 TD, 102 targets) once Tyler Shough took over at QB — the current volume looks like a continuation of that role, not a one-game blip.

roster.name: Ladd McConkey
roster.reason: Played through the Week 1 rib injury (suffered on a hit from Mack Wilson vs. Arizona) in Sunday's Week 2 win over the Raiders, wearing a flak jacket for protection — caught 4 of 6 targets for 39 yards and a TD in the 31-14 win. No setback or re-aggravation reported; the rib did not limit his workload and he remains the Chargers' clear top target earner. NEW (9/30): the earlier rib injury is long resolved (he was fully cleared off the injury report for Week 3), but McConkey popped up on the Week 4 injury report with a separate, new foot injury — limited in Wednesday's practice. No MRI, surgery, or multi-week timeline has been reported yet; beat coverage (Chargers.com, NBC Sports, ClutchPoints) frames Thursday/Friday practice as the deciding factor for Sunday's game at Seattle, with nothing suggesting a severe issue (9/30). WORSENED (10/4-5): did play Week 4 at Seattle, but the foot injury flared up in the first half and he was downgraded from "questionable to return" to officially out, finishing with 0 catches on 2 targets (NBC Sports, 10/4). HC Jim Harbaugh called him "week-to-week" with the same foot injury in Monday's presser (RotoWire, CBS Sports, FantasyFootballers, 10/5) -- the SAME foot issue first flagged 9/30, not a new injury, but clearly worse than last week's minor framing. No Wednesday practice report yet as of today; bumping tag from Health Watch to Injury given the real doubt now attached to his Week 5 availability. UPDATE (10/10): remains in the Chargers' Week 5 injury mix with the lingering foot injury first flagged 9/30 and worsened in Week 4; HC Jim Harbaugh's "week-to-week" framing from Monday had not been updated with a firm practice report via search as of Friday. Teammate Quentin Johnston was confirmed OUT for Sunday's game vs. Denver (see his note), which would put extra pressure on McConkey's snaps if he plays through it. Week 5 final (10/11-12): technically active but played zero offensive snaps in the Chargers' 23-17 loss to Denver, with the lingering foot injury clearly still a real limiter despite no official game-day inactive designation. HC Jim Harbaugh said Monday (10/12) McConkey will keep working into practice ahead of Week 6 vs. Kansas City (Sun 10/18); no firmer return signal beyond that has surfaced yet. Keeping the standard Injury tier. UPDATE (10/16): limited in practice both Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the foot injury -- a step up from the zero offensive snaps he played in Week 5 (active but essentially an emergency-only option). HC Jim Harbaugh said early in the week it was only "possible" he returns to full practice; trending toward another Questionable tag for Sunday vs. Kansas City (10/18), with no official Friday grade confirmed yet. CLEARED (10/18): ESPN's Adam Schefter reported McConkey has no injury designation for Sunday night's Week 6 game vs. Kansas City, and our roster tracker confirms ACTIVE -- a real step up after he played zero offensive snaps in Week 5 despite being active. The recurring foot injury had him limited in practice through Wednesday/Thursday this week per HC Jim Harbaugh, so treat his workload as worth confirming early in the game rather than assuming an immediate return to full volume. Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch. NEW INJURY -- CONCUSSION (10/18): a different issue from the foot problem that dogged him in recent weeks -- ruled out early in the 2nd quarter of a 22-6 loss at Kansas City after his head hit the turf on a tackle, finishing with just 1 catch for 17 yards (ESPN, Yahoo Sports, 10/18). Concussion-protocol timelines are inherently unpredictable and no return estimate has been reported, but the Chargers are on their Week 7 bye (next game Nov. 1 at the Rams), which gives him a real runway to clear protocol before it costs him a game. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the new, distinct injury and genuine uncertainty; Quentin Johnston and KeAndre Lambert-Smith are the top receiving options in LA's banged-up WR room if he's still out Week 8.

roster.name: Patriots D/ST
roster.reason: Top-10 fantasy finish in 2025, but that leaned on a soft schedule; added Dre'Mont Jones, Kevin Byard, and a 2nd-round pick. Real talent additions, but a much tougher 2026 slate makes them a regression candidate off last year's ranking.

roster.name: Keaton Mitchell
roster.reason: Explosive change-of-pace back for the Chargers, but Omarion Hampton is the clear RB1 on the current depth chart; Mitchell has a slight edge over Kimani Vidal for the No. 2 job behind him, per Chargers.com and Yahoo Sports. Weak as a receiver out of the backfield, which caps his standalone fantasy value to a change-of-pace/big-play role in a Hampton-led committee rather than a real workload threat. NEW (9/30): limited in Wednesday's Week 4 practice with an ankle injury and was seen afterward in a walking boot, though he told reporters he was "ok." Beat/fantasy coverage frames logging a limited Wednesday session as a good sign he's trending toward playing Sunday at Seattle, with two more practice windows to upgrade; no structural diagnosis reported. Kimani Vidal would be next man up behind Omarion Hampton if Mitchell can't go (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, DraftSharks, 9/30). CLEARED (10/3): the ankle issue resolved without a setback -- logged full practice sessions after Wednesday's limited session and carries no designation into Sunday's game at Seattle. Removing Health Watch tag; still a change-of-pace role behind Omarion Hampton with Kimani Vidal as the other depth option.

roster.name: Kendre Miller
roster.reason: NEW (10/16): led New Orleans' Week 5 backfield with 10 carries and a rushing TD (10/12) while Alvin Kamara was limited in practice this week with a back issue (see Kamara's note). TheFantasyFootballers flags Miller as the likely early-down beneficiary again Sunday at the Giants (10/18) if Kamara's back lingers.

roster.name: De'Von Achane
roster.reason: No current injury flag entering Week 3, but missed time each of the last two seasons plus offseason shoulder surgery — the durability risk flagged all along showed up again. Suffered a non-contact knee injury on a 1st-quarter run vs. Kansas City in Week 3 (9/27), tackled awkwardly by a Chiefs defender, and was ruled out for the rest of the game; HC Jeff Hafley said postgame the outlook "does not sound very optimistic." CONFIRMED SEASON-ENDING: Monday's MRI (9/28) confirmed a torn ACL in the left knee. Miami placed him on IR and he will have surgery, ending his 2026 season just months after signing a 4-yr/$64M extension (CBS Sports, ESPN, RotoWire, Yahoo Sports, 9/28). Upgrading tag from Injury to Long-Term Injury to reflect the confirmed season-ending diagnosis — drop him in all non-dynasty/non-IR-stash formats.

roster.name: Joe Burrow
roster.reason: Played through the back tightness as expected — active and started Cincinnati's 20-6 win over Houston (Sun 9/20), going 20/31 for 207 yards and 2 TDs (both to Ja'Marr Chase, from 32 and 18 yards) with no INTs, though he did take 5 sacks. Confirms the back issue was minor/day-to-day as reported all week — no setback, no in-game re-aggravation reported, and no new limitation entering Week 3 prep. Elite passing-volume QB1 when right — the profile concern remains price/ADP more than health at this point.

roster.name: Kenneth Walker III
roster.reason: Immediately looks like the lead back in Kansas City's backfield after the free-agent signing (3yr/$43.05M) — leads the NFL with 47 carries (56 touches) through 2 games, backing up a Week 1 explosion (23-173-1 rush, 2 total TDs vs. Denver) with a Week 2 workhorse outing (24-117 rush, 6 catches/61 yds vs. Indianapolis). CONFIRMED: despite HC Andy Reid's talk of "balance" with rookie Emmett Johnson, Walker's Week 3 role barely budged — 78% of the RB snaps and 20 of 23 RB carry opportunities before the final drive, extending his streak to three straight weeks with a 70%+ snap share and 20+ PPR points in a 24-10 win over Miami. Dolphins did hold him to just 16 yards from scrimmage after halftime, worth monitoring, but the workhorse role itself is unchanged (Arrowhead Pride, RotoWire, 9/28).

roster.name: Roschon Johnson
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Tee Higgins
roster.reason: Played through a heel contusion in Week 1, catching 3 of 6 targets for 59 yards. NEW (9/30): ruled OUT for Thursday's Week 4 game at Jacksonville with a shoulder injury, after not practicing Wednesday (CBS Sports, FantasyPros, RotoWire, 9/30). Reporting doesn't yet specify when the shoulder issue arose or a return timeline — flagging this as fresh news since our own roster tracker's status field hasn't yet caught up to the OUT designation. S Jessie Bates III (neck) is also out for Cincinnati Thursday. Ja'Marr Chase remains the clear top target in his absence. UPDATE (10/5): missed a second straight game with the shoulder injury in Thursday's Week 4 loss to Jacksonville, never practicing that week (CBS Sports, National Football Post, Sportskeeda, 10/1-2). Today's flip from OUT back to QUESTIONABLE suggests real practice-field progress toward a return -- HC Zac Taylor has called him "on the right trajectory to play" -- but no firm return date has been reported yet, so keeping the standard Injury tier rather than Short-Term. Ja'Marr Chase remains Cincinnati's clear top target in his continued absence. CORRECTION (10/8): previous notes describing a 'shoulder' injury that kept Higgins out of the Jacksonville game were inaccurate. The real story: Higgins played in Week 4's 22-17 loss to Jacksonville and had a big game (11 catches for 157 yards on 16 targets) before hurting his adductor on a late sideline catch, leaving briefly and managing one final-drive snap. HC Zac Taylor called him day-to-day Monday and did not rule him out for Sunday's Week 5 game at Miami, alongside Ja'Marr Chase's concussion situation (FieldLevelMedia, RotoBaller, 4for4, 10/5). Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch given the day-to-day framing and that he already played through it once. CLEARED (10/12): played through the adductor injury with no setback reported in Sunday's Week 5 win at Miami (Bengals won 31-24, now 3-2); specific catch/yardage totals for Higgins could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update. Ja'Marr Chase (see his note) also cleared concussion protocol and had a big game in the same contest.

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.reason: Elite volume floor even coming off a down 2025 — earned a 30%+ target share early last season and has topped 23% every year of his career.

roster.name: Sam LaPorta
roster.reason: The hip flare-up was a non-issue once games started — produced in both Week 1 (9.8 fantasy pts, opener vs. New Orleans) and Week 2 (17.2 fantasy pts in Thursday night's win over Buffalo), with no re-aggravation reported.

roster.name: Justin Jefferson
roster.reason: Down year by his own standard in 2025 (WR30 overall) but still finished 6th league-wide in target share (28.5%) — new QB Kyler Murray has a track record of feeding elite WR1s. Left Sunday's Week 3 win over Tampa Bay (23-16) early in the 1st quarter with a left ankle injury after a defender landed on it during a 10-yard screen reception, and did not return. NEW: Monday's MRI (9/28) revealed a clean ankle sprain with no structural/long-term damage — a real relief given the initial fear of a high-ankle or deltoid-ligament issue. HC Kevin O'Connell called the outlook positive and said the team will manage his practice reps through the week to gauge Week 4 availability vs. Miami; there's a real chance he plays (ESPN, NBC Sports, Bleacher Report, Athlon, 9/28-29). Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch given the clean imaging and plausible Week 4 clearance. WORSENED (10/2-3): despite the clean MRI and earlier optimism, Jefferson was officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. Miami (CBS Sports' Week 4 injury report, PrizePicks, 10/2-3) -- the ankle sprain needed more than a week of management after all. Bumping tag from Health Watch to Injury; no multi-week timeline reported, so treat as a week-to-week absence for now rather than Short/Long-Term. TRENDING UP (10/7): QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at New Orleans. HC Kevin O'Connell said as of 10/3-4 that Jefferson has made "great progress" on the ankle, though it's "too early to say" definitively if he plays (ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, Fox9, NBC Sports). No setback reported since last week's OUT designation -- keeping the Injury tag for now given he's not yet confirmed to play, but this reads as a real step toward a Week 5 return rather than a new concern. UPDATE (10/8): was a limited practice participant to begin Week 5 prep (Wednesday, 10/7) for Sunday's game at New Orleans -- a step up from last week's OUT designation, though not yet confirmation he plays. Final designation comes Friday. CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/12): played a full workload in Sunday's Week 5 win at New Orleans (Vikings won 23-13 to improve to 5-0 and head into their bye) with no setback from the ankle -- 6 catches for 79 yards and a touchdown (a 15-yard TD from Kyler Murray in the 3rd quarter), his first score since Week 1. Upgrading tag from Injury to Healthy given the clean workload and no re-aggravation.

roster.name: Falcons D/ST
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Harrison Butker
roster.reason: Added off waivers this week. Kansas City's long-time starting kicker with no camp competition; no fresh injury or role news found as of this update -- standard low-variance K1 role behind a pass-heavy Chiefs offense.

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.reason: Led Buffalo's backfield as expected in the opener vs. Houston: 13 carries for 57 yards and 3 catches for 12 yards, though he didn't find the end zone in a game the Bills controlled on the ground. Signed a 4-year, $48M extension (up to $30M guaranteed) in August 2025, locking him in through 2029.

roster.name: Tyler Shough
roster.reason: Firmly entrenched as New Orleans' starting QB heading into 2026 after opening the season with 410 passing yards in Week 1 and leading the Saints to a last-second Week 2 win over Baltimore (24-17). No injury concerns reported on Shough himself; the Saints' broader offensive-line and receiver injury situation (Dillon Radunz torn ACL/out for the season, Kelvin Banks Jr. high-ankle sprain, Jordyn Tyson hamstring/expected out ~2 months) is worth monitoring as a drag on his supporting cast and pass-pro, but doesn't threaten his starting job. NEW (10/8): limited at Wednesday's practice with a left (non-throwing) hand injury ahead of Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Minnesota; beat reporters note it isn't expected to affect his throwing, and he remains New Orleans' starter (Saints' official injury report via Crescent City Sports/Canal Street Chronicles, 10/7). CLEARED (10/9): full practice participant as of Thursday's report on the left (non-throwing) hand injury suffered during Monday's loss to Atlanta -- firmly on track to start Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Minnesota, with no threat to his job (Saints beat/Field Level Media, 10/7-8). Week 5 final (10/11): rough outing against a tough Minnesota defense (No. 2 DVOA, No. 1 vs. the pass) -- 16-of-25 for 96 yards, no TD, 2 INT, and his first career game without a rushing attempt, in a 23-13 loss that was also his first game all season under 250 passing yards. No injury reported; one bad matchup rather than a threat to his starting job. Saints play at the Giants in Week 6 (Sun 10/18).

roster.name: Denzel Boston
roster.reason: 2026 second-round rookie (No. 39 overall, Washington) who opened the season in Cleveland's starting WR2 spot alongside Jerry Jeudy. Broke out in Week 2 vs. Tampa Bay with 5 catches for 95 yards and a 55-yard TD, earning an NFL Rookie of the Week nomination. NEW (10/16): picked up a foot injury this week -- logged back-to-back limited practices Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15), which is why he's carrying a QUESTIONABLE tag for the first time this season ahead of Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Baltimore (10/18). Beat writers (NBC Sports, CBS Sports) still expect him to play without real restriction. CLEARED (10/18): carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Baltimore after logging back-to-back limited practices Wednesday/Thursday -- beat reporting (NBC Sports, The Fantasy Footballers) had already expected him to play without real restriction. Dropping the Health Watch tag now that the foot issue produced no game-status designation.

roster.name: Germie Bernard
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.reason: Rookie hype exceeds his current role — projected ~250 att/1,125 yds, but likely won't clear 70% snap share with Mitchell handling passing downs. High-variance breakout, not a lock.

roster.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
roster.reason: Diagnosed with a deltoid ligament sprain in his left ankle (not an Achilles issue — HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed the Achilles is intact) after leaving the Sept 10 opener vs. the Rams early without a target. Underwent ankle surgery Wednesday (Sept 16) after the injury proved worse than initially believed, and was officially placed on injured reserve — revised from the earlier ~1-month outlook to a firmer ~10-week absence per Shanahan's post-surgery update. Drop-and-stash-if-needed territory in shallow leagues for the next couple of months. Still a real deep-league breakout stash for whenever SF's WR room opens back up.

roster.name: Jonah Coleman
roster.reason: With both RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins banged up, Coleman led Denver's backfield in Week 2 snap share (42.4%), touches (13) and total yards (58 plus a TD) in the win over Jacksonville — his first career rushing TD. Named a top Week 3 waiver-wire target by NFL.com (9/24). REVISED (from the earlier "minor, shouldn't affect gameday status" framing, then from last update's "short absence" framing): the ankle is a high ankle sprain, and Denver placed Coleman on injured reserve Saturday (9/26) rather than just ruling him out week-to-week — he's expected back no sooner than Oct. 25 vs. Arizona (first eligible date), meaning at least 4 additional games missed on top of Week 3 (ESPN, NFL.com, Denver Gazette, CBS Sports, 9/26). Upgrading the tag from Short-Term to Long-Term Injury to reflect the real, IR-confirmed absence. The good news for Denver: both J.K. Dobbins (hip) and RJ Harvey (hamstring) escaped the injury report with no designation and are expected to play Week 3 — the backfield rotation should run through them for the next several weeks with Coleman on IR. UPDATE (10/5): remains on IR with the Week 2 high-ankle sprain, first eligible to return Week 7 (no change to the previously reported Oct. 25 vs. Arizona target). Denver lost Week 4 to the Chargers; in that game J.K. Dobbins clearly won the early-down split over RJ Harvey -- 11 carries for 83 yards and a TD plus a catch, vs. just 2 carries for 2 yards and 3 catches for 14 yards for Harvey (CBS Sports/RotoWire). Dobbins looks like the stronger side of Denver's committee right now while Coleman remains out.

roster.name: Drake Maye
roster.reason: Rough Week 1 debut of the new-weapons era: 23/33 for 178 yds, 1 TD, but 3 INTs — all in the 4th quarter, including a game-sealing pick in the end zone — in a 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game loss to Seattle. Added 47 rush yds. Called the turnovers "unacceptable" postgame; also lost top target A.J. Brown to an ankle injury mid-game. Coming off a QB2-overall 2025 (20.7 PPG); Patriots traded for A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs, giving him real weapons — widely projected top-5 fantasy QB before Week 1's opener.

roster.name: Chuba Hubbard
roster.reason: The camp hamstring issue was fully behind him for the opener — played through it and led Carolina's backfield in the Week 1 loss to Chicago: 10 carries for 49 yards and a rush TD plus 3 catches for 38 yards and a receiving TD (23.7 fantasy pts). NEW: with Jonathon Brooks now on injured reserve (core-muscle surgery, minimum 6 weeks) as of 9/23, the earlier 1A/1B timeshare is over — Hubbard is Carolina's undisputed lead back, with AJ Dillon next man up in a diminished RB2/short-yardage role.

roster.name: Kyren Williams
roster.reason: Remains the lead back in a McVay-preferred ~65:35 split with Blake Corum — not under real threat, but not a bell-cow either. Split carries close to even with Blake Corum in Monday night's win over the Giants (12-85-0 rush plus a receiving TD for Williams), and lost a fumble at his own 11 late in the first half — worth tracking whether the committee trends more even going forward (CBS Sports/RotoWire). UPDATE (10/13): scored the game-tying touchdown late in Monday night's 37-34 OT loss to Buffalo (10/12) but was otherwise inefficient per fantasy outlets. The loss was partly due to K Harrison Mevis missing two field goals, including a potential OT game-winner (see his note) -- worth monitoring whether kicking struggles start costing the Rams short-field/red-zone possessions that would otherwise run through Williams.

roster.name: Ja'Marr Chase
roster.reason: Played through the knee hyperextension with no setback, though production was quiet in the opener — 2 catches for 12 yards on 4 targets vs. Tampa Bay. Role and target volume are unchanged; treat it as a one-game blip rather than a trend. NEW DESIGNATION (10/5): flipped from Active to QUESTIONABLE today. Multiple searches found no new injury report, game-exit note, or beat-writer comment tied to this specific change -- stating that plainly rather than inventing a cause. His only 2026 injury history is a minor practice knee hyperextension in late August that he said didn't concern him and that carried no designation by late September. Treat as unconfirmed/precautionary for now; downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending more specific reporting. CONFIRMED (10/8): the mechanism behind last week's QUESTIONABLE tag is now clear -- Chase left the Week 4 loss to Jacksonville in the 2nd quarter with a head injury (facemask pull into a second hit) and was ruled out with a concussion; he remains in the NFL's concussion protocol as of Monday's update, with HC Zac Taylor calling him day-to-day and not ruling him out for Sunday's Week 5 game at Miami (Fox19, NBC Sports, RotoBaller, Newsweek, 10/4-5). No confirmation yet that he's cleared protocol -- a return to practice is required before clearance, so check Thursday/Friday. CLEARED CONCUSSION PROTOCOL (10/12): played a full workload in Sunday's Week 5 win at Miami (Bengals won 31-24, now 3-2) with no setback -- caught 6 passes for 77 yards including a highlight-reel touchdown grab late in the 3rd quarter that made it 28-10. Joe Burrow threw 4 TD passes in the win. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean return and full role.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.reason: Clear WR1 with essentially no target competition (~30% target share); should produce top-10 WR numbers, with QB play the main swing factor rather than his role. Delivered a massive game in Thursday night's Week 3 win over Green Bay (35-14): 9 catches for 194 yards (including gains of 68 and 40 yards), tied to Michael Penix Jr.'s efficient return under center (18/25, 256 yards, 1 TD) (CBS Sports, 9/24). NEW (10/13): QB Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury on a late sack in Atlanta's 30-23 overtime loss to Baltimore (10/12) and did not return to that game; Ian Rapoport reported it's not believed serious, and Penix said he expects to play Week 6 vs. Chicago, but the team was still evaluating him in practice as of midweek. Worth checking Friday's injury report before trusting London's volume outlook -- a limited or sidelined Penix would be a real dent in his target efficiency.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.reason: The groin injury fully resolved — played through the Week 1 loss to Baltimore with no setback, catching 3 of 5 targets for 13 yards and a receiving TD. NEW (10/18): added to Indianapolis' injury report Friday as a limited participant with a groin injury, drawing a QUESTIONABLE tag for Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Tennessee -- he dealt with a groin issue back in August, so this could be a recurrence rather than a fresh injury, though that hasn't been confirmed (4for4, The Fantasy Footballers, 10/16). Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending the final gameday call. CONFIRMED OUT (10/18): officially inactive for Indianapolis' Week 6 game vs. Tennessee with the groin injury that popped up on Friday's practice report -- likely a recurrence of the same groin issue from August camp rather than a brand-new injury, though that hasn't been formally confirmed (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, StampedeBlue, 10/17-18). No return timeline reported yet. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier now that it has actually cost him a game. UPDATE (10/22): did not practice Wednesday (10/21) with the groin injury, per the Colts' official report -- HC Shane Steichen called him "progressing really well" but deferred to the injury report rather than guaranteeing Sunday's availability. Indianapolis' Week 7 opponent is Minnesota (not a repeat of last week's Tennessee game). No Thursday/Friday grade or official designation confirmed yet as of this update; keeping the standard Injury tier.

roster.name: Saquon Barkley
roster.reason: The $16.75M-guaranteed workhorse role is intact when healthy, but he suffered a stinger to his left arm/shoulder on Philadelphia's very first offensive snap of the Week 2 win at Tennessee and missed most of that game (4 carries for 9 yards, 1 catch for 11 yards). CLEARED and CONFIRMED: played through the stinger with no setback, telling reporters beforehand he didn't expect it to affect him. Ran effectively in Monday night's Week 3 loss at Chicago — 82 yards on 15 carries, with 73 of those yards coming in the first half before Philadelphia's offense stalled with three straight second-half three-and-outs in the 27-7 defeat (RotoWire, CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 9/28). No health concerns entering Week 4. NEW DESIGNATION (10/5): flipped from Active to QUESTIONABLE today. No specific new injury or in-game exit report from Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Rams was found via search -- stating that plainly. Given his Week 2 stinger history (cleared with a clean MRI), this is plausibly continued precautionary arm/shoulder management rather than a new injury, but that mechanism is not confirmed. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending clearer reporting. WORSENED (10/8): DNP in back-to-back Wednesday and Thursday practices this week with a hamstring injury -- a different, more concrete issue than the stinger/arm precaution referenced above, and analysts now see him as unlikely to play Sunday's Week 5 game in London vs. Jacksonville. Bumping tag from Health Watch to Injury given the two straight missed practices and real chance of a missed game; no multi-week timeline reported (Philadelphia Eagles official injury report, PhillyVoice, Yahoo Sports, 10/8). CONFIRMED (10/10): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 5 game in London vs. Jacksonville with the hamstring injury -- missed back-to-back Wednesday/Thursday practices, and Ian Rapoport reported him not expected to play (10/8). Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce are set to handle the Eagles' backfield work in London (see Shipley's note). Week 5 final (10/11): missed a second straight game as Jacksonville beat Philadelphia 19-17 in London on a last-second Cam Little field goal. Will Shipley and newly-activated Dameon Pierce (making his 2026 debut) handled the Eagles' backfield work in his absence; fellow absentee Tank Bigsby (abdomen) also sat out. UPDATE (10/14): real positive signal for Week 6 vs. Carolina (Sun 10/18, home) -- RotoBaller reported (10/12) Barkley "has a chance to return," with Ian Rapoport earlier characterizing the hamstring injury as "not believed serious." No Wednesday practice report confirming actual participation had posted as of this update; keeping the standard Injury tier until that's confirmed. SETBACK (10/14): also did NOT practice Wednesday -- the Eagles' team injury report listed him remaining sidelined even as other players returned from IR (Heavy.com/Yahoo; one Yahoo headline said "limited" but the fuller team-report language points to DNP). A real step back from the "has a chance to return" framing from earlier in the week for Sunday's game vs. Carolina; recheck Friday before trusting the more optimistic read. UPDATE (10/16): a worse trend than teammate DeVonta Smith -- officially a non-participant in both Wednesday and Thursday practice (10/14-10/15), a second straight full DNP, and hasn't played since the Week 4 hamstring injury. Dameon Pierce would start Sunday vs. Carolina (10/18) if Barkley sits, with Carson Steele as backup; Friday's practice is the real swing factor. CONFIRMED (10/18): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. Carolina after missing every practice this week with the hamstring injury -- a second straight full missed game (NBC Sports Philadelphia injury reports, 10/13-10/17). QB Jalen Hurts is also out (blood clot in his calf), with Tanner McKee starting; Dameon Pierce is set to lead Philadelphia's backfield Sunday with Carson Steele as backup. UPDATE (10/22): Philadelphia is NOT on a bye this week -- they host Dallas on Monday Night Football (10/26). Per Bleacher Report (citing Ian Rapoport/Adam Schefter), the Eagles "believe" there's a "realistic" chance Barkley returns for that game, but no official Wednesday practice-report grade confirming actual participation was found as of this update -- treat as optimistic-but-unconfirmed, not a practice confirmation. Keeping the standard Injury tier; Dameon Pierce remains the lead back in the meantime.

roster.name: Steelers D/ST
roster.reason: DST5 in points per game in 2025 (7.8 PPG) even with T.J. Watt missing three games, powered by 27 forced turnovers and 48 sacks. Secondary got shredded at times — free agents Jamel Dean and Jaquan Brisker were brought in to fix that, but this remains one of the league's oldest defensive units.

roster.name: Matt Gay
roster.reason: Signed by Las Vegas as a free agent in March 2026 after previously kicking for the Colts and Rams; locked in as the Raiders' K1 after winning the camp competition over Kansei Matsuzawa. NEW (10/17): added off waivers this week by a fantasy manager -- no new on-field news beyond his standard role as Las Vegas' placekicker behind an offense that leans heavily on Brock Bowers (see his note) in the passing game.

roster.name: Kyler Murray
roster.reason: Cleared the NFL's concussion protocol on Monday 9/21 (suffered the concussion in Week 1 vs. Green Bay on a hit from S Javon Bullard); missed Week 2 vs. Chicago, which Carson Wentz started and won 9-3. Confirmed by HC Kevin O'Connell as the Week 3 starter at Tampa Bay (Sun 9/27) — no lingering designation, fully back atop the depth chart. Note: Murray was released by Arizona in March 2026 and signed with Minnesota as a free agent (Arizona still covering most of his prior extension salary) — his Minnesota team tag is accurate, not a data error. Vikings are 2-0 to start the season.

roster.name: Tony Pollard
roster.reason: Entrenched starter chasing a 5th straight 1,000-yard season — hit 1,000 rushing yards in each of the past 4 years. CLEARED: returned to a full practice Friday (9/25) and is off the final Week 3 injury report entirely — no designation for Sunday vs. the Giants (RotoWire, FantasyPros, NBC Sports, 9/25). Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (ankle) remains Questionable — if Spears is limited or sits, Pollard is positioned for an even bigger workload bump on top of his already-larger carry share (53.4% snap share to Spears' 42.7% through two weeks, with roughly double Spears' carries). NEW (9/30): a new foot injury (distinct from the ankle issue referenced earlier) — Pollard was a non-participant in Wednesday's Week 4 practice. HC Mike Vrabel's staff said they are "not overly concerned about Sunday" for Pollard and don't believe it will affect his Week 4 availability vs. Baltimore; backfield mate Tyjae Spears also sat out Wednesday with an ankle issue (CBS Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, Newsweek, 9/30). CLEARED (10/1-2): the foot issue that held him out of Wednesday's practice did not linger — Pollard returned to a full practice Thursday and carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Baltimore. Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (ankle) remains limited/Questionable, keeping Pollard's bell-cow workload intact (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 10/1-2). Week 4 final (10/4): the foot issue was a non-factor -- went for 16 carries, 48 yards and a 3-yard rushing TD plus 2 catches for 2 yards in a 24-18 loss to Baltimore that dropped Tennessee to 0-4. Backfield mate Tyjae Spears was marginal (2 carries, 7 yards), confirming Pollard as the clear lead back even in a lost season. Worth watching: with Tennessee winless, ESPN's Adam Schefter floated Pollard as a potential trade-deadline candidate -- no deal reported yet, just speculation (NBC Sports, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports, 10/4). NEW (10/8): did not practice Wednesday with a foot injury and is QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Houston; beat coverage describes it as a possible maintenance/veteran rest day rather than a new injury, consistent with how Tennessee has handled him in past weeks (10/7). CLEARED (10/8): back to a full practice participant Thursday after sitting out Wednesday with the foot issue -- on track to play Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Houston, continuing the pattern of maintenance-related absences that haven't cost him game time all season (Yahoo Sports/Titans beat, 10/8).
