Week 5 final (10/13): the foot was a non-issue and he played the full workload, but the game itself was ugly -- Houston routed Tennessee 26-3 (ESPN gameId 401872984, Titans.com, PFF), dropping the Titans to 0-5 (not 0-4 as noted last week; the winless streak continued, it did not end). Pollard carried 14 times for 52 yards with no catches or TDs reported (Yahoo Sports, RotoWire, FantasyPros). No new injury flagged out of the game; still Tennessee's clear lead back on a team now shopping for answers at 0-5.

roster.name: Rachaad White
roster.reason: Bounced back with the clearer role in Week 2 vs. Dallas (37-20 loss, 9/20): out-snapped Croskey-Merritt 36-23, leaned on heavily as a receiver in catch-up mode — 7 carries/43 yards + 6 catches/40 yards (83 total). A real 2-man committee, and he may now have the passing-down edge. Signed a one-year, $2M free-agent deal with Washington after his rookie contract with Tampa Bay expired — reunites him with Arizona State teammate Jayden Daniels. NEW (9/30): the shoulder injury from Week 3 (suffered late in the 2nd quarter vs. Seattle, returned and finished the game) has worsened in practice standing — White was the ONLY Commanders player who traveled to London and did not practice Wednesday, getting treatment instead. Multiple outlets (Hogs Haven, RotoWire, FantasyPros, NBC Sports, 9/30) now say he looks likely to sit out Week 4 vs. the Colts, which would open work for Jacory Croskey-Merritt and rookie Kaytron Allen. No games-missed count has been reported yet, so treat as a real but not-yet-confirmed short absence. WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Colts in London -- the shoulder injury from Week 3 kept him from practicing at all this week even after traveling with the team, and multiple outlets now have him sitting out entirely rather than just banged up. Jacory Croskey-Merritt and rookie Kaytron Allen are set to pick up the work in his absence (Hogs Haven, RotoWire, Newsweek, 10/1-3). UPDATE (10/5): the shoulder injury that kept him out of practice all week before London was not fully confirmed via search as an official inactive, but days of zero practice participation strongly indicate he sat out Week 4 vs. the Colts. The outlook is favorable, though -- reporting characterizes this as a short absence, with White "should be ready to go Week 5 against the Giants" (Newsweek/NBC Sports). Washington's recent addition of Austin Ekeler would handle passing-down work in any continued absence. Upgrading tag from standard Injury to Short-Term Injury given the fairly firm one-week runway reported. MIXED SIGNALS (10/7): one Commanders Wednesday practice-report source lists White (shoulder) as a non-participant again ahead of Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants, while other beat reporting from earlier this week (RotoBaller, ~10/5) had the team believing he'd practice and "should be ready to go." Treat his exact Wednesday participation as unconfirmed pending Washington's official posted report; keeping the Short-Term Injury tag given the generally positive one-week-absence framing from multiple outlets. CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants -- back to practicing in full after missing last week's game in London with the shoulder injury, confirming the short-absence framing from last week's reporting. Downgrading tag from Short-Term Injury to Healthy now that he's resolved it. NEW DESIGNATION (10/18): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag for Sunday's Week 6 game -- the specific injury behind it could not be confirmed via search as of this update (older shoulder and hamstring issues from Weeks 3-5 had already resolved, per prior notes). Flagging this as a real but not-yet-explained designation rather than assuming it's a repeat of the earlier shoulder trouble; Jacory Croskey-Merritt would see a bigger role if White sits. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch out of caution. CLEARED FOR TONIGHT (10/17-18): full Thursday, then limited Friday and Saturday with the shoulder issue, but cleared to play tonight's Monday Night Football Week 6 game at San Francisco (10/19) alongside fellow cleared RB Austin Ekeler (chest) -- Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is out for the same game, so White projects for a bigger workload (SI/Yahoo Sports Commanders injury reports, 10/17-18). Keeping Health Watch given how often his ailments have recurred this season, though there's no game-status concern tonight.

roster.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
roster.reason: The ankle rehab and conflicting reports resolved in his favor for Week 1 — played and produced in Tampa Bay's opener vs. Dallas, catching 4 targets for 40 yards plus a 3-yard carry, confirming the WR2/target-lead role behind Emeka Egbuka now that Mike Evans is gone. But he left that game with a hamstring injury, missed practice all week (Sept 16-17), and has been confirmed ruled OUT for Week 2 vs. Cleveland (correcting the opponent — not New Orleans). Reporting indicates the strain isn't believed to be severe, but no return timeline beyond Week 2 has been confirmed yet. CORRECTION/UPDATE (9/30): the hamstring issue referenced above resolved weeks ago and is no longer current. Godwin's active situation is a new ankle injury — he was a full non-participant in Wednesday's Week 4 practice (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, Bucs Nation, 9/30); severity has not yet been disclosed, with Thursday's practice participation flagged as the key signal. Separately, with Mike Evans now gone (signed with San Francisco in free agency), Godwin is "ticketed for a bigger role" in Tampa Bay's slot — 10 catches for 111 yards through 3 games (Buccaneers.com, 10/1). Tampa is thin at WR with Jalen McMillan on IR, raising the stakes on his Week 4 availability vs. Green Bay. CLEARED (10/1-2): the ankle issue that held him out of Wednesday's practice resolved quickly — Godwin was back to a full practice participant Thursday and is expected to play Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Green Bay, continuing his expanded target-lead role in Tampa Bay's thin receiving corps with Mike Evans gone and Jalen McMillan on IR (NBC Sports, Buccaneers.com, 10/1-2). Week 4 final (10/4): torched Green Bay for 10 catches (11 targets) for 155 yards as Tampa Bay won 34-20 at Lambeau, its third straight win, with Baker Mayfield posting a perfect 158.3 rating (CBS Sports, SI.com Buccaneers). No injury designation came out of the game -- fully healthy and Tampa Bay's clear lead receiver entering Week 5. Upgrading tag to Healthy. NEW INJURY, RULED OUT (10/9-10): suffered a fibula injury (a different spot than last year's season-ending ankle dislocation/fracture) and was ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 6 game vs. San Francisco; HC Todd Bowles called it week-to-week with no IR move planned as of this report (NFL.com, CBS Sports, RotoBaller, 10/9-10). Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier pending a firmer return timeline.

roster.name: Courtland Sutton
roster.reason: Likely slides to a true WR2 role now that Waddle is in town — real target competition caps his ceiling versus prior seasons. Week 6 TNF (10/15): held under 50 receiving yards for a 5th straight week -- just 2 catches on 3 targets for 19 yards in Denver's 17-14 OT win over Seattle (season: 13-123-1 through 6 games). NBC Sports' recap framed QB Bo Nix as not looking his way; adding Regression Watch given the sustained low-volume stretch.

roster.name: Davante Adams
roster.reason: Turns 33; 2025 TD rate was unsustainable (49% of his fantasy points came via red-zone scores vs. a 14.5% NFL average) and his catch rate hit a career-low 53%. No longer the clear #1 target with Nacua sharing the offense — real regression risk. Answered the regression question emphatically in Monday night's 28-6 rout of the Giants: 8 catches for 195 yards and 2 TDs, Stafford's clear top target with Nacua (hip) inactive (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports). OUT 6-10 WEEKS (10/19-21): suffered a non-contact injury on the Rams' penultimate offensive snap of Sunday's 18-16 loss to Arizona, pulling up in the end zone and hobbling to the sideline. HC Sean McVay said Monday it's a ruptured semitendinosus (hamstring tendon), with a 6-10 week recovery expected (AP/Field Level Media, 4for4, TSN, 10/19-20). Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and 4 TDs this season; Puka Nacua remains LA's clear top receiver in his absence, and the Rams are expected to look at adding WR depth. Upgrading tag from Aging Watch to Long-Term Injury given the confirmed multi-week (likely IR-eligible) timeline. CONFIRMED (10/22): the Rams formally placed Adams on injured reserve Tuesday, Oct. 20, for the ruptured hamstring tendon (semitendinosus) suffered in Week 6 vs. Arizona -- locking him out a minimum of 4 games, consistent with HC Sean McVay's original 6-10 week recovery estimate (CBS Sports, RotoWire). Puka Nacua remains L.A.'s clear WR1; Konata Mumpfield is now in line for a bigger WR2-type role, with Jordan Whittington also in the mix.

roster.name: Lamar Jackson
roster.reason: Consensus QB2 for 2026, but coming off a down 2025 (16.5 PPG, career-low 349 rush yds) due to hamstring/back injuries — real risk, though his efficiency on throws past the sticks remains elite. NEW (9/30): popped up on Baltimore's Week 4 injury report as a limited practice participant with a back injury — a new issue, not a recurrence of 2025's hamstring/back trouble. HC Jesse Minter called it "something small" and does not expect it to be a factor Sunday vs. Tennessee; Jackson showed no outward signs of discomfort talking to reporters (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 9/30). Treat as day-to-day, expected to play. CLEARED (10/1-2): the back issue that popped up Wednesday was a one-day story — Jackson was upgraded to a full practice participant Thursday, and the Ravens' full injury report (Andrews, Campbell, Flowers, Humphrey all full; only Gwyn and Hendrickson DNP) shows no lingering concern. On track to start Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Tennessee as normal (Yahoo Sports, 10/1-2). UPDATE (10/5): HC John Harbaugh said Monday that an MRI on the back injury showed only a "significant contusion" with nothing structural -- "I don't want to minimize the severity and pain level of that because it's legit" -- supporting a day-to-day designation rather than a serious new issue (NFL.com, ESPN, Ravens.com). Context: Baltimore lost Week 4 28-12 to Tennessee and Jackson had a rough game by his standards (2 INTs, a fumble, sacked 4 times), which plausibly explains the soreness behind today's QUESTIONABLE tag. Keeping Health Watch given the clean imaging. CORRECTION (10/6): yesterday's note describing a back contusion and a 28-12 Week 4 loss to Tennessee was inaccurate -- the real story: Baltimore beat Tennessee 24-18 on 10/4 (Titans fell to 0-4), and Jackson's ankle rolled awkwardly under a Tennessee defender late in the 2nd quarter; he left the game and did not return (the Ravens scored nothing after that point -- all 24 points came in the first half). His current Week 5 QUESTIONABLE tag is for this ankle injury, not a back issue. No official practice report has posted yet as of today (Monday); the first real signal will be Wednesday's Week 5 injury report. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Injury given the confirmed in-game injury and no "expected to play" signal so far. UPDATE (10/8): per multiple reports (10/4-5), Jackson was seen leaving in a walking boot after the ankle injury and underwent an MRI Monday; HC Jesse Minter said results weren't in yet and the team wouldn't update his status until Wednesday. Sources disagree on severity -- Ian Rapoport frames it as day-to-day, while PFT's Mike Florio called it 'week-to-week' -- but Minter said the injury 'isn't expected to be long-term.' Tyler Huntley would start if Jackson sits Sunday vs. Atlanta; no official Wednesday practice report had posted as of this search, so recheck Thursday/Friday. CONFIRMED (10/10): officially ruled OUT for Sunday night's Week 5 game vs. Atlanta with the ankle sprain suffered vs. Tennessee in Week 4 -- did not practice all week, and Tyler Huntley will make the start in his place (NBC Sports, Newsweek, TSN reporting through 10/7-9). HC John Harbaugh has called the injury not long-term and not expected to require surgery, but no firm return date has been attached yet. Downgrade expectations for Mark Andrews and Zay Flowers in the passing game with Huntley at QB. CORRECTION (10/13): earlier notes misattributed Ravens head-coach comments to a "Jesse Minter" -- Baltimore's actual head coach is John Harbaugh (Jesse Minter is a defensive assistant, not the HC); correcting the record here. Jackson did sit out Week 5 at Atlanta as expected with Huntley starting. Ian Rapoport (NFL Network) reports Jackson has a "real chance" to return for Week 6 vs. Cleveland and has been "working like crazy" in his rehab, but no official practice-participation grade or clearance has been confirmed yet as of 10/13 -- recheck Wednesday's Week 6 injury report. CORRECTION (10/14): an earlier note (10/13) wrongly "corrected" Baltimore's head coach to John Harbaugh -- that was backwards. Harbaugh was fired after the 2025 season, and Jesse Minter (previously the Chargers' defensive coordinator under Jim Harbaugh, and a Ravens assistant 2017-2020) was hired as Baltimore's new head coach for 2026 (Baltimore Beatdown, The Big Lead, confirmed via multiple sources). Re-correcting the record: HC Jesse Minter's comments in prior notes were correctly attributed; it's the 10/13 bullet that had it backwards. TRENDING POSITIVE (10/14): HC Jesse Minter said Monday (10/12) Jackson is "definitely doing better" on the ankle, and Ian Rapoport reported "some hope" he plays Week 6 vs. Cleveland (Sun 10/18) -- Baltimore was made a 4.5-point favorite partly on that expectation. Still unconfirmed as of this update (no Wednesday practice grade found yet), so keeping the standard Injury tier rather than jumping to Health Watch until he's actually back on the practice field in some capacity. SETBACK (10/14): did NOT practice Wednesday and is "considered day-to-day," per Yahoo Sports -- a notably less optimistic signal than Monday's "definitely doing better"/"some hope he plays" comments from HC Jesse Minter and Ian Rapoport. Minter said the team wants to see how Jackson responds before ruling on Sunday's game vs. Cleveland. Keeping the standard Injury tier; this is now a real question mark rather than a lean toward playing. SETBACK (10/16): did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (10/14-10/15) for a second straight week with the ankle injury -- HC Jesse Minter still calls him "day-to-day," but The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec said Sunday's outcome (home vs. Cleveland, 10/18) "seems pretty obvious" after the second absence (Baltimore Sun, CBS Sports). Tyler Huntley would start again if Jackson sits. roster.name: Breece Hall
roster.reason: Groin was a non-issue in Week 1 — ran for 102 yards and a TD on 22 carries plus 2 catches for 16 yards in the opener vs. Tennessee, his best workload in well over a year. Exited Sunday's Week 3 loss to Detroit in the second half with a quad/thigh injury after being tackled near the sideline (13 carries/32 yards, 3 catches/23 yards before leaving) — did not return. NEW: Monday's MRI (9/28) came back better than initially feared — the Jets and multiple reports now describe Hall as "week-to-week" rather than facing a long absence, with hope it's a couple of weeks rather than a month-plus. Reporting frames the likely absence as closer to a couple of weeks than a month-plus, with the Jets reportedly hopeful he can return before hitting the 4-game IR floor — but no outlet has nailed down an exact return week yet, so the Injury (not yet Short-Term or Long-Term) tier still fits. Braelon Allen remains the clear lead back in his absence, with Isaiah Davis next in line (NBC Sports, JetsXFactor, Jet Nation, 9/28-30). CONFIRMED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 game at Chicago with the quad/thigh injury, still described as week-to-week rather than a firm number of games. Braelon Allen again starts in his place, with Isaiah Davis next in line (RotoBaller, PrizePicks, 10/1-3). UPDATE (10/6): no firmer timeline has emerged since last week's report -- still officially OUT and described as "week-to-week" with no specific number of games attached. He did miss the actual Week 4 game at Chicago (10/4) as expected, with Braelon Allen (see his note) taking over as the clear lead back. Reporting continues to frame the Jets as hopeful he avoids IR, but no firm return date has been set as of today; keeping the standard Injury tier rather than Short-Term or Long-Term until a real number of weeks is reported (NBC Sports, SI/RotoBaller, NYJets.com). Braelon Allen remains the clear lead back in the meantime (see his note); keeping the standard Injury tier pending a firmer timeline. Still no firm number-of-games timeline from the Jets; Braelon Allen remains the clear lead back in his absence (see his note). HC Aaron Glenn continues to call the quad injury "week-to-week" and reportedly doesn't expect him to practice at all this week (ESPN, NBC Sports). Braelon Allen remains the clear lead back regardless. Still described as week-to-week with no specific games-missed count and no indication the Jets are moving him to IR (Newsweek, Yardbarker, 10/16). Braelon Allen remains the clear lead back in his absence. roster.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
roster.reason: Top-5 fantasy WR three years running (WR4 in PPG each of the last 3 seasons) — high floor, high ceiling, first-round caliber. Answered a quiet first half with 9 catches, 142 yards and 2 TDs in Thursday night's loss to Buffalo — his usual bell-cow target share showing up even in a losing effort.

roster.name: CeeDee Lamb
roster.reason: Coming off a down 2025 (75/1,077/3, worst yardage since his rookie year) but still a Round 2 pick — expected bounce-back with Pickens locked in alongside him. NEW (10/8): left Thursday night's Week 5 loss to Tampa Bay in the 4th quarter with a quad/thigh injury -- a recurrence of the thigh issue first flagged during the Week 3 win at Houston. Finished with a season-low 2 catches for 9 yards on 5 targets (coming off a 17-catch, 189-yard, career-high 21-target Week 4) as Dallas fell to the previously winless Buccaneers (DallasNews, NBC Sports, RotoBaller, 10/8). No Week 6 return timeline confirmed yet; George Pickens would be in line for a bigger target share if Lamb sits vs. Green Bay. UPDATE (10/15): no official Wednesday designation found yet for Sunday Night Football at Green Bay (10/18, Lambeau) -- but team sentiment remains optimistic: EVP Stephen Jones said Friday (10/10) he expects Lamb "all ready to go," and Ian Rapoport has characterized the quad injury as a bruise that's "not considered serious." Recheck Friday's final report for official confirmation. CLEARED (10/16): flipped from QUESTIONABLE back to ACTIVE -- the quad/thigh issue was confirmed as a bruise, not a strain, by NFL Network's Ian Rapoport ("not a major injury"), and Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones said Thursday he expects Lamb "all ready to go" for Sunday Night Football at Green Bay (10/18). Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. Week 6 final (10/18): played through the cleared quad bruise with no setback in Sunday Night Football's 23-13 loss at Green Bay -- drew a team-high 18 targets but converted them to just 9 catches for 70 yards, including a costly slipped route on a slant that Packers rookie Brandon Cisse intercepted. Dallas fell behind 17-0 at halftime and dropped to 2-4, its second straight loss; Dak Prescott threw 2 INTs on 34-of-54 passing. No new injury reported -- the quad is confirmed fully behind him; this was a low-efficiency game, not a health setback.

roster.name: Dallas Goedert
roster.reason: Suffered an MCL sprain in Philadelphia's Week 2 win over Tennessee when a Titans defender rolled into the side of his leg; initial reporting pegged him to miss a few weeks, and the Eagles brought back Zach Ertz as insurance at tight end. Played through it and appeared in each of the last two games rather than missing extended time, but was DOUBTFUL for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Jacksonville (played in London) after not practicing in the early part of that week -- a real step back rather than a continuation of the recent playing-through-it pattern. CLEARED (10/9-10): logged limited practices Wednesday/Thursday and then a full session Friday, and carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Jacksonville in London -- NBC Sports Philadelphia (John Clark) and RotoBaller both confirm he's expected to play. Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch given the clean practice ramp-up. Teammates DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Saquon Barkley (hamstring) are both inactive for the same game, which could mean extra receiving-game work funneling through Goedert if game script allows. Week 5 final (10/11): played through it as expected -- caught 6 passes for 38 yards in Jacksonville's 19-17 last-second win over Philadelphia in London. No new injury or setback reported; the MCL sprain appears fully behind him.

roster.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
roster.reason: Listed RB1 on New England's first unofficial 2026 depth chart ahead of TreVeyon Henderson — handles early-down/short-yardage work. New England's offense was thoroughly dominated in that game, complicating value for both backs, but downgrading Stevenson's tag from Depth Chart Secured to Depth Chart Battle to reflect Henderson's takeover (RotoWire, dknetwork, 9/27-28). Worth watching alongside the ongoing early-down competition with TreVeyon Henderson. Still splitting work with TreVeyon Henderson, but no indication the injury limited his role. UPDATE (10/13): the Henderson/Stevenson competition tilts back Stevenson's way -- Henderson suffered a new ankle injury in the same Week 5 win and was ruled out partway through (see Henderson's note), sent for testing Monday. With Henderson's Week 6 status uncertain, Stevenson is expected to see the bulk of New England's carries, reversing the recent trend toward Henderson as lead back (Yahoo Sports, 10/12). Upgrading tag from Depth Chart Battle toward a bigger role pending confirmation of Henderson's timeline. UPDATE (10/14): with TreVeyon Henderson now DOUBTFUL for Week 6 after Monday's ankle MRI (see Henderson's note), Stevenson is expected to handle the bulk of New England's backfield work vs. the Jets (Sun 10/18) -- a reversal of the Henderson-trending-to-lead-back pattern from the last few weeks. He played through his own leg issue with no setback in the Week 5 win over Las Vegas (9 carries, 57 yards, and a 3rd-quarter rushing TD through the portion of the game tracked before Henderson's exit). UPDATE (10/15): no fresh Week 6 practice-designation found for his own minor leg issue; the last confirmed report (10/8) had him banged up from Week 4 but not considered serious. Still expected to be New England's lead back for Week 6 given TreVeyon Henderson's doubtful/likely-out status (see Henderson's note).

roster.name: Travis Kelce
roster.reason: Now 37, the oldest TE in the league; production down two straight years (11.4 PPG in 2025, worst since 2015) — projected for a further step down (74/770/4).

roster.name: Kyle Monangai
roster.reason: Was fully healthy through Week 2 — the mid-August hyperextended knee and a hamstring tweak were non-issues, carrying no designation into Week 2's win over Minnesota as Chicago's clear RB2 behind Swift. CLEARED: returned to a full practice Friday (9/25) after being limited Wed/Thu — reporting is split on the exact body part (SI/Yahoo say hamstring, NBC Sports said knee; the Bears never officially disclosed it), but he carries no designation into Monday night's game at Philadelphia (9/28) (Bleacher Nation, Heavy.com, 9/25). Bigger Week 3 story for Chicago's offense is elsewhere: starting QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) is expected to sit Monday night, with Case Keenum tabbed to start — see Williams' note. Monangai remains Chicago's clear RB2 behind D'Andre Swift in that game script. HUGE WEEK 4 (10/4): ran for a reported 146 yards and 2 TDs as Chicago beat the Jets 23-12 with Tyson Bagent starting at QB (Chicago Sun-Times, Yahoo Sports) -- by far his best game of the season. Today's flip from Active to QUESTIONABLE has no confirmed new-injury report behind it as of 10/5; given his August hyperextended-knee history, treat this as a possible post-workload precaution rather than a confirmed new injury until a designation reason is reported. CONFIRMED (10/5): the specific reason behind Friday's Active-to-Questionable flip is now known -- a right thumb injury suffered late in Sunday's 146-yard, 2-TD Week 4 explosion (30 carries, after taking over the bulk of the workload once D'Andre Swift fumbled and exited with knee soreness in the 3rd quarter), which led Chicago to sit him the final ~4 minutes. HC Ben Johnson called it "day-to-day," said imaging showed nothing concerning, and expects him fine for Sunday vs. Green Bay (NBC Sports, Chicago Sun-Times, 10/5). Not knee-related as initially speculated. WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/10): flipped from QUESTIONABLE to OUT for Sunday's Week 5 game at Green Bay. HC Ben Johnson had called the thumb injury "not an issue" and expected him to play, but a separate turf-toe issue -- reported mid-week as potentially a 1-2 week issue -- proved to be the bigger factor, and he did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. D'Andre Swift (now cleared, see his note) projects for a bigger workhorse workload Sunday in his absence; Roschon Johnson is next in line. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Short-Term Injury given the reported 1-2 week framing. REVISED FROM SHORT-TERM TO STANDARD INJURY (10/14): the turf-toe timeline looks worse than last week's 1-2-week framing -- per Chicago Sun-Times reporting around 10/8-9, he was seen in a walking boot and saw a toe specialist, and HC Ben Johnson called it "a bigger deal than initially anticipated." No positive practice-return signal has surfaced since; downgrading tag back from Short-Term Injury to the standard Injury tier given the walked-back timeline, though the team has not put him on IR or attached a new firm number of weeks. D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's clear workhorse in the meantime; Bears play at Atlanta in Week 6 (Sun 10/18). UPDATE (10/16): estimated as a DNP again Wednesday (10/14) with turf toe (which HC Ben Johnson has called "a bigger deal than we initially anticipated") plus a thumb injury, after already missing Week 5 -- trending toward a second straight missed game Sunday vs. Atlanta (10/18). Not expected to land on IR; D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's clear lead back in the meantime. CONFIRMED (10/18): ruled out for Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Atlanta per the Chicago Sun-Times -- a second straight missed game with turf toe (plus a lingering thumb injury) after not practicing all week. HC Ben Johnson still calls it 'week-to-week' and said he's 'trending in the right direction,' while ESPN's Jeremy Fowler had floated a possible 1-2 week absence. D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's clear workhorse in the meantime, with Roschon Johnson next in line. UPDATE (10/22): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip matches the start of the new Week 7 practice-report cycle, but no independent beat reporting confirming improved practice participation for the turf toe/thumb issues was found as of this update -- HC Ben Johnson's "week-to-week"/"trending in the right direction" comments from last week remain the most recent confirmed word. Keeping the standard Injury tier rather than reading the flip as a confirmed recovery; D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's clear workhorse regardless.

roster.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
roster.reason: Just 1 catch on 1 target in Arizona's Week 2 blowout loss to Seattle despite playing 74% of offensive snaps — 1 catch total through 2 games this season, a sharp reversal from earlier optimism about an expanded role under new OC Mike LaFleur. ESPN's Dan Graziano reported (9/22) that league executives were wondering whether Arizona could explore trading Harrison; trade buzz intensified 9/22-9/23, and he was deactivated for Arizona's Week 5 game vs. Detroit (10/10-11) while a deal got finalized. TRADE CONFIRMED CLOSED (10/11): Houston Texans HC DeMeco Ryans confirmed the trade is complete after Houston's Week 5 win over Tennessee -- the Texans acquired Harrison from Arizona (KSL.com, TSN, AP/ABC News, 10/11). Reporting on the exact package is slightly inconsistent across outlets but the most-repeated version has Houston sending a 2027 2nd-round pick and a 2027 6th-round pick to Arizona, with Arizona sending Harrison plus a 2027 7th-round pick back -- a different final structure than the earlier 2028-2nd/Indianapolis-interest speculation. Our roster feed's "ARI" pro-team field is now stale data; he belongs to Houston. Finished his Arizona tenure with just 5 catches on 12 targets for 85 yards and a TD through 4 games. Role outlook is unsettled: he reunites with Ohio State teammate/Texans QB C.J. Stroud, and the pick investment signals real belief in unlocking his talent, but Nico Collins remains Houston's clear WR1 and Jaylin Noel has also been seeing expanded passing-game work (Saturday Down South, RotoBaller, SI, 10/11-12). No confirmed Week 6 practice report or 'will play' designation found yet as of 10/13 -- treat his immediate role/target share as unconfirmed rather than assume a big workload out of the gate.

roster.name: Titans D/ST
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Zach Charbonnet
roster.reason: Tore his ACL in the NFC Divisional Round last January and opened 2026 on Reserve/PUP, which requires missing at least Seattle's first four regular-season games (through Week 4) before he's even eligible to return to practice. HC Mike Macdonald said Friday (9/19) the team is "getting down to him possibly finding a date where he can start practicing again... that's coming soon," and multiple outlets describe his rehab as ahead of schedule with no setbacks — but he cannot play in Week 3 regardless, and an actual return likely lands closer to Week 5-6 once a practice window opens (Seahawks.com, Field Gulls). In his absence, Seattle signed away former Packers backup Emanuel Wilson, who stepped into real early-down work (21 carries/92 yards in Seattle's Week 2 win over Arizona).

roster.name: James Conner
roster.reason: Suffered a serious right foot injury in Week 3 of the 2025 season (loss at San Francisco), was carted off, and then-HC Jonathan Gannon confirmed days later that he needed season-ending foot surgery. Arizona opened the 2026 season with Conner on injured reserve continuing that rehab; per Draft Sharks/Arizona Sports, he's ineligible to return before Week 5 at the earliest (must miss a minimum of the first 4 games). New 2026 HC Mike LaFleur (Gannon was fired after the 2025 season) has declined to give a firm target return date, saying Conner has "earned the right to know" his timeline before it's made public — no confirmed return week, and no report found yet that Arizona has opened his 21-day practice window.

roster.name: Brock Purdy
roster.reason: Signed a massive 5-yr/$265M extension; finished as a QB1-range fantasy scorer in every full season as a starter, behind a receiving corps upgraded with Mike Evans and Christian Kirk.

roster.name: Christian McCaffrey
roster.reason: Full workhorse usage in the opener with no ill effects from the calf scare: 10 carries for 68 yards plus 5 catches for 20 yards in the win over the Rams. Held out of the end zone, but the touch volume is exactly what you want to see after last year's injury history. HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed this week the Week 1 split with rookie Kaelon Black (who out-carried him 14-10, 44% of snaps) was a deliberate plan to lighten McCaffrey's load: "That was the goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more... love taking some off Christian." Total touches were even (15-15), but expect Black to keep chipping into the carry share.

roster.name: Derrick Henry
roster.reason: Turns 32; 2025 was still elite (1,595 yds / 16 TD) with no decline signs yet, but a new play-caller and remade O-line add real variance this year. Showed zero decline signs in the Week 1 opener vs. Indianapolis: 24 carries for 144 yards and 3 rushing TDs (35.3 fantasy pts) as Baltimore's clear lead back, with only Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali behind him on the depth chart. Week 2 usage raised a flag: 16 carries for 68 yards and a TD plus 3 catches for 19 yards in the loss to New Orleans, but no explosive runs (long of 8 yards) and he was "puzzlingly" limited to just 5 carries in the second half even while Baltimore led — worth monitoring, not yet a confirmed workload cut (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Baltimore Beatdown). UPDATE: bounced back from the Week 2 workload dip — went for 89 yards and 2 TD on the ground in Baltimore's wild 34-31 win over Dallas in Brazil (Week 3, 9/27), reaffirming the workhorse role with no lingering effects from the light second-half usage two weeks ago. Week 4 (10/4): Baltimore beat Tennessee 24-18, but Henry was reportedly held in check by the Titans' run defense per a CBS Sports recap headline ("Derrick Henry shut down") -- the exact carry/yardage total could not be independently confirmed via box score due to source access limits, so treat this as a quiet, below-his-standard game rather than a new injury or role concern. Worth a follow-up once a clean box score is available.

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.reason: Missed Week 2 vs. New Orleans with the recurring hamstring injury (first tweaked in a Week 1 TD catch-and-run, aggravated further in that same game). CLEARED AND DELIVERED: active and effective in Sunday's Week 3 win over Dallas in Rio — 5 catches on 6 targets for 84 yards plus a 20-yard carry, turning half his touches into 20+ yard gains, including a 27-yard catch with time expiring that set up the game-winning field goal (NBC Sports, 9/27). No re-aggravation reported; the hamstring concern appears fully resolved with a full workload back in hand — Flowers projects back into his lead-receiver role for Baltimore. NEW (9/30): flipped back to a game-status designation (limited practice) as Baltimore continues managing the same hamstring that had him on a "pitch count" through Week 3's 5-catch, 84-yard game. HC Jesse Minter said Monday he expects Flowers to carry a full workload Week 4 vs. Tennessee; FantasyPros projects him roughly 79% likely to play with no new setback reported (NBC Sports, RotoWire, FantasyPros, 9/29-30). CLEARED (10/1-2): upgraded from limited to a full practice participant Thursday, officially shaking the hamstring designation ahead of Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Tennessee — full workload expected as Baltimore's lead receiver (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, 10/1-2). NEW DESIGNATION (10/2-3): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag again this week, but this reads as routine hamstring management rather than a new setback -- HC Jesse Minter said Flowers is "coming out of this thing really ready to push to be back in there closer to full time," and multiple outlets (RotoBaller, FantasyPros) are calling him a must-start WR1 Sunday vs. the 0-3 Titans if there's no in-week change. Watch Friday's final report, but treat this as a likely-to-play Questionable, not a real doubt. Entered Week 4 off a full Thursday practice with no setback, and OC/staff expected him to carry a full workload vs. Tennessee after Baltimore's win (team reports, 10/1). No new injury or designation has surfaced since; treating the hamstring issue as resolved and upgrading tag to Healthy as Baltimore's lead receiver. (Exact Week 4 box-score line could not be independently confirmed via search -- sourcing on the Ravens-Titans final was inconsistent.) UPDATE (10/8): the recurring hamstring issue produced another QUESTIONABLE tag -- Flowers was downgraded in Baltimore's final Week 4 injury report (questionable vs. Tennessee) and now carries the same designation into Sunday's Week 5 game at Atlanta as the team continues managing his workload week to week. No new injury or setback reported, just the same ongoing hamstring maintenance pattern. UPDATE (10/13): flipped from QUESTIONABLE back to ACTIVE. Pregame reporting had him questionable with a foot issue (distinct wording from the recurring hamstring, possibly just reporting inconsistency) but ESPN's Adam Schefter said he was expected to play Sunday night at Atlanta; Lamar Jackson (ankle) was out for that game with Tyler Huntley starting (see Jackson's note). Could not independently confirm the final score or Flowers' box-score line for that game via search as of this update -- treating today's ACTIVE flip as a likely no-new-designation reset for Week 6 rather than confirmed proof the hamstring is fully behind him. Recheck next cycle for the actual Week 5 result. Week 5 final (10/11): quiet by his standards but heavy volume -- 8 catches on 9 targets for 53 yards plus a 13-yard carry in Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win over Atlanta (Tyler Huntley started for the injured Lamar Jackson and scored the winning TD). No touchdown, and his longest catch went for just 12 yards -- a 26-yard grab on the late game-tying drive was wiped out by a defensive pass-interference penalty drawn in his favor. No new injury reported. NEW (10/15-16): added to Baltimore's Week 6 injury report with a toe injury, limited in both Thursday and Friday practice -- but no game designation on the final report, so he's good to play Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. Cleveland (10/18) per NBC Sports (10/16). Lamar Jackson's ankle (see his note) remains the bigger question mark for the Baltimore offense. CONFIRMED (10/18): today's QUESTIONABLE-to-ACTIVE flip matches what was already being reported -- the toe injury produced no game designation on Baltimore's final Week 6 report (NBC Sports, 10/16), so he's playing Sunday's home game vs. Cleveland at full workload as Baltimore's lead receiver. Lamar Jackson (ankle) is the bigger question for the passing game, now officially OUT (see his note) with Tyler Huntley starting.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.reason: Played through the previously undisclosed issue with no setback and led Pittsburgh's offense with 10 targets, turning them into 4 catches for 40 yards in the opener vs. Atlanta — the target volume was there even if the per-catch efficiency wasn't. Traded from Seattle to Pittsburgh in 2025 (Steelers sent a 2nd- and 7th-rounder, got back a 6th) and signed a 5-year, $150M extension there. UPDATE: named Steelers' Player of the Week after his Week 4 performance, remaining Pittsburgh's clear top target earner (Steelers.com, early week of 10/5). NEW (10/18): added to Pittsburgh's injury report Friday with an illness (not an injury) after missing practice -- RotoBaller reports he wasn't on the Wednesday/Thursday report, suggesting he started feeling sick late in the week. Steelers' WR room is thin behind him (Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek both out), so Germie Bernard would see a bigger role if Metcalf can't go Sunday vs. Tampa Bay. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch given the swift, late-week designation; illness-driven Questionable tags often clear on gameday, so recheck the final inactive list. CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/18): removed from Pittsburgh's injury report Saturday, ending the late-week illness scare, then delivered a big game in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over Tampa Bay -- 11 catches for 93 yards, tied with Germie Bernard (also 11 catches) for Pittsburgh's team high in receptions (Yahoo Sports, Behind the Steel Curtain, 10/18-19). Teammate Pat Freiermuth (calf) also carried a late QUESTIONABLE tag into the same game -- see his note. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean, productive game.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.reason: Played in the opener as expected off Achilles recovery, but usage was light (2 catches, 12 yards on 5 targets, 46.2% of snaps) — matches Shanahan's stated plan to manage his snap count. The Achilles maintenance plan wrapped up clean — upgraded to a full practice Friday (9/18) and removed from the injury report entirely, with no designation for Sunday vs. Miami; Wed/Thu limited reps were confirmed as planned workload management, not a new setback (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, 9/18).

roster.name: A.J. Brown
roster.reason: Left his Patriots debut early in the 3rd quarter of the Sept 9 NFL Kickoff Game (a 13-10 loss to Seattle) with a right ankle injury after Seahawks CB Nehemiah Pritchett's knee landed on his ankle; had 3 catches for 26 yds on 4 targets before exiting. Thursday's (Sept 10) MRI confirmed a high-ankle sprain (Tuesday-night X-rays had been negative). Confirmed Sept 11 (AP): Patriots are placing him on injured reserve, officially ruling him out a minimum of four games under IR roster rules — New England is also signing DT DaQuan Jones as a separate roster move. Treat him as unplayable through at least Week 4. Arrived via trade from PHI (Patriots sent Philadelphia a 2028 1st-round pick and a 2027 5th-round pick); signed for up to $112.75M with $32.75M guaranteed. Was stepping into a wide-open target share atop New England's WR room before the injury. ACTIVATED AND RETURNED (10/18): activated off injured reserve and made his Patriots home debut in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets, ending a 4-game absence with the high-ankle sprain suffered in his Sept. 9 Patriots debut. The return was rusty -- just 3 catches for 27 yards on 9 targets with multiple drops, plus a muffed-onside-kick mishap his teammates covered for (Boston Globe, NESN, 10/18-19). Drake Maye (3 TD passes, 0 INT) carried New England's offense in the win; expect Brown's role/rapport to build gradually. Downgrading tag from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch now that he's actually back on the field. MANAGED, NOT A SETBACK (10/20-21): limited at Monday's walkthrough and Tuesday's practice with the same high-ankle sprain he returned from last week, but this reads as short-week load management rather than a new issue -- Brown told reporters he's "absolutely" ready for Thursday night's Week 7 game at the Bears, and HC Mike Vrabel and Brown himself both describe the ankle as not a lingering concern (ESPN's Mike Reiss, Heavy.com, Athlon, 10/20). Keeping Health Watch; today's QUESTIONABLE game-status flip is expected to clear by Thursday's kickoff.

roster.name: Woody Marks
roster.reason: Was Houston's clear passing-down/receiving-work back behind David Montgomery through the first several weeks, holding real standalone value even in a committee. NEW (10/13): took over as Houston's lead back after David Montgomery exited Sunday's Week 5 win over Tennessee (26-3) with a groin injury -- finished with a season-high 15 carries for 62 yards plus 4 catches, reportedly logging roughly 85% of the Texans' backfield snaps once Montgomery left (FantasyPros, Athlon Sports, SI/OnSI, 10/12). With Montgomery now DOUBTFUL/week-to-week (see his note), Marks projects as Houston's clear lead back for as long as that lasts. UPDATE (10/13): confirmed to keep the expanded lead-back role for Week 6 in Montgomery's continued absence, replicating his Week 5 workload (15 carries/62 yards, 4 catches) -- per FantasyFootballers and CBS Sports (~10/13). Jawhar Jordan and practice-squad RB Deuce Vaughn are the depth pieces behind him if needed.

roster.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
roster.reason: Finished 2025 as the No. 2 fantasy TE in PPR and was projected top-5 again in 2026 as one of Penix's top two targets alongside London, but the profile hasn't shown up in the box score through 3 games. NEW: just 1 catch on 2 targets for 5 yards in Thursday night's Week 3 win over Green Bay (35-14) — his line through 3 games is now just 2 catches for 20 yards on 6 targets. QB Michael Penix Jr. is clearly funneling the passing game elsewhere (London had a 9/194 day the same game); worth downgrading expectations until target share shows up (RotoWire/NBC Sports, 9/24).

roster.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
roster.reason: Fractured his left wrist coming down awkwardly after a Lamar Jackson end-zone target during Sunday's win over Indianapolis; finished with 1 catch for 11 yards before exiting in the 2nd quarter. Surgery on the wrist was performed Wednesday morning (Sept 16) and reported successful; Baltimore officially placed him on injured reserve the same day. The NFL's mandatory 4-game minimum rules him out through Week 5 (Saints, Cowboys, Titans, Falcons), with HC Jesse Minter saying he has "a really good chance of coming back here pretty quick" once eligible — Week 6 vs. Cleveland is the target, not yet guaranteed. Ravens promoted WR Chris Moore from the practice squad to fill the roster spot. Puts his WR2-behind-Flowers breakout runway on hold for at least a month. ACTIVATED (10/17): designated for return and logged a full practice before being activated off injured reserve ahead of Sunday's Week 6 game at Cleveland, ending the 4-game-minimum absence from his Week 1 wrist fracture/surgery (Baltimore Ravens official site, NBC Sports Fantasy, 10/14-17). His specific snap count/target share in Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns could not be confirmed via search as of this update -- Baltimore's passing game ran through backup Tyler Huntley (19-of-31, 165 yds, 1 TD) with Lamar Jackson out again (ankle, see his note), so expect a gradual route back to volume rather than an immediate workload. Softening tag from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch now that he's actually back and eligible. WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): active for his first game off IR, as expected, in Baltimore's 13-10 loss at Cleveland; his specific snap count/target share could not be confirmed via search as of this update, with Baltimore's passing game going through backup QB Tyler Huntley (Lamar Jackson out again, ankle -- see his note). Keeping Health Watch pending a clearer read on his workload next week.

roster.name: DJ Moore
roster.reason: Confirmed trade (official March 11, 2026, roster move finalized Aug 17): Bears sent Moore plus a 2026 5th-round pick to Buffalo for a 2026 2nd-round pick. Bills guaranteed $15.5M of his 2028 salary, and the trade also guaranteed his 2027 salary — reshapes the WR room alongside Shakir. Followed a strong Week 1 (21.0 fantasy pts) with a scary exit from Thursday night's Week 2 win over Detroit (AC joint sprain), but the injury turned out to be minor. CLEARED: active for Sunday's Week 3 win over the Chargers and led Buffalo in targets, catches and receiving yards (6 catches on 10 targets for 67 yards) with no setback reported (NBC Sports, 9/27) — the shoulder is fully behind him. NEW (9/30): back on a game-status designation (limited, worked in a non-contact jersey) as Buffalo continues managing the same AC joint/shoulder sprain from Week 2 — not a new injury or setback. Reporting across RotoWire/CBS/Yahoo frames it as ongoing rest/management; he's expected to play Week 4 vs. New England (9/30). CLEARED (10/3): the AC-joint/shoulder sprain is fully behind him -- back to a full practice week with no setback, and expected to play Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. New England. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. NEW DESIGNATION (10/5): back to QUESTIONABLE today after being cleared to Healthy on 10/3. No new injury mechanism or beat-writer report has surfaced tying this to a specific in-game exit from Sunday's Week 4 game vs. New England -- stating that plainly rather than guessing. Given his recurring AC-joint/shoulder history, treat this as probable continued precautionary management rather than a new, more serious issue until further reporting clarifies it. Downgrading tag from Healthy back to Health Watch. WORSENED (10/16): did not practice the estimated Wednesday report or Thursday's walkthrough with the AC joint/shoulder sprain (originally a Week 2 injury that's been re-aggravated multiple times) -- multiple outlets (WGRZ, Heavy.com) now say he's unlikely to play Sunday vs. the Raiders (10/18) and could instead use Buffalo's Week 7 bye to fully heal. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the real absence risk. CONFIRMED OUT (10/18): officially inactive for Buffalo's 33-30 win at Las Vegas with the recurring AC-joint/shoulder sprain, missing his second game in three weeks; Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir absorbed the added target share. Buffalo now has its Week 7 bye before a Nov. 1 game vs. Baltimore, giving Moore roughly two extra weeks to heal with no specific new timeline reported -- keeping the standard Injury tier given the recurring nature of this shoulder issue, but the bye materially helps his odds of a clean return. BYE-WEEK RESET (10/22): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip is procedural, not a recovery signal -- Buffalo is on its Week 7 bye (confirmed via NFL.com/Fox Sports bye lists), so there's no game this week for any designation to attach to. The recurring AC-joint/shoulder sprain hasn't been given any new timeline by the team; next game is Nov. 1 vs. Baltimore, giving Moore the full two-week bye window to heal.

roster.name: Caleb Williams
roster.reason: Had emerged as a fantasy-relevant weekly starter behind an improved Ben Johnson offense before the injury hit — real weekly upside as a rushing/passing dual threat. CONFIRMED: officially ruled OUT for Week 3 vs. Philadelphia with a Grade 2 hamstring strain and did not play (0 fantasy points). Reporting pegs the expected absence at 3-4 weeks, which would also cost him Weeks 4-5 (NYJ, GB) with a Week 6 return vs. Atlanta as the earliest realistic target (SI/OnSI, Yahoo Sports, 9/27-29). HC Ben Johnson has called him "week to week" without confirming the Week 4 questionable framing bettors are seeing — with no progress in practice participation this week, Williams should be considered questionable at best, and more likely a second-straight missed game. Keeping the Injury tag (not yet Long-Term) since the reported 3-4 week window sits just under the ~month/4-game long-term threshold, but this bears watching if it slips further. UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to DOUBTFUL for Week 4 vs. the Jets, but this looks like a procedural downgrade rather than a sign he's rounding into game shape — the operative 3-4 week / Week 6-at-Atlanta timeline from last week's reporting has NOT been revised as of the Wednesday practice cycle (Yahoo Sports, BearGoggleson.com, ProFootballNetwork). HC Ben Johnson continues to call him "week-to-week" without confirming a Week 4 questionable framing. Treat him as unlikely to play Sunday; Case Keenum (not Tyson Bagent, who is also out) remains Chicago's starter after authoring a 247-yard, 2-TD upset of Philadelphia (27-7) on Week 3 Monday Night Football, including an 8-yard TD to Luther Burden III plus a rushing score. CONFIRMED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. the Jets, missing a second straight game with the Grade 2 hamstring strain -- the original 3-4 week / Week 6-at-Atlanta timeline from two weeks ago has NOT been revised. Case Keenum remains Chicago's starter (SI/Betting, PrizePicks, 10/1-3). CORRECTION + UPDATE (10/5): Chicago's Week 4 starter was Tyson Bagent, not Case Keenum as referenced in last week's note -- Bagent threw for a career-high 268 yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets (Chicago Sun-Times, Yahoo Sports, 10/4), with Kyle Monangai running for 146 yards and 2 TDs behind him (see Monangai's note). Williams (hamstring) missed a second straight game and remains "week to week" per HC Ben Johnson with no firm return date announced as of 10/5; Chicago is in no rush given Bagent's play. The original 3-4 week / Week 6-at-Atlanta timeline has still not been formally revised. FLAGGING A DISCREPANCY (10/10): ESPN's roster status flipped from OUT to QUESTIONABLE ahead of Sunday's Week 5 game at Green Bay, but this does NOT appear to reflect a real return -- all beat reporting through Thursday (10/8) continued to describe Williams as not practicing and "week-to-week" with the Grade 2 hamstring strain, with Tyson Bagent set to start a third straight game and the Week 6-vs.-Atlanta target still the operative return expectation (RotoBaller, Athletic/Wiederer via RotoBaller, 10/5-8). Treating the QUESTIONABLE tag as a likely data/procedural artifact rather than confirmation he's playing Sunday -- recheck the Bears' actual Friday practice report before trusting it. Keeping the standard Injury tier. CONFIRMED (10/12): missed a fourth straight game, inactive for Sunday's Week 5 loss at Green Bay (Packers won 31-7). Tyson Bagent started again and struggled (12-of-21, 87 yards, 0 TD, 2 INT, 27.4 rating, 2 sacks) before being benched in the 4th quarter for Case Keenum (11-of-19, 108 yards, 1 INT). No new return timeline reported; Week 6 vs. Atlanta remains the target, keeping the standard Injury tier. UPDATE (10/13): real progress -- returned to a limited practice Friday (10/9) after resuming throwing drills, and The Athletic's Dan Wiederer reports Chicago never placed him on IR, keeping Week 6 vs. Atlanta (10/18) live as his target. He's still building back to full-speed running, and HC Ben Johnson is calling his return "to be determined"/benchmark-based rather than confirming he plays -- Rapoport/Pelissero flagged Week 6 or the following week (10/22 vs. NE) as the likely activation window, with no hard date set (NBC Sports, Bleacher Nation, 10/9-10). UPDATE (10/14): trending toward a Week 6 return vs. Atlanta (Sun 10/18) but still unconfirmed by the team itself -- Ian Rapoport reported (10/12) "all signs point" to Williams playing, citing a completed strenuous pregame workout and his first limited practice since the injury (Fri 10/9). HC Ben Johnson has NOT guaranteed it, saying only that Williams would be "close." The Chicago Sun-Times (10/11) floated the team instead targeting the following week (Oct 22 vs. New England) given the short Thu turnaround after a Sunday game, calling the decision "to be determined." Keeping the standard Injury tier until an actual designation/practice grade confirms he's playing. UPGRADE (10/14): took a full practice Wednesday, per HC Ben Johnson (Yahoo Sports/SI, BleacherNation) -- a real step up from last week's limited/estimated sessions. Johnson still won't commit to naming him the starter until closer to Sunday's game at Atlanta, but a full practice week is a strong signal he plays. Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Health Watch given the clean practice participation. UPDATE (10/16): a full practice participant Wednesday (10/14) after missing three straight games with a Grade 2 hamstring strain -- NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports "all signs point" to Williams returning Sunday vs. Atlanta (10/18), and the Bears have moved to roughly 3-point favorites, suggesting the market expects him back. HC Ben Johnson hasn't confirmed the start, calling it "still fluid." RETURNED AND DOMINANT (10/18): made his return from the 3-game hamstring absence in Sunday's 31-23 win at Atlanta with zero lingering effects -- went 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a TD to Colston Loveland, including a 12-of-12 start before his first incompletion. Chicago held off a 24-point Atlanta rally attempt to improve to 4-2; D'Andre Swift ran for 2 TDs (see his note). Williams said afterward his body felt great but that managing it will be "a weekly thing" (ESPN, CBS Chicago, Yahoo Sports, 10/18). Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Healthy given the clean, full-workload return; Chicago is back in action Thursday vs. New England on a short week, worth checking his practice reps given the quick turnaround.

roster.name: Jaylen Warren
roster.reason: Confirmed as Pittsburgh's Week 1 RB1 over Rico Dowdle, and it held up in the box score — out-touched Dowdle 15-10 in the Week 1 win, the more involved back in both the run and pass game. Signed a 2-year extension through 2027 (~$17.5M total, $12M guaranteed) in September 2025. CLEARED: played through the shoulder issue and delivered Pittsburgh's clear workhorse performance in Sunday's Week 3 win vs. Cincinnati with Dowdle (toe) out — a season-high workload (48 total touches through 3 games, headlined by a big Week 3 day) confirms him as the unquestioned RB1 for as long as Dowdle is sidelined (NBC Sports, 9/27). Rookie 7th-rounder Eli Heidenreich or Travis Homer remain the only backup options behind him. NEW (10/1): produced 17 carries for 93 yards plus 3 catches for 33 yards in Thursday Night Football's Week 4 loss at Cleveland (27-24) with Dowdle again out — his third straight game as Pittsburgh's clear lead back, continuing the workhorse role with no sign of a committee forming.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.reason: Chicago's clear RB1 in Ben Johnson's scheme. The Sept 3 practice scare was cramping, not a leg injury, and it showed no lingering effect — torched Carolina for 18 carries, 124 yards and 3 TDs (plus a catch) in Sunday's 59-37 win, arguably his best game as a Bear. The Week 2 knee/ankle concern is resolved — logged a full practice Friday (9/18) and was removed from Chicago's injury report entirely, carrying no designation into Sunday's game at Minnesota (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, 9/18). NEW (10/1-2): popped up on Chicago's Week 4 injury report as a non-participant Thursday with a knee injury — a new issue, not a recurrence of the earlier cramping/knee-ankle scares. He was off the Wednesday walkthrough report and had just carried 20 times for 84 yards in Chicago's prior game, so beat writers flagged the sudden Thursday DNP as worth watching; no designation confirmed yet pending Friday's report, with hope he's a full go Sunday vs. the Jets (Chicago Sun-Times, Bleacher Nation, 10/1-2). CLEARED (10/3): the Thursday DNP knee scare did not linger -- Swift practiced fully later in the week and carries no designation into Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Jets, remaining Chicago's unquestioned RB1. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. NEW (10/4): fumbled in the 3rd quarter of Chicago's 23-12 Week 4 win over the Jets and did not return, finishing with 15 carries for 58 yards and 2 catches for 16 yards; was seen limping postgame with soreness in the same knee that had been a minor pregame concern. HC Ben Johnson did not frame it as a benching. Kyle Monangai (see his note) took over and torched the Jets for 146 yards/2 TD on 30 carries in relief. No official injury designation or severity reported yet as of 10/5-6 -- downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending clarity; Chicago's Week 5 backfield split is worth watching since both backs picked up bumps in the same game (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Bleacher Nation, Heavy.com, 10/4). CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Green Bay -- the hip/knee issue that kept him out of Wednesday's practice resolved by Friday. Remains Chicago's lead back; downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

roster.reason: Still a fantasy WR1 when healthy (ESPN ranks him WR10) — three straight 1,000-yard seasons, 21 TDs over that stretch — but the Grade 1 hamstring strain has now cost him back-to-back games. CONFIRMED: officially ruled OUT for Week 3 vs. the Colts (Sunday) — his second straight missed game with the same hamstring strain (NBC Sports, Last Word on Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/25-26). NEW: HC DeMeco Ryans said he's "hopeful" Collins is available for Week 4 vs. Dallas, and Adam Schefter reports a "decent chance" he returns, but Collins did not practice Monday and will need to show up as at least a limited participant Wednesday-Friday to have a realistic shot at playing (ESPN/Schefter, CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 9/27-29). Keeping Injury tag until he's actually back on the practice field; Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Jaylin Noel remain Houston's top three WRs in his absence. UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Week 4 vs. Dallas. HC DeMeco Ryans said Monday (9/28) he's "hopeful"/there's a "decent chance" Collins plays, calling his rehab progress "really good" (CBS Sports, NBC Sports). The QUESTIONABLE tag implies he returned to practice in at least a limited fashion this week for the first time since the injury — a real, meaningful step, but he'll still need Thu/Fri practice participation to be considered a lock. One aggregator flagged a separate "knee (limited)" note that isn't corroborated elsewhere and should be treated with caution rather than as a new injury. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte continue to lead Houston's WR snaps/targets in his absence. CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/2-3): officially active for Monday Night Football's Week 4 game at Dallas, ending his absence with the hamstring strain -- he told ESPN Friday "Hell yeah, I'm playing this week" and was not listed on Houston's final injury report. Downgrading tag from Injury to Healthy; this snaps him back in as Houston's clear WR1 over Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte. Week 4 final (10/4): played in his return from the hamstring strain and caught 4 of his targets for 54 yards as Houston routed Dallas 34-10 (CBS Sports). Modest workload in the first game back -- no new injury reported, worth tracking snap/target share growth as he ramps back toward full volume in Week 5.

roster.name: Mike Evans
roster.reason: Monday (9/21) update: Shanahan said the hip "will have to be managed this week" and Evans would likely miss some practice time. Turns 33 in August — an aging watch item independent of any single-week injury. UPDATE: exited Week 3's loss to Arizona early in the 2nd quarter with a rib injury after a hard hit from S Budda Baker on a middle-of-the-field catch — was carted off and did not return, finishing with 3 catches for 34 yards and a TD before leaving (ESPN, CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/27-28). Downgrading tag from Aging-Watch-only injury risk to Health Watch: Evans returned to practice Friday and is officially Questionable for Week 4 vs. Denver, with HC Kyle Shanahan indicating optimism that he'll play (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Last Word on Sports, 9/26-29). Treat as a game-time-decision-caliber Questionable, not a real absence risk at this point. CLEARED (10/5): the rib strain suffered vs. Arizona in Week 3 is behind him -- today's status flip from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE confirms he's cleared the issue that had him day-to-day. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to reflect no current injury; turns 33 in August remains a standalone long-term watch item (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Last Word on Sports). UPDATE (10/8): the Week 3 rib injury remains a recurring game-status item -- Evans played through it in Week 4 (76 yards, NBC Sports, 10/4) and is again QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Denver; Forbes' fantasy injury roundup (10/7) described it as 'not overly serious' at this point, consistent with his pattern of limited practice reps but suiting up. CORRECTION + CLEARED (10/10): last week's note misstated San Francisco's Week 5 opponent as Denver -- the 49ers actually play Seattle in Week 5. Evans was upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's game vs. the Seahawks; he was limited in Wednesday's practice with the recurring rib issue (NBC Sports Fantasy, 10/7) but cleared by Friday, continuing the pattern of playing through this injury each of the last two weeks. DELIVERED (10/13): no setback from the rib -- caught 7 passes for 113 yards and a TD, plus a 2-point conversion, in San Francisco's 32-29 win over Seattle on Sunday 10/11, pushing the 49ers to 5-0 (ESPN box score, gameId 401872992). Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean workload and no re-aggravation; remains SF's clear top receiving weapon alongside Deebo Samuel (who left the same game with a hamstring injury -- see his note). NEW (10/15-16): HC Kyle Shanahan said Evans will not practice Thursday due to Achilles soreness, on top of the recurring rib issue he's played through in recent weeks; his status for Monday night's Week 6 home game vs. Washington (10/19) is in question. With Deebo Samuel Sr. also out (hamstring, see his note), Jacob Cowing, Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins would see larger roles if Evans sits too. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch given the fresh soreness and missed practice; no multi-week framing reported, treat as day-to-day pending Friday's practice report. EXITED (10/19): left Monday night's 23-17 win over Washington before halftime with right Achilles soreness after leading all receivers with 3 catches for 94 yards; did not return. HC Kyle Shanahan described it as Achilles tendonitis and said he didn't believe further imaging was needed, and beat reporter Jennifer Lee Chan reports the tendon is intact -- he's expected to miss "a little time," with speculation his return could line up around San Francisco's Week 8 bye (ESPN, NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, 10/19-20). Revising tag from Health Watch to Short-Term Injury given the relatively optimistic, tendon-intact framing, but his Sunday vs. Atlanta status is unconfirmed as of this update -- some analysts expect SF to rest him given the upcoming bye. Deebo Samuel Sr. remains out separately (hamstring, see his note), so a Niners WR room already thin would thin further if Evans also sits.

roster.name: Isaiah Likely
roster.reason: Signed for 3yr/$40M+, now the clear TE1 ahead of Theo Johnson, reunited with HC John Harbaugh — real path to a top-10 fantasy TE role after sharing looks with Mark Andrews in Baltimore. NEW (10/8): limited at Wednesday's practice with a knee/groin issue and carries a QUESTIONABLE tag into Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington (Giants' official injury report, 10/7) -- first injury concern since signing. No severity or timeline reported yet; check Friday's final designation. CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday night's Week 5 game vs. Atlanta -- no setback from the knee/groin issue that limited him in practice this week. First clean bill of health since signing with Baltimore.

roster.name: Jaylen Waddle
roster.reason: The camp hamstring strain was fully resolved for Week 1 with Denver, but the passing-game role was thin in his Broncos debut — just 1 catch for 2 yards on 3 targets as Courtland Sutton and the run game dominated the offense. Worth monitoring whether target share improves in Week 2 now that he's fully healthy, or whether Denver's offense simply doesn't feed him volume. Week 3 (9/27, 30-26 win over the Rams): played a full complement of snaps (~73%) but was again a non-factor in the passing game — just 2 catches on 7 targets for 10 yards, plus a 14-yard end-around carry and a 2-point conversion catch. Sutton and the run game continue to dominate Denver's offense (NBC Sports, ESPN box score). NEW (9/30): Tracker flips ACTIVE to QUESTIONABLE after Waddle was seen leaving the stadium postgame in a walking boot on his right foot, which triggered 48 hours of speculation. Multiple outlets (NBC Sports, RotoWire, RotoBaller, Yahoo Sports/ClutchPoints, Heavy.com, all 9/29) cite team sources/beat reporting that he is "fine"/"okay" and that the boot was a routine postgame-inflammation precaution, not a structural injury — once a player is limited in practice, the injury report requires a game-status tag. No source indicates a ligament or fracture issue. Best read: trending toward playing Week 4 at San Francisco in the same complementary role. CLEARED (9/30): the postgame walking-boot scare is fully resolved — Waddle was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, officially clearing him for Week 4 vs. San Francisco. HC Sean Payton and team sources had already downplayed the boot as a routine precautionary measure, not a structural foot/ankle issue; no diagnosis was ever confirmed (RotoBaller, Mile High Report, PrizePicks, 9/30). Role still capped by Denver's run-first offense — just 2 catches on 7 targets for 10 yards in Week 3. Week 4 final (10/4): Denver fell to San Francisco 24-14 (Broncos to 2-2). Waddle caught 5 of 6 targets for 35 yards and his first TD as a Bronco (a 13-yard score with a 2-point conversion that cut the deficit to 17-14) -- but was otherwise quiet, targeted on roughly 16% of his routes for a third time in four games. Denver's run-first, Bo Nix-led offense still isn't feeding him consistent volume despite the touchdown (NBC Sports, Mile High Report, CBS Sports, 10/4).

roster.name: 49ers D/ST
roster.reason: Fringe top-10 pass rush anchored by Nick Bosa, though the unit ranks closer to the middle of the pack (~20th) in preseason fantasy defense rankings — streaming-caliber if the front seven stays healthy. Added off waivers with no notable injury or personnel news to report.

roster.name: Cam Little
roster.reason: Jacksonville's starting kicker, known for elite leg strength on long attempts — no competition for the job.

roster.name: Bryce Young
roster.reason: Legitimate early-season breakout: 6 total TDs (passing) against just 1 INT through two 2026 games, averaging 8.9 yards per attempt, with a 34-3 Week 2 rout of Atlanta headlined by a 23-of-36, 287-yard, 3-TD, 0-INT line (116.3 rating). Became the second QB in Panthers history with multiple TD passes in each of the team's first two games (joining Jake Delhomme in 2007); new OC Brad Idzik's scheme change is being credited by beat writers as a real driver of the improvement, not just matchup variance. Worth monitoring for regression given a small sample and the difficulty of NFL defenses adjusting, but two clean, efficient starts is a real signal after a rocky first three pro seasons (ESPN, Yahoo Sports).

roster.name: DeMario Douglas
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Pat Freiermuth
roster.reason: NEW (10/18): added to Pittsburgh's injury report late in the week with a calf issue and carried a QUESTIONABLE tag into Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Tampa Bay, alongside DK Metcalf's own (since-cleared) illness scare (Yahoo Sports, sportsnetpittsburgh, 10/17-18). His specific playing status/usage in Sunday's 26-19 OT win over the Buccaneers could not be confirmed via search as of this update -- DK Metcalf (11 catches, 93 yards) and Germie Bernard (11 catches) combined to dominate Pittsburgh's receiving game, which could mean a lighter role for Freiermuth even if he suited up. Recheck the next report to confirm he's clear of the calf issue. WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): played through the calf issue with a light workload -- 2 catches for 11 yards on 3 targets in the 26-19 OT win over Tampa Bay, with DK Metcalf (11-93) and Germie Bernard (game-winning TD, 11 catches/87 yards) dominating the receiving game as expected (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports box score, 10/18). No setback reported. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean clearance, though his real-world role remains a distant complementary piece behind Metcalf and Bernard.

roster.name: Alvin Kamara
roster.reason: Made his 2026 season debut in Week 2 (24-17 win over Baltimore) after missing the entire preseason and Week 1 with a sprained MCL; efficiency was underwhelming in the opener back — 9 carries for 15 yards, plus 5 catches (6 targets) for 7 yards. Split early-down work with Travis Etienne Jr., whose role changed noticeably once Kamara returned to the lineup; expect a committee approach in New Orleans' backfield for now rather than a clear bell-cow role. Profiles as a low-end RB3/flex for Week 3 vs. the Raiders on PPR volume alone, but the explosive-play juice from his pre-injury form hasn't shown up yet (CBS Sports). UPDATE (9/30): with Travis Etienne Jr. now out with a hamstring injury (see Etienne's note), Kamara becomes New Orleans' clear early-down/passing-down workhorse near-term rather than a committee piece — upgrading the tag from Committee to Workhorse Lock while Etienne is sidelined. Kendre Miller/CJ Donaldson are the only complementary depth behind him (SI/Saints, NBC Sports, atozsports.com, 9/27-29). UPDATE (10/5-6): scored 3 TDs in New Orleans' Monday night win over Atlanta, reinforcing his status as the clear lead back with Travis Etienne Jr. still on IR (CBS Sports, 10/5-6). NEW (10/8): did not practice Wednesday with a back injury and is a real question mark for Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Minnesota (Saints' official injury report via Canal Street Chronicles, 10/7) -- a new issue, not the rib history from past seasons. With Travis Etienne Jr. still on IR, a Kamara absence would push touches to Kendre Miller (and possibly rookie CJ Donaldson). CLEARED (10/12): played through the back injury in Sunday's Week 5 home loss to Minnesota (Saints fell 13-23, held to just 142 total yards on offense); specific carry/yardage totals for Kamara could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update. Remains New Orleans' clear lead back with Travis Etienne Jr. still on IR. UPDATE (10/16): logged a second straight limited practice Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the back injury; no formal game designation yet, but outlets project him active Sunday at the Giants (10/18). Backup Kendre Miller logged 10 carries and a TD in Week 5 and would be the clear early-down beneficiary again if Kamara's back limits him further (see Miller's note). WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): played through the back injury with no issue in New Orleans' 34-27 win over the Giants -- 7 carries for 34 yards plus 2 catches for 35 yards, including a 31-yard TD reception, and the game pushed him past 5,000 career scrimmage yards (NFL.com, 10/18). Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; remains New Orleans' clear lead back with Travis Etienne Jr. still on IR.

roster.name: Cam Skattebo
roster.reason: Fully cleared from last year's gruesome rookie ankle injury (dislocation + open fracture) and confirmed as the Giants' Week 1 starting RB over Tyrone Tracy Jr., hosting Dallas on Sunday Night Football. Held to just 12 carries for 36 yards, 4 catches for 19 yards, and a lost fumble in Monday night's 28-6 loss at the Rams — the whole Giants game plan was wrecked after QB Jaxson Dart left with a knee injury on the first series (182 total team yards); treat the poor box score as game-script-driven, not a role change (RotoWire, CBS Sports). NEW (10/8): limited at Wednesday's practice with a shoulder issue, officially QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington (Giants' injury report, 10/7) -- distinct from last year's season-ending ankle fracture/dislocation. No word yet on severity or workload impact pending Friday's report. CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington -- cleared the shoulder issue that limited him in back-to-back Wednesday/Thursday practices after opening the week in a non-contact jersey. On track for his usual workhorse workload (bolavip, NBC Sports Fantasy, 10/7-9). Week 5 final (10/11): played through the shoulder issue with no setback -- 13 carries for 59 yards plus 2 catches for 12 yards (40 of his 71 scrimmage yards came in overtime) in a 27-27 tie at Washington. Costly moment: fumbled at the Washington 24-yard line late in OT with the Giants in range for a potential game-winning field goal. No injury fallout reported from the game; remains the clear starter.

roster.name: Jadarian Price
roster.reason: Handled the clear early-down workload before exiting: 13 carries for 52 yards plus a catch for 8 yards in Sunday's 31-7 win at Arizona (Drew Lock starting for the injured Sam Darnold), before leaving in the second half — officially Questionable to return, then held out. CLEARED: full practice Friday, no designation for Week 3 vs. Washington — HC Mike Macdonald confirmed the shoulder is a non-issue (SI, NBC Sports, Seahawks.com, 9/24-25). Efficiency profile stands out even in a crowded backfield: through 2 games he ranks top-6 among qualifying RBs in explosive-run rate, top-5 in yards after contact per attempt, and top-6 in missed-tackle rate (FantasyPros) — but Zach Charbonnet (PUP/ACL) aside, Seattle is still running a real 3-way rotation with George Holani and Emanuel Wilson rather than handing Price a clean bell-cow role. NEW (9/30): this is a recurring chest injury (originally suffered in Week 2 at Arizona, now confirmed by Seahawks PR and national reporters as chest, not the shoulder issue referenced in an earlier note) — Price was limited again in Wednesday's Week 4 practice with the same issue. He played through a full clearance into Week 3 but logged a career-low 28% snap share/6 touches (22 scrimmage yards) in that game, and now the chest is lingering into Week 4 prep vs. the Chargers. No structural/imaging concern has been reported; HC Mike Macdonald had given a positive update earlier in the cycle (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 9/30). NEW/WORSENED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. the Chargers with the recurring chest injury, after being limited/DNP through the week. No surgery or multi-week timeline has been reported, so this stays at the standard Injury tier rather than Short-Term, pending a clearer return estimate. George Holani and Emanuel Wilson (newly added to this roster) are set to pick up the early-down work in Seattle's RB-by-committee backfield, with Zach Charbonnet still out on PUP/recovering from ACL surgery.

roster.name: Romeo Doubs
roster.reason: Signed in free agency; profiles as a high-volume slot piece similar to Diggs' old role now that Diggs is gone. PLACED ON IR (10/19-20): dove for a 42-yard go-ahead TD catch from Drake Maye in the 1st quarter of Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets and landed hard on his shoulder, first questionable to return before being ruled out; the Patriots officially placed him on injured reserve Monday (10/19), which rules him out a minimum of four games under NFL IR rules (ESPN, NBC Sports, Boston.com, Heavy.com, 10/19). No surgery has been announced and a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler the injury isn't expected to keep him out long-term -- he's hopeful to return around New England's bye in late November, with one outlet pegging Week 12 vs. the Chargers as an earliest-return target. Upgrading tag from Breakout Watch to Long-Term Injury per the official IR designation (our fixed tiering rule treats any IR stint as Long-Term regardless of the softer verbal outlook); Mack Hollins and DeMario Douglas are set to see expanded roles in New England's receiver room in the meantime.

roster.name: Jordan Love
roster.reason: Played Thursday night's Week 3 loss at Atlanta (Falcons won 35-14) with no recurrence of the Week 2 elbow/hand-numbness scare — a clean non-issue as expected. Final line: 28/53, 312 yards, 2 TD (Christian Watson 4-yard, Matthew Golden 15-yard), 1 INT, 75.4 rating, took only 1 sack. Note the yardage was inflated by heavy garbage-time volume (53 attempts) after Green Bay fell behind 27 unanswered points — treat this as a middling real performance dressed up by a big raw stat line (RotoWire/CBS Sports, Heavy.com, 9/24-25). Team-level concern: RT Zach Bako-Bewele's season-ending torn patellar tendon remains an O-line issue worth monitoring for Love's protection going forward.

roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.reason: Led the NFL with 323 carries in 2025 — 1,585 yds, 18 rush TD, RB1 overall. New contract extension cements him as the Colts' offensive centerpiece; staff may trim touches slightly to manage wear, but role security is elite. New extension (announced Aug 6, 2026): 2 years, $44M ($39M guaranteed, up to $47M) — the 2nd-highest-paid RB in the NFL by AAV.

roster.name: J.K. Dobbins
roster.reason: CLEARED the hip issue that cost him the second half of Denver's Week 2 win over Jacksonville and started Sunday's Week 3 game vs. the Rams as the clear lead-carry back. NEW: production hasn't matched the volume — led Denver with 17 carries but managed just 49 yards (plus a 4-yard catch) in Sunday's 30-26 win, and is still without a rushing TD through 3 games (35 carries total, no other Broncos RB over 10) (CBS Sports, RotoWire, NBC Sports, 9/27-28).
