Still the clear lead back on paper, but the inefficient workload — combined with RJ Harvey's return to health as the passing-down option — is worth monitoring heading into Week 4. Week 6 TNF (10/15): scored a rushing TD in Denver's 17-14 OT win over Seattle (17 carries, 41 yards). RJ Harvey led the backfield in receiving work and also scored (see his note) -- still a muddled two-man committee with no single back pulling away.

roster.name: Matthew Golden
roster.reason: The early skepticism has faded fast — Golden has been a real Week 2-3 riser: 9.8 fantasy pts in Week 2, then 5 catches for 100 yards and a TD (15-yard grab, plus a 45-yard catch that set up Green Bay's first score) in Thursday night's Week 3 loss at Atlanta, playing like a true No. 1 WR and called the Packers' "lone bright spot" by multiple outlets (RotoWire/CBS/Yahoo, 9/24). 253 receiving yards and 15 catches through 3 games — trending toward a real featured role opposite Watson rather than the depth-chart battle framing from earlier in camp.

roster.name: DeVonta Smith
roster.reason: Played through the hamstring that had kept him out of practice in Week 1 and delivered a huge Week 2 (10 catches, 117 yards, 1 TD in the 24-20 win over Tennessee) — Philly's unquestioned WR1 now that A.J. Brown is in New England. CLEARED and CONFIRMED: practiced in full Saturday, carried no injury designation into Monday night's Week 3 game at Chicago, and played through it cleanly — the hamstring flare-up is fully resolved. Led the Eagles with 6 catches (on 8 targets) for 65 yards, including the offense's longest play (a 30-yard grab), in a 27-7 loss where Jalen Hurts and the passing game otherwise struggled (NBC Sports, RotoWire, 9/28). With Smith healthy, newly-acquired Dontayvion Wicks (traded from Green Bay in April) remains in a normal WR2 complementary role rather than a lead-receiver fill-in. NEW (9/30): DNP Wednesday with the same hamstring that flared up in Week 3 — following the identical weekly pattern (DNP Thu/Wed, limited Fri, full Sat) that preceded him playing through it each of the last two weeks. Beat writers (NBC Sports Philadelphia, Bleeding Green Nation) expect the Eagles to manage him the same way again ahead of the Week 4 game vs. the Rams; no new setback or revised severity reported (9/30). WORSENED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Rams after missing three straight practices with the same hamstring that has now flared up repeatedly -- a real step back from the DNP/limited/full weekly pattern that let him play through it the prior two weeks. Bumping tag from Health Watch to Injury given the back-to-back-week recurrence; no multi-week timeline reported yet. Dontayvion Wicks is in line for a bigger complementary role Sunday with Smith out (National Football Post, ESPN, NBC Sports Philadelphia, 10/1-3). NO IMPROVEMENT (10/7): DNP again in Wednesday's practice ahead of the Eagles' Week 5 game vs. Jacksonville, played in London (10/11) as part of the NFL's international series. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo called him "questionable at very best" and floated a possible multi-game absence -- that specific framing hasn't been independently corroborated elsewhere, so treat the multi-game risk as a single-source flag rather than confirmed, but the hamstring clearly has not turned the corner after three recurrences. Keeping the standard Injury tier since no concrete number of weeks has been confirmed; Dontayvion Wicks again projects for a bigger role if Smith sits. STILL OUT (10/8): DNP again in Thursday's practice, continuing the recurring hamstring issue -- trending toward missing a third straight game Sunday vs. Jacksonville in London. Dontayvion Wicks (himself now dealing with a hamstring issue, see his note) and the receiving corps remain thin behind him (Bleeding Green Nation, PhillyVoice, 10/8). WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/10): officially flipped from QUESTIONABLE to OUT for Sunday's Week 5 game in London vs. Jacksonville -- a third straight missed game with the recurring hamstring strain, which never progressed past DNP/limited across this week's practices (NBC Sports Philadelphia, PhillyVoice, Bleeding Green Nation reporting through 10/8-9, one unconfirmed single-source report even floated a multi-game absence). Dontayvion Wicks (now himself cleared, see his note) projects for a season-high role in his absence. Week 5 final (10/11): missed a third straight game as Jacksonville beat Philadelphia 19-17 in London on a last-second 57-yard Cam Little field goal after Philly had taken a late 17-16 lead -- Eagles fell to 2-3. Dallas Goedert (6 catches, 38 yards) and Dameon Pierce (making his 2026 debut after being activated 10/7) picked up extra work with Smith, Saquon Barkley, and Tank Bigsby all out. UPDATE (10/14): cautiously positive signal for Week 6 vs. Carolina (Sun 10/18, home) -- RotoBaller (citing NFL Network's Mike Garafolo, 10/12) reports Smith "has a chance to return." No Wednesday practice report confirming actual participation level had posted as of this update; keeping the standard Injury tier pending that confirmation rather than upgrading to Health Watch prematurely. SETBACK (10/14): did NOT practice Wednesday, and his designation reportedly expanded to "hamstring/toe" (Heavy.com/Yahoo) -- a real step back from HC Nick Sirianni's Monday "hopeful" framing for Sunday's game vs. Carolina. Keeping the standard Injury tier; recheck Friday's final practice report before trusting the "chance to return" framing from earlier in the week. UPDATE (10/16): progressed from a Wednesday DNP to a limited Thursday practice (10/14-10/15), with the designation reportedly covering both hamstring and toe. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo said Smith has "a shot" to play Sunday vs. Carolina (10/18) -- a real step up from this week's earlier setback, though not yet a confirmed green light. CLEARED (10/18): no game status on the final Week 6 injury report vs. Carolina -- the recurring hamstring (plus a newly-reported toe issue) progressed from a Wednesday DNP to limited Thursday to a full practice Friday (Philadelphia Inquirer, RotoBaller/Garafolo). First game available since Week 3. Smith himself said availability was 'up to the doctors' earlier in the week, so treat this as cleared-but-worth-watching-usage in his first game back rather than a clean bill of health. Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch. QB Jalen Hurts remains out (blood clot), with Tanner McKee starting.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.reason: 2025: 126 rec/1,239 yds/11 TD, led all TEs in target share (25.4%). New Cardinals staff invested heavily in the run game (drafted RB Jeremiyah Love 3rd overall, signed Tyler Allgeier) — his 683-route workload likely won't repeat. Still a top-2 TE, just not a top-15-overall ceiling. NEW (9/30): suffered a concussion on a head-on hit from Lions S Brian Branch in Week 3 (3 catches, 25 yards before exiting) and is ruled OUT for Week 4 vs. Washington (Bleacher Report, ClutchPoints, AZCardinals.com, 9/28). Worth tracking as a protocol case — no set return timeline until he clears the steps, but concussions can also clear quickly. He'd been out-targeting Marvin Harrison Jr. 23-4 through two games, so his absence is a meaningful hit to Arizona's passing-game volume for at least this week. UPDATE (10/5): remains in the concussion protocol after the head-on hit from Lions S Brian Branch in Week 3; did not practice that week and was ruled out for Arizona's following game, with Elijah Higgins, Tip Reiman and Travis Vokolek filling in at TE (azcardinals.com, CBS Sports, NBC Sports). Note: several injury-report sources mislabeled that game as "vs. Washington"; Arizona's actual Week 4 opponent was the New York Giants -- an indexing error in those sources, not a real schedule conflict. Team-sourced reporting says he "should have a good chance to clear protocol in time for Week 5" -- a short, routine absence. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Short-Term Injury given that fairly firm timeline.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.reason: The camp toe sprain didn't cost him any time — played through it in the Week 1 opener vs. Cincinnati, catching 5 of 6 targets for 63 yards. Locked in as Tampa Bay's WR1 with Mike Evans gone to SF. UPDATE (10/13-14): has fully taken over as Tampa Bay's clear top receiver amid the WR room's injuries -- 25 catches, 445 yards and 5 TD through 5 games. With Chris Godwin (fibula) and Bucky Irving (foot/shoulder) both ruled out for Week 6 vs. San Francisco (see their notes), Egbuka's target share should only grow further this week.

roster.name: Browns D/ST
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Tyler Loop
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Rome Odunze
roster.reason: Played through the calf injury that had him Questionable into the weekend and finished with 2 catches for 52 yards on 3 targets as Chicago routed Carolina 59-37 — light volume, but more a function of the blowout game script than the calf, which held up with no setback reported. Remains Caleb Williams' clear WR1 with DJ Moore traded away; expect target share to normalize now that the calf is no longer a question. UPDATE: with Caleb Williams (hamstring) and backup Tyson Bagent both out, journeyman Case Keenum authored a 247-yard, 2-TD Week 3 Monday Night upset of Philadelphia (27-7, 9/28). Chicago's passing offense is now running through a stopgap QB for the next several weeks — worth tempering expectations on Odunze's target efficiency until Williams returns, even though the WR1 role itself remains his.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.reason: Rough 2025: a 3-game suspension to start the year, only 17.4% target share (Jefferson had 28.2%), finished WR43. QB upgrade to Kyler Murray helps, but MIN also signed WR Jauan Jennings — adds competition rather than clearing it. Profiles more WR3/bench right now. NEW (10/8): sidelined at Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury and carries a QUESTIONABLE tag (per the Vikings' own injury report) into Sunday's Week 5 game at New Orleans -- though one outlet flagged a conflicting Minnesota listing, so confirm Friday's final designation. First hamstring concern of the season, and it comes while he's already fighting for target share behind Justin Jefferson (himself limited this week with an ankle issue). CONFIRMED (10/12): inactive for Sunday's Week 5 game at New Orleans with the hamstring injury after a true game-time call (only two limited practices during the week). Minnesota (5-0) now has its Week 6 bye, so Addison's next chance to play isn't until Oct. 25 vs. the Colts -- effectively a two-week break to heal rather than a sign of a longer-term issue. Justin Jefferson (see his note) returned and played a full workload in the same game. NON-EVENT (10/14): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip is a procedural reset, not real news -- Minnesota is on its Week 6 bye (confirmed via Vikings.com/FoxSports league bye list), so there's no game for Addison to be questionable for. He remains on track to return Week 7 (Oct 25) vs. the Colts per last week's report; no new hamstring details surfaced.

roster.name: Xavier Worthy
roster.reason: A distant WR2 behind Rice — only a 16.1% target share and WR60 finish in 2025; deep-threat/boom upside but not a reliable weekly starter. Dislocated his right shoulder and suffered a torn labrum colliding with Travis Kelce in the Week 1 win over Denver, missing most of that game, but avoided season-ending surgery per HC Andy Reid. Played through the shoulder in Week 2 vs. Indianapolis (9/20): 5 catches on 7 targets for 25 yards in the 33-30 OT win — back on the field as hoped, but modest per-target efficiency (5.0 YPT) so far post-labrum injury; worth tracking snap/route share before trusting a big workload.

roster.name: Rico Dowdle
roster.reason: Suffered a toe injury on a pass-blocking/fumble-recovery rep in the 2nd quarter of a loss to New England, was carted to the locker room, returned for a few series coming out of halftime, then appeared to re-aggravate it and was ruled out for good; finished with 9 total touches for 44 yards. CONFIRMED: officially ruled OUT for Week 3 vs. Cincinnati after DNP all week, despite the issue being described as "day-to-day" (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/25-26). NEW: still hasn't practiced — listed DNP again on Monday (9/28) — which is a real concern given Pittsburgh is on a short week for Thursday Night Football at Cleveland in Week 4. He'll need a near-miracle practice ramp-up to play Thursday and enters the week very much questionable (NBC Sports, 9/28). Jaylen Warren is set for another game of workhorse usage should Dowdle sit again. UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE ahead of Thursday's short-week game at Cleveland, but beat coverage through Tuesday's practice (the last fully-indexed report at research time) still had him a full DNP and in a walking boot, with Steelers Depot and Still Curtain both explicitly framing him as "trending towards missing a second-straight game" and calling Wednesday's practice report the real swing session. Treat the QUESTIONABLE tag cautiously — it may reflect today's (Wed 9/30) official report showing him as at least limited, but the stronger prior signal through Tuesday still points toward sitting out. Jaylen Warren (20 touches Week 3) remains the clear lead back regardless of Dowdle's exact designation. UPDATE (9/30): officially ruled OUT for Thursday Night Football's Week 4 short-week game at Cleveland — still hasn't practiced since the Week 2 toe injury (DNP every session, previously spotted in a walking boot). No surgery or exact "X weeks" timeline has been given, but Pittsburgh's mini-bye before Week 5 (not playing again until Oct. 11 vs. Indianapolis) is the beat-writer-flagged likely return window (NBC Sports, RotoWire, Yahoo Sports/AP, 9/29-30). Jaylen Warren continues as the clear workhorse (~90% snap share) in his absence. CONFIRMED, tag revised from Injury to Short-Term Injury: Dowdle (toe) was a full DNP all week and was ruled OUT for Thursday Night Football's Week 4 game at Cleveland, which Pittsburgh lost 27-24 on a last-second field goal — his second straight missed game. NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported afterward that Dowdle has a "pretty good chance" to return for Week 5 vs. Indianapolis on Oct. 11, giving this a fairly firm ~1-week runway rather than open-ended (Steelers Depot, Yahoo Sports, 10/1-2). Jaylen Warren again handled the workhorse Thursday (17 carries/93 yards, 3 catches/33 yards) and remains the clear starter in Dowdle's absence. ON TRACK (10/7): QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Colts, consistent with the ~1-week return runway Rapoport reported last week. Beat reporting describes him as "making progress" this week, though the team hasn't yet confirmed his availability. Keeping Short-Term Injury given the still-intact short timeline; Jaylen Warren remains the starter regardless of Dowdle's exact Sunday role. REVISED FROM SHORT-TERM TO STANDARD INJURY (10/12): remained out for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Colts despite returning to limited practice Wed/Thu and HC Mike McCarthy calling him 'making progress' -- our roster tracker confirms OUT, and Jaylen Warren again carried the workload, exploding for 188 total yards and two long touchdowns (an 80-yard catch, a 50-yard run) in Pittsburgh's 34-22 win. This is now three straight missed games since the Week 2 toe injury, well past the ~1-week runway Ian Rapoport reported two weeks ago -- revising the tag from Short-Term Injury to the standard Injury tier since that short timeline did not hold up and no new firm return date has been reported. Warren remains the clear starter regardless of Dowdle's eventual role. REVISED BACK TO SHORT-TERM (10/14): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip tracks real news -- Steelers OC Brian Angelichio said Monday (10/12) he expects Dowdle back for Week 6's game at Tampa Bay, per The Athletic's Mike DeFabo. Re-upgrading the tag to Short-Term Injury given the now-firm 1-week-away target, after it had been bumped to the standard Injury tier two weeks ago when the original ~1-week Rapoport estimate didn't hold. HC Mike McCarthy still called Jaylen Warren "our featured player right now," signaling Dowdle likely returns to a shared role rather than instantly reclaiming the full workhorse job. UPDATE (10/15): no fresh Wednesday/Thursday Week 6 practice-report confirmation found yet beyond OC Brian Angelichio's Monday (10/12) comments expecting him back -- recheck Friday's final injury report before fully trusting the short-term return target. CORRECTION (10/16): the injury is a dislocated toe, not the quad/hamstring framing earlier notes used -- Dowdle has missed three straight games (Weeks 3-5) with it. HC Mike McCarthy said after the Week 5 win over Indianapolis that Dowdle was "close" and he's hopeful for a Week 6 return vs. Tampa Bay (10/18), with an expectation he practices this week; no Wednesday/Thursday practice report could be confirmed via search as of this update. Jaylen Warren remains Pittsburgh's clear lead back, with McCarthy floating a "one-two punch" once Dowdle is back -- keeping the Short-Term Injury tag given the team's stated Week 6 target. CLEARED (10/17): logged a full practice Thursday -- the first full practice participation since the Week 2 toe injury -- and carries no designation into Sunday's Week 6 game at Tampa Bay, ending a three-game absence (Weeks 3-5). Softening tag from Short-Term Injury to Health Watch now that he's actually cleared. HC Mike McCarthy has signaled a "one-two punch" split with Jaylen Warren rather than Dowdle instantly reclaiming the full workhorse job, so expect a shared role in his first game back. NEW DESIGNATION (10/18): flipped from yesterday's clean clearance back to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 6 game at Tampa Bay -- but this reads as a standard return-from-injury designation rather than a new setback: he was a full practice participant Thursday AND Friday (The Fantasy Footballers), and Steelers OC Brian Angelichio had already said Monday he expected Dowdle back this week. HC Mike McCarthy has indicated Jaylen Warren keeps the larger role of the two even once Dowdle is active, so this isn't a 50/50 split. Keeping Health Watch given the clean back-to-back full practices. WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): played a complementary role in his first game back from the toe injury, as expected -- 7 carries for 40 yards plus 3 catches for 9 yards in Pittsburgh's 26-19 OT win over Tampa Bay, behind Jaylen Warren's 14 carries for 50 yards and 2 catches for 28 yards (Yahoo Sports box score, 10/18). No re-aggravation reported. Keeping Health Watch -- this confirms HC Mike McCarthy's stated "one-two punch" plan rather than Dowdle reclaiming the full workhorse role.

roster.name: Emanuel Wilson
roster.reason: Signed a one-year deal with Seattle in March after three seasons in Green Bay; added to this fantasy roster off waivers this week. Part of a genuine four-man rotation in Seattle's backfield (George Holani, Jadarian Price, Wilson, with Zach Charbonnet still out on PUP/ACL recovery) rather than a clear role -- stands to see a bump in work with Price now ruled OUT for Week 4 (chest) alongside Holani. ROLE CHANGE (10/16): took over as Seattle's clear every-down back in Thursday night's 17-14 OT loss at Denver (10/15) with both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price out -- a real workload shift, not just a one-game spot start, since both remain sidelined (see their notes). Upgrading tag from Committee to Job Secured while that depth-chart math holds.

roster.name: Jalen Hurts
roster.reason: No 2026 camp or preseason injury reports; practiced fully through August, including joint sessions vs NE. Standard top-5 fantasy QB profile — the rushing floor keeps him there even on off passing days. RULED OUT (10/15-16): a precautionary ultrasound taken in London ahead of the Jacksonville trip found a superficial blood clot in his calf; team doctors initially cleared him to play, but a Wednesday (10/14) follow-up scan showed the clot had moved, and the Eagles ruled him out for Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. Carolina (6abc, Fox affiliates, NBC Sports, 10/15). NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports he is "out indefinitely" with no return timeline set as the team determines a treatment plan -- Tanner McKee will start in his place. Tagging the standard Injury tier given the genuinely open-ended, pending-further-evaluation nature of a blood clot rather than a normal soft-tissue strain; this is a real health situation to keep close tabs on, not a routine week-to-week designation. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith (both hamstring) are also in doubt for the same game -- see their notes. CONFIRMED (10/19): the roster tracker now lists Hurts on injured reserve for the calf blood clot (no independent beat-reporter confirmation of the exact IR transaction was found via search, but the practical effect -- out well beyond this week -- matches reporting). Backup Tanner McKee started Sunday's 25-14 loss to Carolina, Philadelphia's fourth straight defeat (now 2-4) and its first 4-game skid since 2020 -- McKee went 26-of-45 for 215 yards and a TD to DeVonta Smith (19-yard score with 10:42 left) before the comeback stalled; the Eagles also signed QB Joe Milton III off Dallas' practice squad for added depth. No return timeline has been reported yet. ESCALATED, OUT FOR SEASON (10/19): the calf clot has progressed -- follow-up testing found a deep vein thrombosis (DVT) with additional blood clots that traveled to both lungs (bilateral pulmonary emboli), not just the original superficial calf clot found in London. Agent Nicole Lynn and the team say he is "clinically stable" with "no significant functional limitations," but he cannot play while on blood thinners -- treatment is expected to sideline him roughly 3+ months, ruling him out for the rest of 2026 (NFL Network, ESPN, Boston Globe, Fox29, 10/19). Prognosis is described as very good with no expected long-term effects, and he's expected to stay around the team as captain. Tanner McKee remains Philadelphia's starter for the foreseeable future. Upgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Long-Term Injury given the confirmed season-ending timeline.

roster.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
roster.reason: Signed a 4-yr/$52M deal with hometown New Orleans as a free agent and is listed as the starter, but Alvin Kamara remains on the roster and real committee risk has materialized early. Was healthy and productive early in Week 3 (led all Saints rushers with 13 carries for 57 yards, plus 2 catches for 13 yards) before pulling up with a hamstring injury after a 16-yard run in the 3rd quarter of Sunday's loss to the Raiders — did not return (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 9/27). NEW: officially OUT — HC Kellen Moore said Monday (9/28) Etienne will have "time lost" with the hamstring, with no specific return timeline set and an IR stint still possible depending on further evaluation (RotoWire, NBC Sports, FantasyPros, 9/28). Kamara is the direct backfield beneficiary given the committee usage already in place; treat Etienne as a bench stash until more clarity emerges. CONFIRMED, tag revised from Injury to Long-Term Injury: New Orleans officially placed Etienne on injured reserve (hamstring) on 10/1. HC Kellen Moore said no surgery is needed, but the recovery is expected to run at least 4 weeks — the team's Week 8 bye makes his next realistic game action Sunday, Nov. 8 at Cleveland (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, FantasyPros, 10/1). Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller are the direct backfield beneficiaries in the meantime; treat Etienne as a stash-only dynasty/IR piece for roughly a month.

roster.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
roster.reason: Two straight down seasons (sub-12 PPG each) with the worst YPRR marks of his career and a shrinking red-zone role. Back in SF on a 1-year “reunion” deal — real chance 2026 is his last fantasy-relevant year. NEW (10/13): strained his hamstring late in the 3rd quarter of Sunday's 32-29 Week 5 win over Seattle, fumbling on the play before being ruled out for the rest of the game (CBS Sports, FantasyPros, 10/11-12). HC Kyle Shanahan said Monday he's expected to miss "at least a couple of weeks" and is not currently being considered for IR (NBC Sports, SF Chronicle, Yardbarker, 10/12). He has a history of this hamstring flaring up and recurring on return per Shanahan's own comments about 2025, so treat the couple-week estimate as the real risk, not a floor. Picking Short-Term Injury given the reported ~2-week timeline; Mike Evans (see his note) is SF's clear top option in the meantime. REVISED FROM SHORT-TERM TO STANDARD INJURY (10/14): HC Kyle Shanahan's full Monday (10/12) comments walk back last cycle's ~2-week framing -- he said Samuel is "going to miss some time," specifically "at least the next couple of games and likely a bit longer," which is a real extension beyond the firm 1-2-week Short-Term framing (ABC7/ABC30, NBC Sports Bay Area, ClutchPoints via Ian Rapoport). Not on IR as of this update. Expect him to miss SF's Week 6 game at Washington (MNF 10/19) and likely Week 7 at Atlanta too, with San Francisco's Week 8 bye potentially extending the absence further before a real return estimate firms up. Mike Evans (7/113/1 in the Week 5 win over Seattle) and Brandin Cooks/Jacob Cowing are the clear beneficiaries in the meantime.

roster.name: Alec Pierce
roster.reason: CONFIRMED: officially placed on injured reserve Wednesday 9/23 (HC Shane Steichen) after aggravating his surgically-repaired left heel late in Sunday's loss at Kansas City — couldn't put weight on it and left on crutches in a boot. ESPN sources report Pierce plans to rehab rather than undergo a second surgery; he and the club are "hopeful" for roughly a 4-6 week absence after a second opinion, with return targeted for midseason — IR guarantees a minimum 4 games missed, and the exact timeline remains rehab-dependent/unconfirmed. Colts signed veteran WR Darius Slayton (agreed to terms 9/22) as a direct replacement. Pierce had led the NFL in yards/catch among qualified WRs the past two seasons; expect targets to spread toward Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, Slayton, and TE Tyler Warren.

roster.name: Matthew Stafford
roster.reason: Reigning NFL MVP — led the league in passing yards (4,707) and TD passes (46) in 2025; real regression risk since his 2025 leaned on unsustainable red-zone efficiency. Went 22-of-31 for 327 yards, 4 TD, 1 INT in Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants; his 426th career passing touchdown moved him past Philip Rivers into 6th all-time (NFL.com, Yahoo Sports).

roster.name: Ollie Gordon II
roster.reason: Stepped in after De'Von Achane tore his ACL in Week 3 vs. Kansas City (season-ending) — 17 carries for 41 yards and a TD, plus 3 catches for 14 yards on 3 targets in relief (Yahoo Sports, Bleacher Report, 9/27-28). Miami's backfield is now a committee with Jaylen Wright (trending back healthy for Week 4) — analysts project roughly a 60/40 split favoring Wright, with Gordon getting goal-line/early-down work. One of the top Week 4 waiver adds league-wide given the timeshare upside (SI/OnSI, Yahoo Sports). Week 4 final (10/4): dominated the Miami backfield in the 15-10 loss to Minnesota -- 9 carries for 100 yards and a TD plus 2 targets on 22 snaps, clearly outplaying Jaylen Wright (5 carries/7 yards, 12 snaps -- see his note). With De'Von Achane out for the season, Gordon now looks like the favorite for lead-back work in Miami's backfield heading into Week 5, not just a 50/50 committee piece (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Heavy.com, 10/4).

roster.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
roster.reason: Was co-starter on paper with Jordan Mason — but Mason's Sept 16 thumb-fracture surgery and IR placement (out a mandatory 4 games minimum, through at least Week 5) handed Jones the clear lead-back role in Minnesota for at least a month. Depth behind him is thin (DeeJay Dallas up from the practice squad). CLEARED: the knee tweak from Minnesota's Week 2 win was removed from the injury report after a full Friday practice — Jones carries no designation into Sunday's game vs. Tampa Bay (NBC Sports, FantasyPros, Vikings.com, 9/25).

roster.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
roster.reason: Opened 2026 with 8 catches for 122 yds and the game-winning 45-yard TD (41 YAC) on 4th-and-1 in the 4th quarter of Seattle's 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game win over New England — early sign the regression fears may be overblown. Backup QB Drew Lock (18/22, 187 yds) finished that game after starter Sam Darnold left with a hip injury on the opening drive; Darnold's Thursday (Sept 10) MRI showed no major structural damage ("dodged a bullet," per the team), but he's still expected to miss Week 2 at Arizona with Lock confirmed as the Week 2 starter — worth tracking since it affects who's throwing Smith-Njigba the ball. Led all NFL WRs with 1,793 yds/10 TD in 2025 and won Offensive Player of the Year; now the highest-paid WR in history (4yr/$168.6M). Top-5 overall fantasy asset — the question is regression off a historic year, not upside. NEW (10/14): picked up a minor ankle injury on a 16-yard lateral run in the second quarter of Seattle's 32-29 Week 5 loss at San Francisco (10/11) -- it didn't meaningfully slow him down; he still topped 100 receiving yards for the 5th straight game, pushing his NFL-leading total to 583 yards and 7 TDs through 5 games. The Seattle Times' Bob Condotta reported he was a limited practice participant Monday (10/12) ahead of a short week (Seahawks play Thursday 10/15 at Denver), with reporting suggesting he should play Thursday without real restriction. Tagging Health Watch given the minor/day-to-day framing -- not a real absence risk at this point. UPDATE (10/15): no official designation beyond Monday's (10/12) limited-practice estimate has surfaced ahead of tonight's Thursday Night Football game at Denver -- RotoBaller's analysis expects him to play without real restriction on the short week, but that's analyst opinion, not a confirmed team designation. Check Seattle's pregame inactive list for final confirmation. RESOLVED (10/16): the minor ankle tweak was a non-issue -- played every snap of Thursday night's 17-14 OT loss at Denver (10/15) with no in-game setback, posting 12 catches on 16 targets for 134 yards (season now 49 catches, 717 yards, 7 TD through 6 games). Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; today's ACTIVE flip reflects a clean bill of health, not a new designation.

roster.name: George Pickens
roster.reason: Franchise-tagged ($27.3M) after a 2025 breakout — 93 rec/1,429 yds/9 TD, top-6 PPR WR despite sharing targets with Lamb.

roster.name: Tucker Kraft
roster.reason: Confirmed "full-go" for Week 1 vs. Minnesota after full-contact clearance and full participation in a joint practice vs. Arizona — a clean upgrade off the torn ACL, though still his first year back.

roster.name: Jameson Williams
roster.reason: Coming off a big season but genuinely boom/bust (WR41 pace Weeks 1-10 vs. WR13 pace Weeks 11-18) — more of a WR3 with real week-winning upside than a lineup lock.

roster.name: Eddy Pineiro
roster.reason: San Francisco's starting kicker behind a run-heavy, red-zone-efficient offense under Kyle Shanahan. Missed all three practices last week (Wed-Fri, 9/16-18) sick, drawing a Questionable tag for Week 2 vs. Miami with the 49ers carrying no other kicker on the roster or practice squad. The 49ers worked out veteran kickers Greg Joseph and Younghoe Koo Saturday (9/19) but signed neither — a strong signal the team expects Pineiro to be active and play Sunday (NBC Sports Bay Area, 9/19-20).

roster.name: Rashee Rice
roster.reason: Made his long-awaited return from suspension and offseason knee cleanup in Kansas City's Week 1 win over Denver, playing through it cleanly — 2 catches for 19 yards and a TD on just 2 targets as the offense eased him back in behind Kenneth Walker III's big rushing day. UPDATE: usage has climbed hard each week since — 2 targets (Wk1) to 6 (Wk2) to 9 in Week 3 (7 catches, 88 yards) in a 49-play win over Miami where Mahomes only threw 24 times — a clear signal Rice is rounding back into the true WR1 role (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, RotoWire, 9/27). NEW INJURY, CONFIRMED (10/4-5): suffered a non-contact hamstring injury early in Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Raiders -- pulled up lame grabbing his leg after a short catch, was downgraded to doubtful, and did not return (SI, KCTV5, NBC Sports, ClutchPoints, AtoZ Sports, DraftKings Network, 10/4). IMPORTANT: search results for Rice are heavily cross-contaminated with his unrelated, much more serious September 2024 knee injury (LCL/hamstring-tendon surgery after a Mahomes collision, which was feared to be an ACL tear at the time) -- that 2024 story is NOT this year's news and should not be merged with it. This week's hamstring strain is a new, separate, and so far lower-severity issue. Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier pending a firmer timeline; keeping Elite Starter since the role/talent profile is unaffected when he's healthy. UPDATE (10/16): a second straight full DNP Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the hamstring/knee injury; HC Andy Reid declined to commit to him practicing the rest of the week or playing Sunday, saying of hamstrings, "it could be a week, it could be two weeks, you don't know" (Arrowhead Pride). Trending toward sitting out Sunday's Week 6 game vs. the Chargers (10/18) rather than a continuation of last week's progress. CONFIRMED (10/18): HC Andy Reid ruled Rice out for Sunday's Week 6 game vs. the Chargers after a third straight full DNP week with the hamstring strain suffered in Week 4 vs. the Raiders. Reid declined a firm number but said hamstring injuries typically cost players '1 to 2 weeks' and called him 'a pretty fast healer,' with Kansas City's primetime Week 7 game at Seattle floated as a realistic return target (Field Level Media, KCTV5, 10/16). Revising tag from the standard Injury tier to Short-Term Injury given that fairly firm 1-2 week framing. UPDATE (10/22): did not practice Wednesday (10/21) with the hamstring -- HC Andy Reid confirmed the sit-out but said Rice "is improving," without predicting whether that's enough for Sunday Night Football at Seattle (10/25, 8:20pm ET, NBC). He needs to mix into practice Thursday/Friday for a real shot to play; keeping the Short-Term Injury tier given last week's firm 1-2-week framing from Reid is still the operative timeline.

roster.name: Quinshon Judkins
roster.reason: Moved to the unambiguous RB1 spot on Cleveland's depth chart, ahead of Sampson and Sanders. Battling a minor "nagging" injury that cost him two camp practices, but coaches aren't concerned — remains Cleveland's clear lead back over Dylan Sampson, Raheim Sanders, and Ahmani Marshall. 2025 2nd-round pick (36th overall, Ohio State), acquired via a Day 1 trade with Jacksonville. Handled 12 of Cleveland's 15 RB carries plus 5 catches (17 touches, 48 total yards) in the Week 2 win over Tampa Bay, confirming him as the clear #1 back even in a tough matchup (CBS Sports, RotoWire). NEW (10/13): picked up a new right ankle "tweak" in Sunday's Week 5 loss to the Jets (10/11); HC Kevin Stefanski called it day-to-day and said he'll "have a chance to play" Week 6 vs. Baltimore (RotoWire, NBC Sports, 10/12). Worth watching closely -- it's the same ankle/fibula area he surgically repaired after a dislocation/fracture last season, which has some beat writers flagging it even though team language is cautiously optimistic (Yahoo Sports/Heavy, Dawg Pound Daily, 10/12). No official Wed/Thu/Fri practice grade confirmed yet -- recheck before Week 6. If he sits, Raheim Sanders would be next in line, though Sanders himself left the same game with a hip injury and his own availability is a wrinkle (ESPN). UPDATE (10/14): did NOT practice Wednesday with the ankle, per NBC Sports/RotoWire -- he was seen in the locker room without the walking boot he'd worn postgame Sunday, a mildly positive visual sign, but no Thursday/Friday practice grade had posted as of this update; his Week 6 call vs. Baltimore still hinges on the rest of the week's practice participation. Correction: the "day-to-day, has a chance to play" comment is attributed by multiple outlets to OC Todd Monken, not HC Kevin Stefanski as previously framed -- flagging since the original Stefanski attribution could not be verified. Separately, backup Raheim Sanders (hip, same Week 5 game) was placed on IR Tuesday (10/13), so he will NOT be available if Judkins sits -- Cleveland signed RB Audric Estime off Minnesota's practice squad as added depth, with Jaleel McLaughlin also in the mix. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty and Wednesday DNP. UPDATE (10/16): did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the ankle, though he was seen without his walking boot. Beat writers still frame him as "day-to-day" without a firm ruling, but Cleveland signed RB Audric Estime off Minnesota's practice squad this week as insurance, and Dawg Pound Daily reports the trend points toward Jaleel McLaughlin as Sunday's lead back vs. Baltimore (10/18) if Judkins sits. CONFIRMED OUT (10/18): did not play in Cleveland's 13-10 win over Baltimore -- tested in pregame warmups on the ankle he tweaked in Week 5 (the same surgically-repaired ankle/fibula from last season) before being held out (USA Today/Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 10/18). Jaleel McLaughlin (9 carries/41 yards) and Audric Estime (9 carries/19 yards, including the game-tying 2-yard TD) split the backfield work in his absence. No firm return timeline has been reported yet for Week 7; recheck Wednesday's practice report. Keeping the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty and the injury's proximity to last year's more serious ankle/fibula fracture. UPDATE (10/22): upgraded to a LIMITED practice participant Wednesday (10/21) -- a real step up from last week's DNP -- with Dylan Sampson also absent from Cleveland's non-participant list, per the Akron Beacon Journal's Chris Easterling. OC Todd Monken said he's "optimistic" about Judkins' availability for Sunday's Week 7 game vs. Tennessee but stopped short of guaranteeing it. Trending positive; keeping the standard Injury tier until he logs a full practice or a firmer designation posts.

roster.name: Jeremiyah Love
roster.reason: Played through the high-ankle sprain that had him Questionable and delivered his first extended workload: 11 carries for 41 yards and a TD plus 2 catches for 9 yards in Sunday's game vs. the Chargers. No setback reported after the game — the ankle no longer looks like a Week 2 concern with a full game under his belt. NEW (10/5-6): tweaked his OTHER ankle (not the preseason high-ankle sprain) late in Sunday's Week 4 loss at the Giants, finishing with 14 carries for 63 yards plus a target that went for -8 yards. HC Mike LaFleur described it Monday as "a management-type thing... he tweaks it and then he feels fine," and Love himself called this shaping up as the "longest year" of his career (NBC Sports, RotoBaller, Heavy.com, SI.com, 10/4-5). No practice report yet as of today (Week 5 practice starts Wednesday); downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending Wednesday's designation. CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Detroit -- HC Mike LaFleur had already downplayed the tweaked ankle as a "management-type thing," and that held up with no setback reported heading into Friday. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. NEW, SEPARATE INJURY (10/16): dealing with a different left-ankle issue (not the preseason high-ankle sprain or the earlier "management-type" tweak) -- did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (10/14-10/15). HC Mike LaFleur's language shifted more cautious, saying the staff wants to "get this ankle right and do it the right way," which beat writers (Arizona Sports, Yahoo Sports) read as a real threat to his Sunday availability vs. the Rams (10/18) even though Love reportedly wants to play through it. Tyler Allgeier would start if he sits. Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier given the genuine uncertainty. CONFIRMED (10/18): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. the Rams -- HC Jonathan Gannon's staff (via AP) confirmed the lingering left ankle injury (aggravated in Week 4 at the Giants) kept him out of practice all week. No IR conversations have taken place per the team, so this reads as a short-term absence rather than a long one. Tyler Allgeier (newly added to this roster, see his note) and Bam Knight are set to handle Arizona's backfield work Sunday. Keeping the standard Injury tier given the no-IR signal, though recheck next week for an actual return target. UPDATE (10/22): did not practice Wednesday (10/21) with the ankle injury -- HC Mike LaFleur said rest is "vital" for him right now, and NBC Sports frames the DNP as putting him "on the wrong side of questionable" for Sunday's Week 7 game vs. Denver. He has a chance to return to practice Thursday/Friday; if he sits, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would again handle Arizona's backfield work. Keeping the standard Injury tier pending the rest of the week's reports.

roster.name: RJ Harvey
roster.reason: CLEARED off the hamstring that cost him Week 2: returned to action in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Rams (30-26), tying for the team lead in targets — 2 carries for 6 yards plus 6 catches on 7 targets for 41 yards (CBS Sports, 9/27). NEW: was evaluated for a concussion in the second half of Sunday's game, but cleared and stayed in — logged just one touch afterward, more a game-flow note than a lingering health concern, though worth a light watch into Week 4. J.K. Dobbins led Denver's backfield in carries Sunday (17 att/49 yds, still without a rushing TD this year) but Harvey's role as the clear passing-down/receiving back is intact; Jonah Coleman remains on IR (high ankle sprain, out at least through Week 6). Week 6 TNF (10/15): scored his first rushing TD of the season (1-yard) in Denver's 17-14 OT win over Seattle, finishing with 6 carries for 25 yards plus 3 catches on 4 targets for 31 yards -- led Denver in receiving. J.K. Dobbins also scored on the ground (see his note); Denver's backfield split continues with no clear lead-back resolution.

roster.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
roster.reason: Led the Browns in receiving as a rookie (72/731/6); with Njoku gone he's the unquestioned TE1 under new OC Todd Monken, who developed Andrews and Likely.

roster.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: TreVeyon Henderson
roster.reason: Missed the Week 1 loss to Seattle (ruled out Sept 8) after not practicing all week with an ankle injury; Rhamondre Stevenson started in his place. Returned to practice Sept 14 and was a full participant that week, officially cleared to Active for Week 2. UPDATE (9/30): clearly took over New England's lead-back role in Week 3's 35-6 loss at Jacksonville — 8 carries for 23 yards plus a target, compared to just 1 carry for Stevenson. Small sample in a blowout script, but the snap/touch distribution points to Henderson as the ascending back; worth tracking whether it holds up in a more competitive game script (RotoWire, dknetwork, 9/27-28). NEW (10/13): suffered a new ankle injury in New England's 45-17 Week 5 win over Las Vegas (10/11) -- first questionable to return, then ruled out, finishing with just 4 carries for 22 yards and 1 catch for 16 yards. Sent for testing Monday (10/12); HC Mike Vrabel said he'd be evaluated (Patriots Communications, DraftSharks, PatsPulpit, 10/11-12). No official Week 6 designation confirmed yet. With Henderson banged up, Rhamondre Stevenson (see his note) is expected to see the bulk of the carries, a reversal of the recent Henderson-as-lead-back trend, with rookie Corey Kiner as the likely change-of-pace option (Yahoo Sports). WORSENED (10/14): status flipped from QUESTIONABLE to DOUBTFUL for Week 6 (home vs. the Jets, Sun 10/18). HC Mike Vrabel confirmed Henderson got an MRI on the ankle Monday (10/12) and said he'd be evaluated, but no diagnosis or specific return timeline has been reported by Patriots beat writers as of this update -- treat the DOUBTFUL tag as a real escalation given the MRI, even though it's not yet matched by a published diagnosis. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the genuine uncertainty. Rhamondre Stevenson (see his note) is expected to handle the bulk of New England's backfield work if Henderson can't go, with rookie Corey Kiner as change-of-pace. UPDATE (10/14): listed as a LIMITED practice participant Wednesday with the ankle (NBC Sports/RotoWire, CBS Sports, Yahoo) -- a step up from a full DNP, but multiple outlets report the Patriots are expected to officially rule him out Friday for Sunday's game vs. the Jets, though that's not yet guaranteed. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported, following Monday's MRI, that it's a high right ankle sprain, no surgery needed, but likely multiple weeks out -- the first real diagnosis/timeline attached to this injury. UPDATE (10/16): a meaningfully better trend than last week's fear of a multi-week absence -- practiced in a non-contact jersey as a LIMITED participant both Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15), the first real practice reps since Monday's ankle MRI, and was seen running and cutting on video Thursday. SI's Patriots Country and DraftSharks now frame him as a plausible Sunday option vs. the Jets (10/18), matching today's status flip from DOUBTFUL back to QUESTIONABLE -- though a full Friday practice is still needed to shed the tag entirely. PLAYED ON PITCH COUNT (10/18): active and started but clearly managed coming off the ankle sprain -- 7 carries for 31 yards plus 1 catch for 9 yards in the 26-19 win over the Jets, and lost his first fumble of the season in the 3rd quarter (forced by Jets rookie David Bailey), which the Jets converted into points (ESPN, CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 10/18). Rookie Corey Kiner reportedly out-touched him on early downs in one beat writer's count (11 carries/57 yards per a Patriots Notebook recap), suggesting a timeshare while Henderson continues to work back to full speed. Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Health Watch now that he's active and playing, but worth monitoring his snap share closely next week given the apparent load management.

Puka Nacua.name: Puka Nacua
bullets: Missed Monday Night Football vs. the Giants (9/21) with a hip/groin issue and stayed OUT all last week; HC Sean McVay confirmed there's no hernia involved.
CONFIRMED: sat out Week 3's 30-26 loss at Denver (9/27) as expected off the DOUBTFUL tag — his second straight missed game with the groin/hip issue.

UPDATE (9/28-29): McVay said the Rams are "hopeful" Nacua can return for Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia, but has since tempered that to "to be determined" and confirmed Nacua will again be limited in practice this week. The team still views it as a short-term issue and believes he's capable of playing now, just not at full explosiveness — no new setback or structural diagnosis, and surgery/IR remain off the table for now (CBS Sports, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, 9/28-29). Keeping Short-Term Injury tag; Davante Adams remains the clear top target in his absence.

UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia. Nothing new medically — this reflects the calendar reaching the week HC Sean McVay has targeted since Week 2. McVay called himself "hopeful" Nacua plays (9/28), described the injury as "almost like pre-hernia" soreness, and said there's "no consideration" of IR; Adam Schefter reports the Rams don't believe surgery will be needed. A follow-up read was more guarded ("to be determined"), so treat this as genuinely 50/50 with a slight lean toward playing, final call likely Friday practice status (NBC Sports, ESPN, CBS Sports, 9/28-29). Davante Adams remains the top target if he sits again.

CLEARED TOWARD PLAYING (10/1-2): logged a full practice Thursday after a limited Wednesday session, with McVay firmly expecting him to play Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia; surgery is not currently expected (SI, NBC Sports, 10/1).

SEPARATE STORYLINE — Personal Conduct Policy: Nacua remains under an active NFL conduct-policy review tied to a civil lawsuit (alleging a bite and an antisemitic remark) and has begun steps toward a diversion program on related misdemeanor charges. He has not been placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List and ESPN's Adam Schefter says there's a real chance he plays out the season with no discipline, but the league can still act at any point since there's no decision deadline — a background risk to monitor, separate from the groin injury (CBS Sports, Fox News/Outkick, 10/1-2).

CLEARED (10/3): officially off the injury-worry list -- full practice participant all week and HC Sean McVay firmly expects him to play Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia with no game-time-decision framing anymore; surgery was never on the table. Downgrading tag from Short-Term Injury to Healthy. Separate conduct-policy review (civil suit) remains unresolved and worth continued background monitoring, but is no longer tied to his on-field availability.

CONFIRMED (10/4-5): played a full workload at Philadelphia in Week 4, posting 14 catches, 199 yards and a rushing TD (our stats database has this at 27.7 fantasy points) despite the Rams' loss (ESPN gameId 401772839). The hip/groin issue (variably described as hip vs. groin, unrelated to his earlier psoas issue) did not limit his role at all -- team-leading target share in the loss, with no lingering concern reported as of 10/5. Upgrading tag from Healthy to include WR1 Lock given the workload. Note: the separate NFL conduct-policy review (civil suit) remains open and unrelated to his on-field availability -- continue monitoring in the background.

UPDATE (10/13): put up a monster line in the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday Night Football (10/12) -- 17 catches (a career-high 24 targets) for 138 yards and a TD. The Rams fell to 2-3 despite the huge game, partly because K Harrison Mevis missed two field goals, including a potential game-winner in overtime (see his note) -- therams.com, Deseret News, AP/Boston Globe.

Malik Nabers.name: Malik Nabers
bullets: CLEARED: the shoulder that "popped out" (and back in) during Week 2's loss at the Rams came back with clean X-rays; Nabers was a full practice participant that Thursday and the ESPN status flipped from Questionable to Active ahead of Week 3 at Tennessee. Told reporters: "Good result. I'm smiling, I'm out there, playing, catching the ball, so good results... I'll be fine" (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Giants.com, 9/24).

UPDATE: played Week 3 and led the Giants with 5 catches on 6 targets for 26 yards (27% target share) in a 12-7 win over Tennessee — a quiet, low-yardage line but with no ill effects reported from the shoulder (NBC Sports, CBS Sports/RotoWire, 9/27-28).

The bigger Week 4 storyline is the QB change, not the shoulder: starter Jaxson Dart is out with a knee injury and Jameis Winston is set to start at QB going forward, which beat writers flag as a likelier drag on Nabers' target quality/fantasy ceiling than the now-resolved shoulder issue (CBS Sports, 9/29-30).

NEW (10/8): flipped to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington after not practicing Wednesday with a knee issue (Giants' official injury report, giants.com, 10/7) -- notable given his 2025 season ended with a torn ACL/meniscus in the same knee, though no beat writer has reported a new tear or setback. Treat as a practice-report flag to watch through Friday, not a confirmed re-injury.

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington -- no setback reported from the knee soreness that had him DNP Wednesday (the knee is the same one that ended his 2025 season with a torn ACL/meniscus, but no new tear or setback has been reported). HC/beat coverage from the Giants was cautiously upbeat all week (bolavip, Newsweek, 10/7-9).

Jayden Daniels.name: Jayden Daniels
bullets: Dislocated his left (non-throwing) elbow — the same joint's 2nd dislocation within under a year — late in the first half of Washington's 37-20 Week 2 loss to Dallas (Sun 9/20); X-rays showed no fracture. Ruled out for Week 3 vs. Seattle, with Marcus Mariota named starting QB (Dan Quinn, 9/22 presser).

NEW (AP, ~9/23): imaging and multiple specialist opinions found NO ligament damage, and Daniels will NOT need surgery; the Commanders are not placing him on IR "for now" (FOX Sports/AP, NBC Sports/PFT, ProFootballRumors) — a real upgrade from Tuesday's total-uncertainty read.

Still no firm return timetable — HC Dan Quinn has declined to commit to one, with re-evaluation expected to continue toward Washington's Week 7 bye. Mariota remains the starter in the interim, and the recurring nature of the injury (2nd dislocation of the same elbow in <1 year) keeps real season-long variance in play even without surgery.

UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Week 4 (in London vs. Indianapolis). He returned to practice this week and traveled with the team, and per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz told teammates he's foregoing surgery and felt he "owed it to them" to return as fast as possible (RotoWire, Washington Times, Hogs Haven, 9/28). HC Dan Quinn said he isn't sure yet if Daniels plays "in six days" but that he "isn't far off" and will practice "in some form" this week. Read this as soft/early-stage QUESTIONABLE, not a real lean toward playing — nearly every outlet still has Marcus Mariota as the presumptive Week 4 starter pending how practice reps go Wed-Fri.

CONFIRMED OUT (10/2-3): ruled out for Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Colts in London -- ESPN's Adam Schefter does not believe Daniels will be active despite making the trip and practicing in some form. Marcus Mariota remains the favorite to start unless Daniels takes the bulk of first-team reps, which hasn't happened (CBS Sports, RotoBaller, Commanders.com, 10/1-3). No surgery still planned this season; recurring elbow dislocation keeps real multi-week variance in play.

CONFIRMED (10/5): did not play Week 4 vs. the Colts in London; Marcus Mariota started for a second straight game and Washington won 17-16 (Colts.com). Per Adam Schefter, Daniels will "eventually need surgery" on the elbow (this is the THIRD dislocation of the same non-throwing elbow within under a year) but is deferring it to the offseason and will likely play in a brace whenever he returns -- no practice/return timeline has been given as of 10/5 (NBC Sports). Given the recurring nature of the injury and no near-term surgical or return plan, upgrading tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury; Mariota remains the starter indefinitely.

IMPROVING, REVISED (10/7): real progress this week -- HC Dan Quinn said Daniels is set for a full Wed-Thu-Fri practice week with the goal of starting Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants, wearing the elbow brace (ESPN, TSN). Added urgency: backup Marcus Mariota suffered his own MCL sprain vs. the Colts, making 7th-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis the emergency option if Daniels can't go. Some practice-report aggregators still show a "limited" tag, so treat this as a real but not fully resolved Questionable rather than a lock. Revising tag down from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch given the firm full-practice/start-Sunday trajectory -- no longer an open-ended absence.

CLEARED (10/8): officially flipped from Questionable to Active ahead of Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants after a full Wednesday practice; per Jay Glazer, Washington plans to start Daniels in the elbow brace, and Tom Pelissero reports the team remains hopeful he returns to the starting role (ESPN, CBS Sports, 10/7-8). Backup situation is in flux -- Marcus Mariota aggravated the same MCL he had surgically repaired in 2022 and is doubtful/out, which only reinforces that Washington needs Daniels back now.

CONFIRMED HEALTHY RETURN (10/12): started Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants in the elbow brace and delivered a big dual-threat performance in a 27-27 overtime tie -- 17-of-25 passing for 199 yards with no interceptions (despite 5 sacks), plus 103 rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns on 9 carries. No setback to the surgically-pending elbow reported. Washington lost a late chance to win in OT after a Daniels scramble ran out the clock instead of spiking it.

Jonathon Brooks.name: Jonathon Brooks
bullets: CONFIRMED: officially placed on injured reserve Wednesday 9/23 after re-aggravating a groin/core-muscle injury late in Carolina's 34-3 Week 2 win over Atlanta (9/20) (Panthers.com; AP via Washington Post/US News) — the earlier "week-to-week, seeking opinions" framing has resolved into a hard IR move.
AP source reporting: Brooks will undergo surgery to repair the core-muscle injury and is expected to miss a minimum of six weeks (IR floor is 4 games); a return later this season is still expected.

Carolina signed S Isaiah Simmons off the practice squad to fill the vacated 53-man spot. Backfield touches now run through Chuba Hubbard (clear-cut RB1, no longer sharing the load) and AJ Dillon (RB2/short-yardage) — Rico Dowdle signed with Pittsburgh in the offseason and is NOT part of Carolina's backfield picture.

Jordan Mason.name: Jordan Mason
bullets: Placed on injured reserve Sept 16 after further evaluation of the sore thumb from Minnesota's Week 1 win over Green Bay revealed a fracture requiring surgery — HC Kevin O'Connell said the exact moment of the break is unclear, but it escalated from what first looked like a bruise.

IR's mandatory 4-game minimum rules him out through Week 5 (vs. Bears, at Bucs, vs. Dolphins, at Saints); O'Connell called the recovery "not expected to be long-term" beyond that window, putting a realistic return at Week 6 or later with no hard date confirmed.
Minnesota promoted RB DeeJay Dallas from the practice squad and signed Jerome Ford to the practice squad as depth behind Aaron Jones.

Jordyn Tyson.name: Jordyn Tyson
bullets: Hamstring injury in an August joint practice vs JAX; placed on IR with a return designation — out at least the first 4 games.

Seahawks D/ST.name: Seahawks D/ST
bullets: Reigning Super Bowl champs and the #1-ranked defense in 2026 projections — led the NFL in scoring defense and led the league with 7 defensive/ST TDs in 2025. Elite, high-floor DST1.

Worth monitoring: starting QB Sam Darnold left the Sept 9 opener with a hip injury; a Sept 10 MRI ruled out major structural damage but he's still expected to miss Week 2 at Arizona — a Drew Lock-led offense for that game could mean tougher field position/offensive support for the defense.

Dalton Kincaid.name: Dalton Kincaid
bullets: Sleeper-caliber TE1 upside (80/1,000/10 pace) after a 7 TD, 14.6 YPC 2025 — durability is the real question, but camp reports have his snap share trending up even with Knox/Hawes healthy.
The breakout thesis showed up in real games: 7 catches on 8 targets for 95 yards and a TD in Thursday night's win over Detroit, his best game of the young season.

PLAYED THROUGH IT (10/18): exited Sunday's 33-30 win at Las Vegas in the 3rd quarter with a rib injury and was briefly questionable to return, but came back in the 4th quarter and helped close out the win -- finished with 7 catches for 38 yards (had a TD nullified by a holding penalty) on a day Buffalo improved to 5-1 (CBS Sports, NBC Sports, DraftKings Network, 10/18). Today's QUESTIONABLE tag reflects that rib soreness still being managed, but Buffalo is on its Week 7 bye (next game isn't until Nov. 1 vs. Baltimore), so he has two full weeks to heal. Keeping Health Watch given he played through it with no larger setback.

BYE-WEEK RESET (10/21): today's QUESTIONABLE-to-ACTIVE flip is procedural -- Buffalo is on its Week 7 bye (confirmed Fox Sports/NBC Sports bye-week lists), so there's no game this week for any designation to attach to. The rib injury that had him questionable to return in the Week 6 win over Las Vegas (10/18) has not been described as a long-term issue by any outlet found; he has two full weeks before Buffalo's next game (Nov. 1 vs. Baltimore) to heal. No new setback reported.

Blake Corum.name: Blake Corum
bullets: RB2 behind Kyren Williams in a ~65:35 split that has been fluid through camp.

Carried a near-even Monday-night workload alongside Kyren Williams (combined 164 rush yards) in the win over the Giants — the split continues to run closer to 50/50 than a clean Williams-lead role (CBS Sports/RotoWire).

Trevor Lawrence.name: Trevor Lawrence
bullets: Ranked QB11 for 2026 — with Etienne now gone to New Orleans, more of the offense funnels through Lawrence's arm and legs; expected to throw 30+ TDs for the first time.

UPDATE: threw 3 TD passes (including to Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers) in Jacksonville's 35-6 rout of New England in Week 3 (9/27) — a strong bounce-back performance for the passing game (Jaguars.com, SI/OnSI).

Carnell Tate.name: Carnell Tate
bullets: Took a hard hit in Monday practice and missed Wednesday's session with dizziness/stiffness — evaluated but not diagnosed with a concussion, has since returned to practice with no Week 1 concern.
Rookie WR with rising fantasy stock as the direct beneficiary any time Wan'Dale Robinson is banged up.
2026 1st-round pick (No. 4 overall, Ohio State) — Tennessee's top rookie weapon for Cam Ward alongside slot man Wan'Dale Robinson.

NEW (10/8): added to Tennessee's injury report Thursday with a back issue, downgraded to limited after a full practice Wednesday -- a new ailment unrelated to the August practice-collision stiffness. Comes right after his best game of the season (9 catches, 145 yards in the Week 4 loss at Baltimore), so a limited Sunday vs. Houston would be a real hit to Cam Ward's passing game (Yahoo Sports/Titans beat, 10/8). QUESTIONABLE heading into the weekend; no final Friday designation found yet.

CLEARED (10/12): HC Robert Saleh's 'good to go' read on the back tightness held up -- Tate played through it with no setback or in-game exit reported in Sunday's 26-3 Week 5 loss at Houston (Titans fall to 0-5). Specific Week 5 catch/yardage totals could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update; revisit once a box score source becomes available. No new injury concern entering Week 6.

Tetairoa McMillan.name: Tetairoa McMillan
bullets: 2025 AP Offensive Rookie of the Year (70/1,014/7); profiles as a safe WR2 (~WR18-20) capped by Carolina's low-volume passing offense, with Jalen Coker now adding real target competition.

Bhayshul Tuten.name: Bhayshul Tuten
bullets: Illness that sent him home from a Sept 2 practice was a non-issue by kickoff — logged a full workload in Jacksonville's Week 1 win over Cleveland with 15 carries for 66 yards plus a catch for 22 yards.

UPDATE: posted a season-high 73 yards on 15 touches with 5 broken tackles in Jacksonville's 35-6 rout of New England in Week 3 (9/27) — a clear positive trendline heading into Week 4 (Jaguars.com, SI/OnSI).

Ashton Jeanty.name: Ashton Jeanty
bullets: The Aug 23 ankle sprain was a non-issue for the Sept 13 opener — Jeanty was off the injury report entirely and delivered a workhorse Week 1 in Las Vegas' game vs. Miami: 23 carries for 102 yards plus 6 catches for 45 yards and 2 receiving TDs (27 touches, 2 total TDs).
Confirmed as the clear lead back over rookie Mike Washington Jr., who saw no meaningful role in Week 1.

Reaffirmed the workhorse role with 25 total touches (21 carries/48 yards, 4-of-7 targets/15 yards) in the Raiders' 26-14 upset of the Chargers in Week 2, but had a late-game injury scare (returned to finish the game) and dropped 3 passes — worth a brief watch, not yet a designation change (CBS Sports, NBC Sports).

NEW (10/8): downgraded to a limited practice participant Thursday with a foot issue layered on top of the ankle he's been managing since exiting Week 4's loss to Kansas City (hobbled off in the 3rd quarter, returned in the 4th). Raiders haven't signaled real concern about Sunday's game vs. New England and one outlet still expects him active, but worth tracking given the back-to-back-day downgrade (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, Newsweek, 10/8).

CLEARED (10/12): played through the ankle/foot combo with no reported setback in Sunday's Week 5 loss at New England (Patriots won 45-17); specific carry/yardage totals for the game could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update. Remains the clear lead back in Las Vegas' (now 3-2) backfield.

James Cook III.name: James Cook III
bullets: Led Buffalo's backfield as expected in the opener vs. Houston: 13 carries for 57 yards and 3 catches for 12 yards, though he didn't find the end zone in a game the Bills controlled on the ground.
Signed a 4-year, $48M extension (up to $30M guaranteed) in August 2025, locking him in through 2029.

Kenneth Walker III.name: Kenneth Walker III
bullets: Immediately looks like the lead back in Kansas City's backfield after the free-agent signing (3yr/$43.05M) — leads the NFL with 47 carries (56 touches) through 2 games, backing up a Week 1 explosion (23-173-1 rush, 2 total TDs vs. Denver) with a Week 2 workhorse outing (24-117 rush, 6 catches/61 yds vs. Indianapolis).

CONFIRMED: despite HC Andy Reid's talk of "balance" with rookie Emmett Johnson, Walker's Week 3 role barely budged — 78% of the RB snaps and 20 of 23 RB carry opportunities before the final drive, extending his streak to three straight weeks with a 70%+ snap share and 20+ PPR points in a 24-10 win over Miami. Dolphins did hold him to just 16 yards from scrimmage after halftime, worth monitoring, but the workhorse role itself is unchanged (Arrowhead Pride, RotoWire, 9/28).

Garrett Wilson.name: Garrett Wilson
bullets: Elite volume floor even coming off a down 2025 — earned a 30%+ target share early last season and has topped 23% every year of his career.

Tee Higgins.name: Tee Higgins
bullets: Played through a heel contusion in Week 1, catching 3 of 6 targets for 59 yards.

NEW (9/30): ruled OUT for Thursday's Week 4 game at Jacksonville with a shoulder injury, after not practicing Wednesday (CBS Sports, FantasyPros, RotoWire, 9/30). Reporting doesn't yet specify when the shoulder issue arose or a return timeline — flagging this as fresh news since our own roster tracker's status field hasn't yet caught up to the OUT designation. S Jessie Bates III (neck) is also out for Cincinnati Thursday. Ja'Marr Chase remains the clear top target in his absence.

UPDATE (10/5): missed a second straight game with the shoulder injury in Thursday's Week 4 loss to Jacksonville, never practicing that week (CBS Sports, National Football Post, Sportskeeda, 10/1-2). Today's flip from OUT back to QUESTIONABLE suggests real practice-field progress toward a return -- HC Zac Taylor has called him "on the right trajectory to play" -- but no firm return date has been reported yet, so keeping the standard Injury tier rather than Short-Term. Ja'Marr Chase remains Cincinnati's clear top target in his continued absence.

CORRECTION (10/8): previous notes describing a 'shoulder' injury that kept Higgins out of the Jacksonville game were inaccurate. The real story: Higgins played in Week 4's 22-17 loss to Jacksonville and had a big game (11 catches for 157 yards on 16 targets) before hurting his adductor on a late sideline catch, leaving briefly and managing one final-drive snap. HC Zac Taylor called him day-to-day Monday and did not rule him out for Sunday's Week 5 game at Miami, alongside Ja'Marr Chase's concussion situation (FieldLevelMedia, RotoBaller, 4for4, 10/5). Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch given the day-to-day framing and that he already played through it once.

CLEARED (10/12): played through the adductor injury with no setback reported in Sunday's Week 5 win at Miami (Bengals won 31-24, now 3-2); specific catch/yardage totals for Higgins could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update. Ja'Marr Chase (see his note) also cleared concussion protocol and had a big game in the same contest.

Joe Burrow.name: Joe Burrow
bullets: Played through the back tightness as expected — active and started Cincinnati's 20-6 win over Houston (Sun 9/20), going 20/31 for 207 yards and 2 TDs (both to Ja'Marr Chase, from 32 and 18 yards) with no INTs, though he did take 5 sacks.
Confirms the back issue was minor/day-to-day as reported all week — no setback, no in-game re-aggravation reported, and no new limitation entering Week 3 prep.
Elite passing-volume QB1 when right — the profile concern remains price/ADP more than health at this point.

De'Zhaun Stribling.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
bullets: Diagnosed with a deltoid ligament sprain in his left ankle (not an Achilles issue — HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed the Achilles is intact) after leaving the Sept 10 opener vs. the Rams early without a target.

Underwent ankle surgery Wednesday (Sept 16) after the injury proved worse than initially believed, and was officially placed on injured reserve — revised from the earlier ~1-month outlook to a firmer ~10-week absence per Shanahan's post-surgery update.
Drop-and-stash-if-needed territory in shallow leagues for the next couple of months. Still a real deep-league breakout stash for whenever SF's WR room opens back up.

Sam LaPorta.name: Sam LaPorta
bullets: The hip flare-up was a non-issue once games started — produced in both Week 1 (9.8 fantasy pts, opener vs. New Orleans) and Week 2 (17.2 fantasy pts in Thursday night's win over Buffalo), with no re-aggravation reported.

Jonah Coleman.name: Jonah Coleman
bullets: With both RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins banged up, Coleman led Denver's backfield in Week 2 snap share (42.4%), touches (13) and total yards (58 plus a TD) in the win over Jacksonville — his first career rushing TD. Named a top Week 3 waiver-wire target by NFL.com (9/24).

REVISED (from the earlier "minor, shouldn't affect gameday status" framing, then from last update's "short absence" framing): the ankle is a high ankle sprain, and Denver placed Coleman on injured reserve Saturday (9/26) rather than just ruling him out week-to-week — he's expected back no sooner than Oct. 25 vs. Arizona (first eligible date), meaning at least 4 additional games missed on top of Week 3 (ESPN, NFL.com, Denver Gazette, CBS Sports, 9/26). Upgrading the tag from Short-Term to Long-Term Injury to reflect the real, IR-confirmed absence.

The good news for Denver: both J.K. Dobbins (hip) and RJ Harvey (hamstring) escaped the injury report with no designation and are expected to play Week 3 — the backfield rotation should run through them for the next several weeks with Coleman on IR.

UPDATE (10/5): remains on IR with the Week 2 high-ankle sprain, first eligible to return Week 7 (no change to the previously reported Oct. 25 vs. Arizona target). Denver lost Week 4 to the Chargers; in that game J.K. Dobbins clearly won the early-down split over RJ Harvey -- 11 carries for 83 yards and a TD plus a catch, vs. just 2 carries for 2 yards and 3 catches for 14 yards for Harvey (CBS Sports/RotoWire). Dobbins looks like the stronger side of Denver's committee right now while Coleman remains out.

Tyler Shough.name: Tyler Shough
bullets: Firmly entrenched as New Orleans' starting QB heading into 2026 after opening the season with 410 passing yards in Week 1 and leading the Saints to a last-second Week 2 win over Baltimore (24-17).

No injury concerns reported on Shough himself; the Saints' broader offensive-line and receiver injury situation (Dillon Radunz torn ACL/out for the season, Kelvin Banks Jr. high-ankle sprain, Jordyn Tyson hamstring/expected out ~2 months) is worth monitoring as a drag on his supporting cast and pass-pro, but doesn't threaten his starting job.

NEW (10/8): limited at Wednesday's practice with a left (non-throwing) hand injury ahead of Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Minnesota; beat reporters note it isn't expected to affect his throwing, and he remains New Orleans' starter (Saints' official injury report via Crescent City Sports/Canal Street Chronicles, 10/7).

CLEARED (10/9): full practice participant as of Thursday's report on the left (non-throwing) hand injury suffered during Monday's loss to Atlanta -- firmly on track to start Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Minnesota, with no threat to his job (Saints beat/Field Level Media, 10/7-8).

Week 5 final (10/11): rough outing against a tough Minnesota defense (No. 2 DVOA, No. 1 vs. the pass) -- 16-of-25 for 96 yards, no TD, 2 INT, and his first career game without a rushing attempt, in a 23-13 loss that was also his first game all season under 250 passing yards. No injury reported; one bad matchup rather than a threat to his starting job. Saints play at the Giants in Week 6 (Sun 10/18).

Denzel Boston.name: Denzel Boston
bullets: 2026 second-round rookie (No. 39 overall, Washington) who opened the season in Cleveland's starting WR2 spot alongside Jerry Jeudy.
Broke out in Week 2 vs. Tampa Bay with 5 catches for 95 yards and a 55-yard TD, earning an NFL Rookie of the Week nomination.

NEW (10/16): picked up a foot injury this week -- logged back-to-back limited practices Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15), which is why he's carrying a QUESTIONABLE tag for the first time this season ahead of Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Baltimore (10/18). Beat writers (NBC Sports, CBS Sports) still expect him to play without real restriction.

CLEARED (10/18): carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Baltimore after logging back-to-back limited practices Wednesday/Thursday -- beat reporting (NBC Sports, The Fantasy Footballers) had already expected him to play without real restriction. Dropping the Health Watch tag now that the foot issue produced no game-status designation.

Omarion Hampton.name: Omarion Hampton
bullets: Rookie hype exceeds his current role — projected ~250 att/1,125 yds, but likely won't clear 70% snap share with Mitchell handling passing downs. High-variance breakout, not a lock.

Harrison Butker.name: Harrison Butker
bullets: Added off waivers this week. Kansas City's long-time starting kicker with no camp competition; no fresh injury or role news found as of this update -- standard low-variance K1 role behind a pass-heavy Chiefs offense.

Justin Jefferson.name: Justin Jefferson
bullets: Down year by his own standard in 2025 (WR30 overall) but still finished 6th league-wide in target share (28.5%) — new QB Kyler Murray has a track record of feeding elite WR1s.
Left Sunday's Week 3 win over Tampa Bay (23-16) early in the 1st quarter with a left ankle injury after a defender landed on it during a 10-yard screen reception, and did not return.

NEW: Monday's MRI (9/28) revealed a clean ankle sprain with no structural/long-term damage — a real relief given the initial fear of a high-ankle or deltoid-ligament issue. HC Kevin O'Connell called the outlook positive and said the team will manage his practice reps through the week to gauge Week 4 availability vs. Miami; there's a real chance he plays (ESPN, NBC Sports, Bleacher Report, Athlon, 9/28-29). Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch given the clean imaging and plausible Week 4 clearance.

WORSENED (10/2-3): despite the clean MRI and earlier optimism, Jefferson was officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. Miami (CBS Sports' Week 4 injury report, PrizePicks, 10/2-3) -- the ankle sprain needed more than a week of management after all. Bumping tag from Health Watch to Injury; no multi-week timeline reported, so treat as a week-to-week absence for now rather than Short/Long-Term.

TRENDING UP (10/7): QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at New Orleans. HC Kevin O'Connell said as of 10/3-4 that Jefferson has made "great progress" on the ankle, though it's "too early to say" definitively if he plays (ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, Fox9, NBC Sports). No setback reported since last week's OUT designation -- keeping the Injury tag for now given he's not yet confirmed to play, but this reads as a real step toward a Week 5 return rather than a new concern.

UPDATE (10/8): was a limited practice participant to begin Week 5 prep (Wednesday, 10/7) for Sunday's game at New Orleans -- a step up from last week's OUT designation, though not yet confirmation he plays. Final designation comes Friday.

CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/12): played a full workload in Sunday's Week 5 win at New Orleans (Vikings won 23-13 to improve to 5-0 and head into their bye) with no setback from the ankle -- 6 catches for 79 yards and a touchdown (a 15-yard TD from Kyler Murray in the 3rd quarter), his first score since Week 1. Upgrading tag from Injury to Healthy given the clean workload and no re-aggravation.

Jonathan Taylor.name: Jonathan Taylor
bullets: Led the NFL with 323 carries in 2025 — 1,585 yds, 18 rush TD, RB1 overall.
New contract extension cements him as the Colts' offensive centerpiece; staff may trim touches slightly to manage wear, but role security is elite.
New extension (announced Aug 6, 2026): 2 years, $44M ($39M guaranteed, up to $47M) — the 2nd-highest-paid RB in the NFL by AAV.

Trey McBride.name: Trey McBride
bullets: 2025: 126 rec/1,239 yds/11 TD, led all TEs in target share (25.4%).

New Cardinals staff invested heavily in the run game (drafted RB Jeremiyah Love 3rd overall, signed Tyler Allgeier) — his 683-route workload likely won't repeat. Still a top-2 TE, just not a top-15-overall ceiling.

NEW (9/30): suffered a concussion on a head-on hit from Lions S Brian Branch in Week 3 (3 catches, 25 yards before exiting) and is ruled OUT for Week 4 vs. Washington (Bleacher Report, ClutchPoints, AZCardinals.com, 9/28). Worth tracking as a protocol case — no set return timeline until he clears the steps, but concussions can also clear quickly. He'd been out-targeting Marvin Harrison Jr. 23-4 through two games, so his absence is a meaningful hit to Arizona's passing-game volume for at least this week.

UPDATE (10/5): remains in the concussion protocol after the head-on hit from Lions S Brian Branch in Week 3; did not practice that week and was ruled out for Arizona's following game, with Elijah Higgins, Tip Reiman and Travis Vokolek filling in at TE (azcardinals.com, CBS Sports, NBC Sports). Note: several injury-report sources mislabeled that game as "vs. Washington"; Arizona's actual Week 4 opponent was the New York Giants -- an indexing error in those sources, not a real schedule conflict. Team-sourced reporting says he "should have a good chance to clear protocol in time for Week 5" -- a short, routine absence. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Short-Term Injury given that fairly firm timeline.

Travis Etienne Jr..name: Travis Etienne Jr.
bullets: Signed a 4-yr/$52M deal with hometown New Orleans as a free agent and is listed as the starter, but Alvin Kamara remains on the roster and real committee risk has materialized early.

Was healthy and productive early in Week 3 (led all Saints rushers with 13 carries for 57 yards, plus 2 catches for 13 yards) before pulling up with a hamstring injury after a 16-yard run in the 3rd quarter of Sunday's loss to the Raiders — did not return (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 9/27).

NEW: officially OUT — HC Kellen Moore said Monday (9/28) Etienne will have "time lost" with the hamstring, with no specific return timeline set and an IR stint still possible depending on further evaluation (RotoWire, NBC Sports, FantasyPros, 9/28). Kamara is the direct backfield beneficiary given the committee usage already in place; treat Etienne as a bench stash until more clarity emerges.
