CONFIRMED, tag revised from Injury to Long-Term Injury: New Orleans officially placed Etienne on injured reserve (hamstring) on 10/1. HC Kellen Moore said no surgery is needed, but the recovery is expected to run at least 4 weeks — the team's Week 8 bye makes his next realistic game action Sunday, Nov. 8 at Cleveland (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, FantasyPros, 10/1). Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller are the direct backfield beneficiaries in the meantime; treat Etienne as a stash-only dynasty/IR piece for roughly a month.

Rome Odunze.name: Rome Odunze
bullets: Played through the calf injury that had him Questionable into the weekend and finished with 2 catches for 52 yards on 3 targets as Chicago routed Carolina 59-37 — light volume, but more a function of the blowout game script than the calf, which held up with no setback reported.
Remains Caleb Williams' clear WR1 with DJ Moore traded away; expect target share to normalize now that the calf is no longer a question.

UPDATE: with Caleb Williams (hamstring) and backup Tyson Bagent both out, journeyman Case Keenum authored a 247-yard, 2-TD Week 3 Monday Night upset of Philadelphia (27-7, 9/28). Chicago's passing offense is now running through a stopgap QB for the next several weeks — worth tempering expectations on Odunze's target efficiency until Williams returns, even though the WR1 role itself remains his.

Jalen Hurts.name: Jalen Hurts
bullets: No 2026 camp or preseason injury reports; practiced fully through August, including joint sessions vs NE.
Standard top-5 fantasy QB profile — the rushing floor keeps him there even on off passing days.

RULED OUT (10/15-16): a precautionary ultrasound taken in London ahead of the Jacksonville trip found a superficial blood clot in his calf; team doctors initially cleared him to play, but a Wednesday (10/14) follow-up scan showed the clot had moved, and the Eagles ruled him out for Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. Carolina (6abc, Fox affiliates, NBC Sports, 10/15). NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports he is "out indefinitely" with no return timeline set as the team determines a treatment plan -- Tanner McKee will start in his place. Tagging the standard Injury tier given the genuinely open-ended, pending-further-evaluation nature of a blood clot rather than a normal soft-tissue strain; this is a real health situation to keep close tabs on, not a routine week-to-week designation. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith (both hamstring) are also in doubt for the same game -- see their notes.

CONFIRMED (10/19): the roster tracker now lists Hurts on injured reserve for the calf blood clot (no independent beat-reporter confirmation of the exact IR transaction was found via search, but the practical effect -- out well beyond this week -- matches reporting). Backup Tanner McKee started Sunday's 25-14 loss to Carolina, Philadelphia's fourth straight defeat (now 2-4) and its first 4-game skid since 2020 -- McKee went 26-of-45 for 215 yards and a TD to DeVonta Smith (19-yard score with 10:42 left) before the comeback stalled; the Eagles also signed QB Joe Milton III off Dallas' practice squad for added depth. No return timeline has been reported yet.

ESCALATED, OUT FOR SEASON (10/19): the calf clot has progressed -- follow-up testing found a deep vein thrombosis (DVT) with additional blood clots that traveled to both lungs (bilateral pulmonary emboli), not just the original superficial calf clot found in London. Agent Nicole Lynn and the team say he is "clinically stable" with "no significant functional limitations," but he cannot play while on blood thinners -- treatment is expected to sideline him roughly 3+ months, ruling him out for the rest of 2026 (NFL Network, ESPN, Boston Globe, Fox29, 10/19). Prognosis is described as very good with no expected long-term effects, and he's expected to stay around the team as captain. Tanner McKee remains Philadelphia's starter for the foreseeable future. Upgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Long-Term Injury given the confirmed season-ending timeline.

Rico Dowdle.name: Rico Dowdle
bullets: Suffered a toe injury on a pass-blocking/fumble-recovery rep in the 2nd quarter of a loss to New England, was carted to the locker room, returned for a few series coming out of halftime, then appeared to re-aggravate it and was ruled out for good; finished with 9 total touches for 44 yards.
CONFIRMED: officially ruled OUT for Week 3 vs. Cincinnati after DNP all week, despite the issue being described as "day-to-day" (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/25-26).

NEW: still hasn't practiced — listed DNP again on Monday (9/28) — which is a real concern given Pittsburgh is on a short week for Thursday Night Football at Cleveland in Week 4. He'll need a near-miracle practice ramp-up to play Thursday and enters the week very much questionable (NBC Sports, 9/28). Jaylen Warren is set for another game of workhorse usage should Dowdle sit again.

UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE ahead of Thursday's short-week game at Cleveland, but beat coverage through Tuesday's practice (the last fully-indexed report at research time) still had him a full DNP and in a walking boot, with Steelers Depot and Still Curtain both explicitly framing him as "trending towards missing a second-straight game" and calling Wednesday's practice report the real swing session. Treat the QUESTIONABLE tag cautiously — it may reflect today's (Wed 9/30) official report showing him as at least limited, but the stronger prior signal through Tuesday still points toward sitting out. Jaylen Warren (20 touches Week 3) remains the clear lead back regardless of Dowdle's exact designation.

UPDATE (9/30): officially ruled OUT for Thursday Night Football's Week 4 short-week game at Cleveland — still hasn't practiced since the Week 2 toe injury (DNP every session, previously spotted in a walking boot). No surgery or exact "X weeks" timeline has been given, but Pittsburgh's mini-bye before Week 5 (not playing again until Oct. 11 vs. Indianapolis) is the beat-writer-flagged likely return window (NBC Sports, RotoWire, Yahoo Sports/AP, 9/29-30). Jaylen Warren continues as the clear workhorse (~90% snap share) in his absence.

CONFIRMED, tag revised from Injury to Short-Term Injury: Dowdle (toe) was a full DNP all week and was ruled OUT for Thursday Night Football's Week 4 game at Cleveland, which Pittsburgh lost 27-24 on a last-second field goal — his second straight missed game. NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported afterward that Dowdle has a "pretty good chance" to return for Week 5 vs. Indianapolis on Oct. 11, giving this a fairly firm ~1-week runway rather than open-ended (Steelers Depot, Yahoo Sports, 10/1-2). Jaylen Warren again handled the workhorse Thursday (17 carries/93 yards, 3 catches/33 yards) and remains the clear starter in Dowdle's absence.

ON TRACK (10/7): QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Colts, consistent with the ~1-week return runway Rapoport reported last week. Beat reporting describes him as "making progress" this week, though the team hasn't yet confirmed his availability. Keeping Short-Term Injury given the still-intact short timeline; Jaylen Warren remains the starter regardless of Dowdle's exact Sunday role.

REVISED FROM SHORT-TERM TO STANDARD INJURY (10/12): remained out for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Colts despite returning to limited practice Wed/Thu and HC Mike McCarthy calling him 'making progress' -- our roster tracker confirms OUT, and Jaylen Warren again carried the workload, exploding for 188 total yards and two long touchdowns (an 80-yard catch, a 50-yard run) in Pittsburgh's 34-22 win. This is now three straight missed games since the Week 2 toe injury, well past the ~1-week runway Ian Rapoport reported two weeks ago -- revising the tag from Short-Term Injury to the standard Injury tier since that short timeline did not hold up and no new firm return date has been reported. Warren remains the clear starter regardless of Dowdle's eventual role.

REVISED BACK TO SHORT-TERM (10/14): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip tracks real news -- Steelers OC Brian Angelichio said Monday (10/12) he expects Dowdle back for Week 6's game at Tampa Bay, per The Athletic's Mike DeFabo. Re-upgrading the tag to Short-Term Injury given the now-firm 1-week-away target, after it had been bumped to the standard Injury tier two weeks ago when the original ~1-week Rapoport estimate didn't hold. HC Mike McCarthy still called Jaylen Warren "our featured player right now," signaling Dowdle likely returns to a shared role rather than instantly reclaiming the full workhorse job.

UPDATE (10/15): no fresh Wednesday/Thursday Week 6 practice-report confirmation found yet beyond OC Brian Angelichio's Monday (10/12) comments expecting him back -- recheck Friday's final injury report before fully trusting the short-term return target.

CORRECTION (10/16): the injury is a dislocated toe, not the quad/hamstring framing earlier notes used -- Dowdle has missed three straight games (Weeks 3-5) with it. HC Mike McCarthy said after the Week 5 win over Indianapolis that Dowdle was "close" and he's hopeful for a Week 6 return vs. Tampa Bay (10/18), with an expectation he practices this week; no Wednesday/Thursday practice report could be confirmed via search as of this update. Jaylen Warren remains Pittsburgh's clear lead back, with McCarthy floating a "one-two punch" once Dowdle is back -- keeping the Short-Term Injury tag given the team's stated Week 6 target.

CLEARED (10/17): logged a full practice Thursday -- the first full practice participation since the Week 2 toe injury -- and carries no designation into Sunday's Week 6 game at Tampa Bay, ending a three-game absence (Weeks 3-5). Softening tag from Short-Term Injury to Health Watch now that he's actually cleared. HC Mike McCarthy has signaled a "one-two punch" split with Jaylen Warren rather than Dowdle instantly reclaiming the full workhorse job, so expect a shared role in his first game back.

NEW DESIGNATION (10/18): flipped from yesterday's clean clearance back to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 6 game at Tampa Bay -- but this reads as a standard return-from-injury designation rather than a new setback: he was a full practice participant Thursday AND Friday (The Fantasy Footballers), and Steelers OC Brian Angelichio had already said Monday he expected Dowdle back this week. HC Mike McCarthy has indicated Jaylen Warren keeps the larger role of the two even once Dowdle is active, so this isn't a 50/50 split. Keeping Health Watch given the clean back-to-back full practices.

WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): played a complementary role in his first game back from the toe injury, as expected -- 7 carries for 40 yards plus 3 catches for 9 yards in Pittsburgh's 26-19 OT win over Tampa Bay, behind Jaylen Warren's 14 carries for 50 yards and 2 catches for 28 yards (Yahoo Sports box score, 10/18). No re-aggravation reported. Keeping Health Watch -- this confirms HC Mike McCarthy's stated "one-two punch" plan rather than Dowdle reclaiming the full workhorse role.

Alec Pierce.name: Alec Pierce
bullets: CONFIRMED: officially placed on injured reserve Wednesday 9/23 (HC Shane Steichen) after aggravating his surgically-repaired left heel late in Sunday's loss at Kansas City — couldn't put weight on it and left on crutches in a boot.

ESPN sources report Pierce plans to rehab rather than undergo a second surgery; he and the club are "hopeful" for roughly a 4-6 week absence after a second opinion, with return targeted for midseason — IR guarantees a minimum 4 games missed, and the exact timeline remains rehab-dependent/unconfirmed.

Colts signed veteran WR Darius Slayton (agreed to terms 9/22) as a direct replacement. Pierce had led the NFL in yards/catch among qualified WRs the past two seasons; expect targets to spread toward Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, Slayton, and TE Tyler Warren.

Jordan Addison.name: Jordan Addison
bullets: Rough 2025: a 3-game suspension to start the year, only 17.4% target share (Jefferson had 28.2%), finished WR43.
QB upgrade to Kyler Murray helps, but MIN also signed WR Jauan Jennings — adds competition rather than clearing it. Profiles more WR3/bench right now.

NEW (10/8): sidelined at Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury and carries a QUESTIONABLE tag (per the Vikings' own injury report) into Sunday's Week 5 game at New Orleans -- though one outlet flagged a conflicting Minnesota listing, so confirm Friday's final designation. First hamstring concern of the season, and it comes while he's already fighting for target share behind Justin Jefferson (himself limited this week with an ankle issue).

CONFIRMED (10/12): inactive for Sunday's Week 5 game at New Orleans with the hamstring injury after a true game-time call (only two limited practices during the week). Minnesota (5-0) now has its Week 6 bye, so Addison's next chance to play isn't until Oct. 25 vs. the Colts -- effectively a two-week break to heal rather than a sign of a longer-term issue. Justin Jefferson (see his note) returned and played a full workload in the same game.

NON-EVENT (10/14): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip is a procedural reset, not real news -- Minnesota is on its Week 6 bye (confirmed via Vikings.com/FoxSports league bye list), so there's no game for Addison to be questionable for. He remains on track to return Week 7 (Oct 25) vs. the Colts per last week's report; no new hamstring details surfaced.

Emanuel Wilson.name: Emanuel Wilson
bullets: Signed a one-year deal with Seattle in March after three seasons in Green Bay; added to this fantasy roster off waivers this week.

Part of a genuine four-man rotation in Seattle's backfield (George Holani, Jadarian Price, Wilson, with Zach Charbonnet still out on PUP/ACL recovery) rather than a clear role -- stands to see a bump in work with Price now ruled OUT for Week 4 (chest) alongside Holani.

ROLE CHANGE (10/16): took over as Seattle's clear every-down back in Thursday night's 17-14 OT loss at Denver (10/15) with both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price out -- a real workload shift, not just a one-game spot start, since both remain sidelined (see their notes). Upgrading tag from Committee to Job Secured while that depth-chart math holds.

Jordan Love.name: Jordan Love
bullets: Played Thursday night's Week 3 loss at Atlanta (Falcons won 35-14) with no recurrence of the Week 2 elbow/hand-numbness scare — a clean non-issue as expected.

Final line: 28/53, 312 yards, 2 TD (Christian Watson 4-yard, Matthew Golden 15-yard), 1 INT, 75.4 rating, took only 1 sack. Note the yardage was inflated by heavy garbage-time volume (53 attempts) after Green Bay fell behind 27 unanswered points — treat this as a middling real performance dressed up by a big raw stat line (RotoWire/CBS Sports, Heavy.com, 9/24-25).
Team-level concern: RT Zach Bako-Bewele's season-ending torn patellar tendon remains an O-line issue worth monitoring for Love's protection going forward.

Deebo Samuel Sr..name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
bullets: Two straight down seasons (sub-12 PPG each) with the worst YPRR marks of his career and a shrinking red-zone role.
Back in SF on a 1-year “reunion” deal — real chance 2026 is his last fantasy-relevant year.

NEW (10/13): strained his hamstring late in the 3rd quarter of Sunday's 32-29 Week 5 win over Seattle, fumbling on the play before being ruled out for the rest of the game (CBS Sports, FantasyPros, 10/11-12). HC Kyle Shanahan said Monday he's expected to miss "at least a couple of weeks" and is not currently being considered for IR (NBC Sports, SF Chronicle, Yardbarker, 10/12). He has a history of this hamstring flaring up and recurring on return per Shanahan's own comments about 2025, so treat the couple-week estimate as the real risk, not a floor. Picking Short-Term Injury given the reported ~2-week timeline; Mike Evans (see his note) is SF's clear top option in the meantime.

REVISED FROM SHORT-TERM TO STANDARD INJURY (10/14): HC Kyle Shanahan's full Monday (10/12) comments walk back last cycle's ~2-week framing -- he said Samuel is "going to miss some time," specifically "at least the next couple of games and likely a bit longer," which is a real extension beyond the firm 1-2-week Short-Term framing (ABC7/ABC30, NBC Sports Bay Area, ClutchPoints via Ian Rapoport). Not on IR as of this update. Expect him to miss SF's Week 6 game at Washington (MNF 10/19) and likely Week 7 at Atlanta too, with San Francisco's Week 8 bye potentially extending the absence further before a real return estimate firms up. Mike Evans (7/113/1 in the Week 5 win over Seattle) and Brandin Cooks/Jacob Cowing are the clear beneficiaries in the meantime.

Matthew Golden.name: Matthew Golden
bullets: The early skepticism has faded fast — Golden has been a real Week 2-3 riser: 9.8 fantasy pts in Week 2, then 5 catches for 100 yards and a TD (15-yard grab, plus a 45-yard catch that set up Green Bay's first score) in Thursday night's Week 3 loss at Atlanta, playing like a true No. 1 WR and called the Packers' "lone bright spot" by multiple outlets (RotoWire/CBS/Yahoo, 9/24).
253 receiving yards and 15 catches through 3 games — trending toward a real featured role opposite Watson rather than the depth-chart battle framing from earlier in camp.

J.K. Dobbins.name: J.K. Dobbins
bullets: CLEARED the hip issue that cost him the second half of Denver's Week 2 win over Jacksonville and started Sunday's Week 3 game vs. the Rams as the clear lead-carry back.

Still the clear lead back on paper, but the inefficient workload — combined with RJ Harvey's return to health as the passing-down option — is worth monitoring heading into Week 4.

Week 6 TNF (10/15): scored a rushing TD in Denver's 17-14 OT win over Seattle (17 carries, 41 yards). RJ Harvey led the backfield in receiving work and also scored (see his note) -- still a muddled two-man committee with no single back pulling away.

Xavier Worthy.name: Xavier Worthy
bullets: A distant WR2 behind Rice — only a 16.1% target share and WR60 finish in 2025; deep-threat/boom upside but not a reliable weekly starter.
Dislocated his right shoulder and suffered a torn labrum colliding with Travis Kelce in the Week 1 win over Denver, missing most of that game, but avoided season-ending surgery per HC Andy Reid.

Played through the shoulder in Week 2 vs. Indianapolis (9/20): 5 catches on 7 targets for 25 yards in the 33-30 OT win — back on the field as hoped, but modest per-target efficiency (5.0 YPT) so far post-labrum injury; worth tracking snap/route share before trusting a big workload.

Emeka Egbuka.name: Emeka Egbuka
bullets: The camp toe sprain didn't cost him any time — played through it in the Week 1 opener vs. Cincinnati, catching 5 of 6 targets for 63 yards.
Locked in as Tampa Bay's WR1 with Mike Evans gone to SF.

UPDATE (10/13-14): has fully taken over as Tampa Bay's clear top receiver amid the WR room's injuries -- 25 catches, 445 yards and 5 TD through 5 games. With Chris Godwin (fibula) and Bucky Irving (foot/shoulder) both ruled out for Week 6 vs. San Francisco (see their notes), Egbuka's target share should only grow further this week.

DeVonta Smith.name: DeVonta Smith
bullets: Played through the hamstring that had kept him out of practice in Week 1 and delivered a huge Week 2 (10 catches, 117 yards, 1 TD in the 24-20 win over Tennessee) — Philly's unquestioned WR1 now that A.J. Brown is in New England.

CLEARED and CONFIRMED: practiced in full Saturday, carried no injury designation into Monday night's Week 3 game at Chicago, and played through it cleanly — the hamstring flare-up is fully resolved. Led the Eagles with 6 catches (on 8 targets) for 65 yards, including the offense's longest play (a 30-yard grab), in a 27-7 loss where Jalen Hurts and the passing game otherwise struggled (NBC Sports, RotoWire, 9/28).
With Smith healthy, newly-acquired Dontayvion Wicks (traded from Green Bay in April) remains in a normal WR2 complementary role rather than a lead-receiver fill-in.

NEW (9/30): DNP Wednesday with the same hamstring that flared up in Week 3 — following the identical weekly pattern (DNP Thu/Wed, limited Fri, full Sat) that preceded him playing through it each of the last two weeks. Beat writers (NBC Sports Philadelphia, Bleeding Green Nation) expect the Eagles to manage him the same way again ahead of the Week 4 game vs. the Rams; no new setback or revised severity reported (9/30).

WORSENED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Rams after missing three straight practices with the same hamstring that has now flared up repeatedly -- a real step back from the DNP/limited/full weekly pattern that let him play through it the prior two weeks. Bumping tag from Health Watch to Injury given the back-to-back-week recurrence; no multi-week timeline reported yet. Dontayvion Wicks is in line for a bigger complementary role Sunday with Smith out (National Football Post, ESPN, NBC Sports Philadelphia, 10/1-3).

NO IMPROVEMENT (10/7): DNP again in Wednesday's practice ahead of the Eagles' Week 5 game vs. Jacksonville, played in London (10/11) as part of the NFL's international series. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo called him "questionable at very best" and floated a possible multi-game absence -- that specific framing hasn't been independently corroborated elsewhere, so treat the multi-game risk as a single-source flag rather than confirmed, but the hamstring clearly has not turned the corner after three recurrences. Keeping the standard Injury tier since no concrete number of weeks has been confirmed; Dontayvion Wicks again projects for a bigger role if Smith sits.

STILL OUT (10/8): DNP again in Thursday's practice, continuing the recurring hamstring issue -- trending toward missing a third straight game Sunday vs. Jacksonville in London. Dontayvion Wicks (himself now dealing with a hamstring issue, see his note) and the receiving corps remain thin behind him (Bleeding Green Nation, PhillyVoice, 10/8).

WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/10): officially flipped from QUESTIONABLE to OUT for Sunday's Week 5 game in London vs. Jacksonville -- a third straight missed game with the recurring hamstring strain, which never progressed past DNP/limited across this week's practices (NBC Sports Philadelphia, PhillyVoice, Bleeding Green Nation reporting through 10/8-9, one unconfirmed single-source report even floated a multi-game absence). Dontayvion Wicks (now himself cleared, see his note) projects for a season-high role in his absence.

Week 5 final (10/11): missed a third straight game as Jacksonville beat Philadelphia 19-17 in London on a last-second 57-yard Cam Little field goal after Philly had taken a late 17-16 lead -- Eagles fell to 2-3. Dallas Goedert (6 catches, 38 yards) and Dameon Pierce (making his 2026 debut after being activated 10/7) picked up extra work with Smith, Saquon Barkley, and Tank Bigsby all out.

UPDATE (10/14): cautiously positive signal for Week 6 vs. Carolina (Sun 10/18, home) -- RotoBaller (citing NFL Network's Mike Garafolo, 10/12) reports Smith "has a chance to return." No Wednesday practice report confirming actual participation level had posted as of this update; keeping the standard Injury tier pending that confirmation rather than upgrading to Health Watch prematurely.

SETBACK (10/14): did NOT practice Wednesday, and his designation reportedly expanded to "hamstring/toe" (Heavy.com/Yahoo) -- a real step back from HC Nick Sirianni's Monday "hopeful" framing for Sunday's game vs. Carolina. Keeping the standard Injury tier; recheck Friday's final practice report before trusting the "chance to return" framing from earlier in the week.

UPDATE (10/16): progressed from a Wednesday DNP to a limited Thursday practice (10/14-10/15), with the designation reportedly covering both hamstring and toe. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo said Smith has "a shot" to play Sunday vs. Carolina (10/18) -- a real step up from this week's earlier setback, though not yet a confirmed green light.

CLEARED (10/18): no game status on the final Week 6 injury report vs. Carolina -- the recurring hamstring (plus a newly-reported toe issue) progressed from a Wednesday DNP to limited Thursday to a full practice Friday (Philadelphia Inquirer, RotoBaller/Garafolo). First game available since Week 3. Smith himself said availability was 'up to the doctors' earlier in the week, so treat this as cleared-but-worth-watching-usage in his first game back rather than a clean bill of health. Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch. QB Jalen Hurts remains out (blood clot), with Tanner McKee starting.

Jadarian Price.name: Jadarian Price
bullets: Handled the clear early-down workload before exiting: 13 carries for 52 yards plus a catch for 8 yards in Sunday's 31-7 win at Arizona (Drew Lock starting for the injured Sam Darnold), before leaving in the second half — officially Questionable to return, then held out.
CLEARED: full practice Friday, no designation for Week 3 vs. Washington — HC Mike Macdonald confirmed the shoulder is a non-issue (SI, NBC Sports, Seahawks.com, 9/24-25).

Efficiency profile stands out even in a crowded backfield: through 2 games he ranks top-6 among qualifying RBs in explosive-run rate, top-5 in yards after contact per attempt, and top-6 in missed-tackle rate (FantasyPros) — but Zach Charbonnet (PUP/ACL) aside, Seattle is still running a real 3-way rotation with George Holani and Emanuel Wilson rather than handing Price a clean bell-cow role.

NEW (9/30): this is a recurring chest injury (originally suffered in Week 2 at Arizona, now confirmed by Seahawks PR and national reporters as chest, not the shoulder issue referenced in an earlier note) — Price was limited again in Wednesday's Week 4 practice with the same issue. He played through a full clearance into Week 3 but logged a career-low 28% snap share/6 touches (22 scrimmage yards) in that game, and now the chest is lingering into Week 4 prep vs. the Chargers. No structural/imaging concern has been reported; HC Mike Macdonald had given a positive update earlier in the cycle (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 9/30).

NEW/WORSENED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. the Chargers with the recurring chest injury, after being limited/DNP through the week. No surgery or multi-week timeline has been reported, so this stays at the standard Injury tier rather than Short-Term, pending a clearer return estimate. George Holani and Emanuel Wilson (newly added to this roster) are set to pick up the early-down work in Seattle's RB-by-committee backfield, with Zach Charbonnet still out on PUP/recovering from ACL surgery.

Caleb Williams.name: Caleb Williams
bullets: Had emerged as a fantasy-relevant weekly starter behind an improved Ben Johnson offense before the injury hit — real weekly upside as a rushing/passing dual threat.

CONFIRMED: officially ruled OUT for Week 3 vs. Philadelphia with a Grade 2 hamstring strain and did not play (0 fantasy points). Reporting pegs the expected absence at 3-4 weeks, which would also cost him Weeks 4-5 (NYJ, GB) with a Week 6 return vs. Atlanta as the earliest realistic target (SI/OnSI, Yahoo Sports, 9/27-29).

HC Ben Johnson has called him "week to week" without confirming the Week 4 questionable framing bettors are seeing — with no progress in practice participation this week, Williams should be considered questionable at best, and more likely a second-straight missed game. Keeping the Injury tag (not yet Long-Term) since the reported 3-4 week window sits just under the ~month/4-game long-term threshold, but this bears watching if it slips further.

UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to DOUBTFUL for Week 4 vs. the Jets, but this looks like a procedural downgrade rather than a sign he's rounding into game shape — the operative 3-4 week / Week 6-at-Atlanta timeline from last week's reporting has NOT been revised as of the Wednesday practice cycle (Yahoo Sports, BearGoggleson.com, ProFootballNetwork). HC Ben Johnson continues to call him "week-to-week" without confirming a Week 4 questionable framing. Treat him as unlikely to play Sunday; Case Keenum (not Tyson Bagent, who is also out) remains Chicago's starter after authoring a 247-yard, 2-TD upset of Philadelphia (27-7) on Week 3 Monday Night Football, including an 8-yard TD to Luther Burden III plus a rushing score.

CONFIRMED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. the Jets, missing a second straight game with the Grade 2 hamstring strain -- the original 3-4 week / Week 6-at-Atlanta timeline from two weeks ago has NOT been revised. Case Keenum remains Chicago's starter (SI/Betting, PrizePicks, 10/1-3).

CORRECTION + UPDATE (10/5): Chicago's Week 4 starter was Tyson Bagent, not Case Keenum as referenced in last week's note -- Bagent threw for a career-high 268 yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets (Chicago Sun-Times, Yahoo Sports, 10/4), with Kyle Monangai running for 146 yards and 2 TDs behind him (see Monangai's note). Williams (hamstring) missed a second straight game and remains "week to week" per HC Ben Johnson with no firm return date announced as of 10/5; Chicago is in no rush given Bagent's play. The original 3-4 week / Week 6-at-Atlanta timeline has still not been formally revised.

FLAGGING A DISCREPANCY (10/10): ESPN's roster status flipped from OUT to QUESTIONABLE ahead of Sunday's Week 5 game at Green Bay, but this does NOT appear to reflect a real return -- all beat reporting through Thursday (10/8) continued to describe Williams as not practicing and "week-to-week" with the Grade 2 hamstring strain, with Tyson Bagent set to start a third straight game and the Week 6-vs.-Atlanta target still the operative return expectation (RotoBaller, Athletic/Wiederer via RotoBaller, 10/5-8). Treating the QUESTIONABLE tag as a likely data/procedural artifact rather than confirmation he's playing Sunday -- recheck the Bears' actual Friday practice report before trusting it. Keeping the standard Injury tier.

CONFIRMED (10/12): missed a fourth straight game, inactive for Sunday's Week 5 loss at Green Bay (Packers won 31-7). Tyson Bagent started again and struggled (12-of-21, 87 yards, 0 TD, 2 INT, 27.4 rating, 2 sacks) before being benched in the 4th quarter for Case Keenum (11-of-19, 108 yards, 1 INT). No new return timeline reported; Week 6 vs. Atlanta remains the target, keeping the standard Injury tier.

UPDATE (10/13): real progress -- returned to a limited practice Friday (10/9) after resuming throwing drills, and The Athletic's Dan Wiederer reports Chicago never placed him on IR, keeping Week 6 vs. Atlanta (10/18) live as his target. He's still building back to full-speed running, and HC Ben Johnson is calling his return "to be determined"/benchmark-based rather than confirming he plays -- Rapoport/Pelissero flagged Week 6 or the following week (10/22 vs. NE) as the likely activation window, with no hard date set (NBC Sports, Bleacher Nation, 10/9-10).

UPDATE (10/14): trending toward a Week 6 return vs. Atlanta (Sun 10/18) but still unconfirmed by the team itself -- Ian Rapoport reported (10/12) "all signs point" to Williams playing, citing a completed strenuous pregame workout and his first limited practice since the injury (Fri 10/9). HC Ben Johnson has NOT guaranteed it, saying only that Williams would be "close." The Chicago Sun-Times (10/11) floated the team instead targeting the following week (Oct 22 vs. New England) given the short Thu turnaround after a Sunday game, calling the decision "to be determined." Keeping the standard Injury tier until an actual designation/practice grade confirms he's playing.

UPGRADE (10/14): took a full practice Wednesday, per HC Ben Johnson (Yahoo Sports/SI, BleacherNation) -- a real step up from last week's limited/estimated sessions. Johnson still won't commit to naming him the starter until closer to Sunday's game at Atlanta, but a full practice week is a strong signal he plays. Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Health Watch given the clean practice participation.

UPDATE (10/16): a full practice participant Wednesday (10/14) after missing three straight games with a Grade 2 hamstring strain -- NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports "all signs point" to Williams returning Sunday vs. Atlanta (10/18), and the Bears have moved to roughly 3-point favorites, suggesting the market expects him back. HC Ben Johnson hasn't confirmed the start, calling it "still fluid."

RETURNED AND DOMINANT (10/18): made his return from the 3-game hamstring absence in Sunday's 31-23 win at Atlanta with zero lingering effects -- went 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a TD to Colston Loveland, including a 12-of-12 start before his first incompletion. Chicago held off a 24-point Atlanta rally attempt to improve to 4-2; D'Andre Swift ran for 2 TDs (see his note). Williams said afterward his body felt great but that managing it will be "a weekly thing" (ESPN, CBS Chicago, Yahoo Sports, 10/18). Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Healthy given the clean, full-workload return; Chicago is back in action Thursday vs. New England on a short week, worth checking his practice reps given the quick turnaround.

NEW (10/8): limited at Wednesday's practice with a knee/groin issue and carries a QUESTIONABLE tag into Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington (Giants' official injury report, 10/7) -- first injury concern since signing. No severity or timeline reported yet; check Friday's final designation.

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday night's Week 5 game vs. Atlanta -- no setback from the knee/groin issue that limited him in practice this week. First clean bill of health since signing with Baltimore.

Cam Little.name: Cam Little
bullets: Jacksonville's starting kicker, known for elite leg strength on long attempts — no competition for the job.

Romeo Doubs.name: Romeo Doubs
bullets: Signed in free agency; profiles as a high-volume slot piece similar to Diggs' old role now that Diggs is gone.

PLACED ON IR (10/19-20): dove for a 42-yard go-ahead TD catch from Drake Maye in the 1st quarter of Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets and landed hard on his shoulder, first questionable to return before being ruled out; the Patriots officially placed him on injured reserve Monday (10/19), which rules him out a minimum of four games under NFL IR rules (ESPN, NBC Sports, Boston.com, Heavy.com, 10/19). No surgery has been announced and a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler the injury isn't expected to keep him out long-term -- he's hopeful to return around New England's bye in late November, with one outlet pegging Week 12 vs. the Chargers as an earliest-return target. Upgrading tag from Breakout Watch to Long-Term Injury per the official IR designation (our fixed tiering rule treats any IR stint as Long-Term regardless of the softer verbal outlook); Mack Hollins and DeMario Douglas are set to see expanded roles in New England's receiver room in the meantime.

Nico Collins.name: Nico Collins
bullets: Still a fantasy WR1 when healthy (ESPN ranks him WR10) — three straight 1,000-yard seasons, 21 TDs over that stretch — but the Grade 1 hamstring strain has now cost him back-to-back games.
CONFIRMED: officially ruled OUT for Week 3 vs. the Colts (Sunday) — his second straight missed game with the same hamstring strain (NBC Sports, Last Word on Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/25-26).

NEW: HC DeMeco Ryans said he's "hopeful" Collins is available for Week 4 vs. Dallas, and Adam Schefter reports a "decent chance" he returns, but Collins did not practice Monday and will need to show up as at least a limited participant Wednesday-Friday to have a realistic shot at playing (ESPN/Schefter, CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 9/27-29). Keeping Injury tag until he's actually back on the practice field; Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Jaylin Noel remain Houston's top three WRs in his absence.

UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Week 4 vs. Dallas. HC DeMeco Ryans said Monday (9/28) he's "hopeful"/there's a "decent chance" Collins plays, calling his rehab progress "really good" (CBS Sports, NBC Sports). The QUESTIONABLE tag implies he returned to practice in at least a limited fashion this week for the first time since the injury — a real, meaningful step, but he'll still need Thu/Fri practice participation to be considered a lock. One aggregator flagged a separate "knee (limited)" note that isn't corroborated elsewhere and should be treated with caution rather than as a new injury. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte continue to lead Houston's WR snaps/targets in his absence.

CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/2-3): officially active for Monday Night Football's Week 4 game at Dallas, ending his absence with the hamstring strain -- he told ESPN Friday "Hell yeah, I'm playing this week" and was not listed on Houston's final injury report. Downgrading tag from Injury to Healthy; this snaps him back in as Houston's clear WR1 over Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte.

Week 4 final (10/4): played in his return from the hamstring strain and caught 4 of his targets for 54 yards as Houston routed Dallas 34-10 (CBS Sports). Modest workload in the first game back -- no new injury reported, worth tracking snap/target share growth as he ramps back toward full volume in Week 5.

Jaylen Waddle.name: Jaylen Waddle
bullets: The camp hamstring strain was fully resolved for Week 1 with Denver, but the passing-game role was thin in his Broncos debut — just 1 catch for 2 yards on 3 targets as Courtland Sutton and the run game dominated the offense.
Worth monitoring whether target share improves in Week 2 now that he's fully healthy, or whether Denver's offense simply doesn't feed him volume.

Week 3 (9/27, 30-26 win over the Rams): played a full complement of snaps (~73%) but was again a non-factor in the passing game — just 2 catches on 7 targets for 10 yards, plus a 14-yard end-around carry and a 2-point conversion catch. Sutton and the run game continue to dominate Denver's offense (NBC Sports, ESPN box score).

NEW (9/30): Tracker flips ACTIVE to QUESTIONABLE after Waddle was seen leaving the stadium postgame in a walking boot on his right foot, which triggered 48 hours of speculation. Multiple outlets (NBC Sports, RotoWire, RotoBaller, Yahoo Sports/ClutchPoints, Heavy.com, all 9/29) cite team sources/beat reporting that he is "fine"/"okay" and that the boot was a routine postgame-inflammation precaution, not a structural injury — once a player is limited in practice, the injury report requires a game-status tag. No source indicates a ligament or fracture issue. Best read: trending toward playing Week 4 at San Francisco in the same complementary role.

CLEARED (9/30): the postgame walking-boot scare is fully resolved — Waddle was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, officially clearing him for Week 4 vs. San Francisco. HC Sean Payton and team sources had already downplayed the boot as a routine precautionary measure, not a structural foot/ankle issue; no diagnosis was ever confirmed (RotoBaller, Mile High Report, PrizePicks, 9/30). Role still capped by Denver's run-first offense — just 2 catches on 7 targets for 10 yards in Week 3.

Week 4 final (10/4): Denver fell to San Francisco 24-14 (Broncos to 2-2). Waddle caught 5 of 6 targets for 35 yards and his first TD as a Bronco (a 13-yard score with a 2-point conversion that cut the deficit to 17-14) -- but was otherwise quiet, targeted on roughly 16% of his routes for a third time in four games. Denver's run-first, Bo Nix-led offense still isn't feeding him consistent volume despite the touchdown (NBC Sports, Mile High Report, CBS Sports, 10/4).

Cam Skattebo.name: Cam Skattebo
bullets: Fully cleared from last year's gruesome rookie ankle injury (dislocation + open fracture) and confirmed as the Giants' Week 1 starting RB over Tyrone Tracy Jr., hosting Dallas on Sunday Night Football.

Held to just 12 carries for 36 yards, 4 catches for 19 yards, and a lost fumble in Monday night's 28-6 loss at the Rams — the whole Giants game plan was wrecked after QB Jaxson Dart left with a knee injury on the first series (182 total team yards); treat the poor box score as game-script-driven, not a role change (RotoWire, CBS Sports).

NEW (10/8): limited at Wednesday's practice with a shoulder issue, officially QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington (Giants' injury report, 10/7) -- distinct from last year's season-ending ankle fracture/dislocation. No word yet on severity or workload impact pending Friday's report.

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington -- cleared the shoulder issue that limited him in back-to-back Wednesday/Thursday practices after opening the week in a non-contact jersey. On track for his usual workhorse workload (bolavip, NBC Sports Fantasy, 10/7-9).

Week 5 final (10/11): played through the shoulder issue with no setback -- 13 carries for 59 yards plus 2 catches for 12 yards (40 of his 71 scrimmage yards came in overtime) in a 27-27 tie at Washington. Costly moment: fumbled at the Washington 24-yard line late in OT with the Giants in range for a potential game-winning field goal. No injury fallout reported from the game; remains the clear starter.

D'Andre Swift.name: D'Andre Swift
bullets: Chicago's clear RB1 in Ben Johnson's scheme.

The Sept 3 practice scare was cramping, not a leg injury, and it showed no lingering effect — torched Carolina for 18 carries, 124 yards and 3 TDs (plus a catch) in Sunday's 59-37 win, arguably his best game as a Bear.

The Week 2 knee/ankle concern is resolved — logged a full practice Friday (9/18) and was removed from Chicago's injury report entirely, carrying no designation into Sunday's game at Minnesota (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, 9/18).

NEW (10/1-2): popped up on Chicago's Week 4 injury report as a non-participant Thursday with a knee injury — a new issue, not a recurrence of the earlier cramping/knee-ankle scares. He was off the Wednesday walkthrough report and had just carried 20 times for 84 yards in Chicago's prior game, so beat writers flagged the sudden Thursday DNP as worth watching; no designation confirmed yet pending Friday's report, with hope he's a full go Sunday vs. the Jets (Chicago Sun-Times, Bleacher Nation, 10/1-2).

CLEARED (10/3): the Thursday DNP knee scare did not linger -- Swift practiced fully later in the week and carries no designation into Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Jets, remaining Chicago's unquestioned RB1. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

NEW (10/4): fumbled in the 3rd quarter of Chicago's 23-12 Week 4 win over the Jets and did not return, finishing with 15 carries for 58 yards and 2 catches for 16 yards; was seen limping postgame with soreness in the same knee that had been a minor pregame concern. HC Ben Johnson did not frame it as a benching. Kyle Monangai (see his note) took over and torched the Jets for 146 yards/2 TD on 30 carries in relief. No official injury designation or severity reported yet as of 10/5-6 -- downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending clarity; Chicago's Week 5 backfield split is worth watching since both backs picked up bumps in the same game (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Bleacher Nation, Heavy.com, 10/4).

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Green Bay -- the hip/knee issue that kept him out of Wednesday's practice resolved by Friday. Remains Chicago's lead back; downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

Bryce Young.name: Bryce Young
bullets: Legitimate early-season breakout: 6 total TDs (passing) against just 1 INT through two 2026 games, averaging 8.9 yards per attempt, with a 34-3 Week 2 rout of Atlanta headlined by a 23-of-36, 287-yard, 3-TD, 0-INT line (116.3 rating).

Became the second QB in Panthers history with multiple TD passes in each of the team's first two games (joining Jake Delhomme in 2007); new OC Brad Idzik's scheme change is being credited by beat writers as a real driver of the improvement, not just matchup variance.

Worth monitoring for regression given a small sample and the difficulty of NFL defenses adjusting, but two clean, efficient starts is a real signal after a rocky first three pro seasons (ESPN, Yahoo Sports).

49ers D/ST.name: 49ers D/ST
bullets: Fringe top-10 pass rush anchored by Nick Bosa, though the unit ranks closer to the middle of the pack (~20th) in preseason fantasy defense rankings — streaming-caliber if the front seven stays healthy.
Added off waivers with no notable injury or personnel news to report.

Mike Evans.name: Mike Evans
bullets: Monday (9/21) update: Shanahan said the hip "will have to be managed this week" and Evans would likely miss some practice time. Turns 33 in August — an aging watch item independent of any single-week injury.

UPDATE: exited Week 3's loss to Arizona early in the 2nd quarter with a rib injury after a hard hit from S Budda Baker on a middle-of-the-field catch — was carted off and did not return, finishing with 3 catches for 34 yards and a TD before leaving (ESPN, CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/27-28).

Downgrading tag from Aging-Watch-only injury risk to Health Watch: Evans returned to practice Friday and is officially Questionable for Week 4 vs. Denver, with HC Kyle Shanahan indicating optimism that he'll play (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Last Word on Sports, 9/26-29). Treat as a game-time-decision-caliber Questionable, not a real absence risk at this point.

CLEARED (10/5): the rib strain suffered vs. Arizona in Week 3 is behind him -- today's status flip from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE confirms he's cleared the issue that had him day-to-day. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to reflect no current injury; turns 33 in August remains a standalone long-term watch item (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Last Word on Sports).

UPDATE (10/8): the Week 3 rib injury remains a recurring game-status item -- Evans played through it in Week 4 (76 yards, NBC Sports, 10/4) and is again QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Denver; Forbes' fantasy injury roundup (10/7) described it as 'not overly serious' at this point, consistent with his pattern of limited practice reps but suiting up.

CORRECTION + CLEARED (10/10): last week's note misstated San Francisco's Week 5 opponent as Denver -- the 49ers actually play Seattle in Week 5. Evans was upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's game vs. the Seahawks; he was limited in Wednesday's practice with the recurring rib issue (NBC Sports Fantasy, 10/7) but cleared by Friday, continuing the pattern of playing through this injury each of the last two weeks.

DELIVERED (10/13): no setback from the rib -- caught 7 passes for 113 yards and a TD, plus a 2-point conversion, in San Francisco's 32-29 win over Seattle on Sunday 10/11, pushing the 49ers to 5-0 (ESPN box score, gameId 401872992). Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean workload and no re-aggravation; remains SF's clear top receiving weapon alongside Deebo Samuel (who left the same game with a hamstring injury -- see his note).

NEW (10/15-16): HC Kyle Shanahan said Evans will not practice Thursday due to Achilles soreness, on top of the recurring rib issue he's played through in recent weeks; his status for Monday night's Week 6 home game vs. Washington (10/19) is in question. With Deebo Samuel Sr. also out (hamstring, see his note), Jacob Cowing, Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins would see larger roles if Evans sits too. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch given the fresh soreness and missed practice; no multi-week framing reported, treat as day-to-day pending Friday's practice report.

EXITED (10/19): left Monday night's 23-17 win over Washington before halftime with right Achilles soreness after leading all receivers with 3 catches for 94 yards; did not return. HC Kyle Shanahan described it as Achilles tendonitis and said he didn't believe further imaging was needed, and beat reporter Jennifer Lee Chan reports the tendon is intact -- he's expected to miss "a little time," with speculation his return could line up around San Francisco's Week 8 bye (ESPN, NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, 10/19-20). Revising tag from Health Watch to Short-Term Injury given the relatively optimistic, tendon-intact framing, but his Sunday vs. Atlanta status is unconfirmed as of this update -- some analysts expect SF to rest him given the upcoming bye. Deebo Samuel Sr. remains out separately (hamstring, see his note), so a Niners WR room already thin would thin further if Evans also sits.

Pat Freiermuth.name: Pat Freiermuth
bullets: NEW (10/18): added to Pittsburgh's injury report late in the week with a calf issue and carried a QUESTIONABLE tag into Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Tampa Bay, alongside DK Metcalf's own (since-cleared) illness scare (Yahoo Sports, sportsnetpittsburgh, 10/17-18). His specific playing status/usage in Sunday's 26-19 OT win over the Buccaneers could not be confirmed via search as of this update -- DK Metcalf (11 catches, 93 yards) and Germie Bernard (11 catches) combined to dominate Pittsburgh's receiving game, which could mean a lighter role for Freiermuth even if he suited up. Recheck the next report to confirm he's clear of the calf issue.

WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): played through the calf issue with a light workload -- 2 catches for 11 yards on 3 targets in the 26-19 OT win over Tampa Bay, with DK Metcalf (11-93) and Germie Bernard (game-winning TD, 11 catches/87 yards) dominating the receiving game as expected (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports box score, 10/18). No setback reported. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean clearance, though his real-world role remains a distant complementary piece behind Metcalf and Bernard.

Alvin Kamara.name: Alvin Kamara
bullets: Made his 2026 season debut in Week 2 (24-17 win over Baltimore) after missing the entire preseason and Week 1 with a sprained MCL; efficiency was underwhelming in the opener back — 9 carries for 15 yards, plus 5 catches (6 targets) for 7 yards.

Split early-down work with Travis Etienne Jr., whose role changed noticeably once Kamara returned to the lineup; expect a committee approach in New Orleans' backfield for now rather than a clear bell-cow role.
Profiles as a low-end RB3/flex for Week 3 vs. the Raiders on PPR volume alone, but the explosive-play juice from his pre-injury form hasn't shown up yet (CBS Sports).

UPDATE (9/30): with Travis Etienne Jr. now out with a hamstring injury (see Etienne's note), Kamara becomes New Orleans' clear early-down/passing-down workhorse near-term rather than a committee piece — upgrading the tag from Committee to Workhorse Lock while Etienne is sidelined. Kendre Miller/CJ Donaldson are the only complementary depth behind him (SI/Saints, NBC Sports, atozsports.com, 9/27-29).
UPDATE (10/5-6): scored 3 TDs in New Orleans' Monday night win over Atlanta, reinforcing his status as the clear lead back with Travis Etienne Jr. still on IR (CBS Sports, 10/5-6).

NEW (10/8): did not practice Wednesday with a back injury and is a real question mark for Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Minnesota (Saints' official injury report via Canal Street Chronicles, 10/7) -- a new issue, not the rib history from past seasons. With Travis Etienne Jr. still on IR, a Kamara absence would push touches to Kendre Miller (and possibly rookie CJ Donaldson).

CLEARED (10/12): played through the back injury in Sunday's Week 5 home loss to Minnesota (Saints fell 13-23, held to just 142 total yards on offense); specific carry/yardage totals for Kamara could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update. Remains New Orleans' clear lead back with Travis Etienne Jr. still on IR.

UPDATE (10/16): logged a second straight limited practice Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the back injury; no formal game designation yet, but outlets project him active Sunday at the Giants (10/18). Backup Kendre Miller logged 10 carries and a TD in Week 5 and would be the clear early-down beneficiary again if Kamara's back limits him further (see Miller's note).

WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): played through the back injury with no issue in New Orleans' 34-27 win over the Giants -- 7 carries for 34 yards plus 2 catches for 35 yards, including a 31-yard TD reception, and the game pushed him past 5,000 career scrimmage yards (NFL.com, 10/18). Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; remains New Orleans' clear lead back with Travis Etienne Jr. still on IR.

Jaylen Warren.name: Jaylen Warren
bullets: Confirmed as Pittsburgh's Week 1 RB1 over Rico Dowdle, and it held up in the box score — out-touched Dowdle 15-10 in the Week 1 win, the more involved back in both the run and pass game. Signed a 2-year extension through 2027 (~$17.5M total, $12M guaranteed) in September 2025.

CLEARED: played through the shoulder issue and delivered Pittsburgh's clear workhorse performance in Sunday's Week 3 win vs. Cincinnati with Dowdle (toe) out — a season-high workload (48 total touches through 3 games, headlined by a big Week 3 day) confirms him as the unquestioned RB1 for as long as Dowdle is sidelined (NBC Sports, 9/27).
Rookie 7th-rounder Eli Heidenreich or Travis Homer remain the only backup options behind him.

NEW (10/1): produced 17 carries for 93 yards plus 3 catches for 33 yards in Thursday Night Football's Week 4 loss at Cleveland (27-24) with Dowdle again out — his third straight game as Pittsburgh's clear lead back, continuing the workhorse role with no sign of a committee forming.

Jahmyr Gibbs.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
bullets: No lingering back/hamstring issue — exploded for 29 carries, 156 yards and 2 TDs plus 5 catches for 30 yards in Sunday's opener, the clear workhorse with Montgomery gone and Isiah Pacheco on IR.

Ground game was quiet in Thursday night's loss to Buffalo (52 yards on 16 carries), but 6 catches and a receiving TD kept his fantasy floor strong — a reminder his receiving work is what makes him a true 3-down workhorse even on an off day rushing.

Colston Loveland.name: Colston Loveland
bullets: Moore's departure opens a big target vacuum; Bears leaning into more 13-personnel — projected ~78 rec/918 yds/7 TD after closing his rookie year red-hot.
2025 1st-round pick (10th overall, Michigan).

UPDATE: Chicago's passing game is now working through journeyman Case Keenum after Caleb Williams' hamstring injury (out at least through Week 5) and Tyson Bagent's own unavailability — Keenum threw for 247 yards and 2 TD in Week 3's 27-7 upset of Philadelphia (9/28). Monitor target share/efficiency with a backup-caliber passer under center for the next several weeks.

Josh Jacobs.name: Josh Jacobs
bullets: Pleaded no contest Sept 10 to misdemeanor battery and criminal-damage charges from the May incident — fined $1,000 plus costs, with the damage charge to be dismissed after a 12-month deferred agreement.

The legal resolution does NOT end his NFL absence: he remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List (can't practice, play, or be on the 53-man roster, though he's paid and can attend meetings/individual workouts) while a separate personal-conduct-policy review continues. Sources still peg the likely suspension range at 4-6 games once announced, with games missed on the exempt list expected to count toward it.

Pleaded no contest Sept 10 in Brown County to the misdemeanor battery charge (found guilty, $1,000 fine + costs) with a 12-month deferred-judgment agreement on the property-damage charge. As of 9/26, the NFL STILL has not announced an official suspension length — reporting indicates the league is navigating legal barriers (a court-ordered bar on releasing video evidence) before finalizing discipline, with the standard 6-game domestic-violence-related baseline still the working estimate (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, ProFootballRumors, 9/24-26).

Green Bay has already hedged, trading a 2028 6th-round pick to Pittsburgh for RB Kaleb Johnson as depth-chart insurance — a real sign the team isn't banking on a quick Jacobs return. Treat him as unplayable/bench for now.

UPDATE (10/6): still no change -- the NFL has NOT announced an official suspension length. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List (confirmed still inactive for Green Bay's Week 4 game vs. Tampa Bay on 10/4). Speculation on the eventual suspension length now ranges from 4-6 games (ESPN's Jeremy Fowler) up to as many as 8 games (NFL Network's Ian Rapoport), still unconfirmed either way. The video-evidence dispute delaying the league's review is still unresolved -- a judge recently declined to permanently seal the incident video on procedural grounds (NBC Sports/PFT, ~10/1-2) -- and Jacobs' next court hearing isn't until Nov. 17, well past several more game weeks. Any time already spent on the Exempt List would count toward an eventual suspension. Green Bay's Kaleb Johnson depth-chart plan is unchanged; still unplayable/bench.

UPDATE (10/13): still no official suspension length announced. HC Matt LaFleur said ahead of Green Bay's Week 6 game at Dallas that he has no word from the league on timing. Reporting still pegs a likely 4-6 game range (6-game baseline for a first battery offense, reducible for mitigating factors), with exempt-list time possibly counting toward it (ProFootballRumors, Yahoo Sports, 10/9-10). Still unplayable/bench.

UPDATE (10/14): still no suspension length officially announced -- HC Matt LaFleur reiterated he has no word yet from the league on timing (AcmePackingCompany/Yardbarker, 10/12-13). This remains a Personal Conduct Policy matter (a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery/criminal damage to property stemming from a May domestic incident), not a PED case. A court fight over releasing police video/records from that incident is reportedly ongoing and may be delaying the league's final ruling (Rolling Out, 10/14). He'll miss a 6th straight game Sunday vs. Dallas. Green Bay's backfield without him: MarShawn Lloyd leads with 40 carries/112 yards/2 TD this season, with Kaleb Johnson (27/106) and Chris Brooks also involved -- Green Bay's run game ranks last in the NFL in his absence.

UPDATE (10/16): filed a civil suit Wednesday (10/15) seeking to restrict public access to records tied to the May incident, as the Commissioner's Exempt List review continues -- no suspension length has been announced yet, and this remains a Personal Conduct Policy matter, not a physical injury (our roster feed's "DAY_TO_DAY" status field reflects the exempt-list/legal situation, not an actual injury). Still unplayable/bench; MarShawn Lloyd remains Green Bay's lead back for Sunday Night Football vs. Dallas (10/18).

EXEMPT LIST LIFTED (10/16-19): the NFL announced it is removing Jacobs from the Commissioner's Exempt List effective Monday (10/19), clearing him to practice and play again starting with Green Bay's Week 7 game (Sun. 10/25) -- missing the first six games of the season in the process. The Personal Conduct Policy investigation into his misdemeanor battery/property-damage case continues separately, and the league has not ruled out an eventual suspension, but for now he is expected to be available to the Packers (AP, Newsweek, NY1, 10/16-19). MarShawn Lloyd has been Green Bay's lead back in his absence and figures to continue sharing work even once Jacobs is back; still a wait-and-see Depth Chart Battle until he actually suits up.

Patrick Mahomes.name: Patrick Mahomes
bullets: The lingering "knee" injury-report notation from his offseason ACL/LCL recovery was a non-factor in Kansas City's Week 1 win over Denver — went 15/27 for 184 yards and 2 passing TDs (1 INT) and added 7 carries for 23 yards and a rushing TD.

Michael Wilson.name: Michael Wilson
bullets: Broke out as the overall WR10 in PPR last year (78/1,006/7); locked in as the Z-receiver in new OC Mike LaFleur's scheme with projected 110-120 targets — camp reports have him looking sharper than Marvin Harrison Jr. so far.

UPDATE (10/16): with Marvin Harrison Jr. now traded to Houston (see his note), beat reporting (KOLD, KSAT, Fox10 Phoenix) frames Wilson as Arizona's new top receiving option, with Kendrick Bourne as the secondary outside piece (see his note). Expect a real target-share bump starting Week 6 vs. the Rams (10/18), though it's not yet reflected in a box score.

Ka'imi Fairbairn.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
bullets: Veteran incumbent, Houston's clear starting kicker with no camp competition reported.

Chris Olave.name: Chris Olave
bullets: Played through the minor hamstring issue with no setback — caught 8 of 10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-17 win over Baltimore, giving him an 18-268-1 line on 23 targets through two games as the Saints' clear top downfield target.

Torched Detroit for 10/182 in the Week 1 opener; the Thursday-emergent hamstring tag never became a real threat — Adam Schefter and Saints beat reporters expected him to play all week, and that's exactly what happened.

NEW (10/8): showed up on New Orleans' Thursday injury report as limited -- the Saints' own report ties it to a veteran rest day, while other outlets describe a lingering foot/knee issue; reporting is inconsistent on the cause. He remains the Saints' clear top target (18 targets through 2 full games, torched Detroit for 10/182 in the opener) and isn't expected to miss Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Minnesota, but worth confirming Friday's final designation (Yahoo Sports/Saints beat, 10/8).

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Minnesota -- the limited-practice issue from Thursday (reporting was split between a vet rest day and a lingering foot/knee issue) resolved without missing a game. Remains New Orleans' clear top target earner; downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

NEW (10/16): missed back-to-back practices Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15) with an illness -- not a new soft-tissue injury -- ahead of Sunday's Week 6 game at the Giants (10/18). RotoWire (10/16) expects no worse than a Questionable tag if he can't practice Friday; illness-based absences typically clear by gameday. Downgrading from Healthy to Health Watch pending final confirmation.

WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): the illness that limited his practice Wednesday/Thursday was a non-issue by gameday -- caught an 18-yard TD from Tyler Shough in New Orleans' 34-27 win over the Giants (NFL.com, PFF, 10/18), remaining the Saints' clear top target earner. Downgrading tag back to Healthy.

De'Von Achane.name: De'Von Achane
bullets: No current injury flag entering Week 3, but missed time each of the last two seasons plus offseason shoulder surgery — the durability risk flagged all along showed up again.

Suffered a non-contact knee injury on a 1st-quarter run vs. Kansas City in Week 3 (9/27), tackled awkwardly by a Chiefs defender, and was ruled out for the rest of the game; HC Jeff Hafley said postgame the outlook "does not sound very optimistic."

CONFIRMED SEASON-ENDING: Monday's MRI (9/28) confirmed a torn ACL in the left knee. Miami placed him on IR and he will have surgery, ending his 2026 season just months after signing a 4-yr/$64M extension (CBS Sports, ESPN, RotoWire, Yahoo Sports, 9/28). Upgrading tag from Injury to Long-Term Injury to reflect the confirmed season-ending diagnosis — drop him in all non-dynasty/non-IR-stash formats.

Vikings D/ST.name: Vikings D/ST
bullets: Through 2 games: 8 sacks (tied for most in the NFL), 4 takeaways, and the league's highest pressure rate (50.6%) — ranked the No. 6 fantasy defense entering Week 3 (Yahoo Sports/PFN, Sportsnaut, ~9/2026).
Held Chicago to 297 total yards and zero TDs in Week 2, with 4 sacks and 2 takeaways — a second straight game with that exact sack/takeaway line.
Minor injury watch: DL Jalen Redmond (elbow) and DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (oblique) were limited in Week 3 practice, but no starters were ruled out as of this week's report (SI/OnSI, 9/23).

Juwan Johnson.name: Juwan Johnson
bullets: Newly added off waivers — has emerged as New Orleans' clear TE1 in Kellen Moore's up-tempo offense, out-snapping backup Noah Fant 76-37 in Week 2.

Ranks TE7 in fantasy points per game through 2 weeks (10.6+ PPR points in each game): 3/54/1 TD in the Week 1 OT loss to Detroit, then 4 catches in Week 2 — a 12.2% target share with 4 red-zone targets (FantasyData, RotoBaller, FantasyPros).
Comes off a strong 2025 finish (77 catches/889 yards/3 TD, 102 targets) once Tyler Shough took over at QB — the current volume looks like a continuation of that role, not a one-game blip.

Jared Goff.name: Jared Goff
bullets: No injury designation — fully healthy through 3 games (Fox Sports injury tracker).

Week 3 vs. NYJ (31-24 win): 25/32 for 269 yards and 2 TD (4-yard to Amon-Ra St. Brown, 11-yard game-winner to Jahmyr Gibbs in the final two minutes), plus 4 carries for 6 yards (CBS Sports, FantasyPros, RotoWire, 9/27). Roughly 802 yards, 8 TD, 0 INT on the season — solid, mistake-free form and a straightforward streaming/starter option.

Kendre Miller.name: Kendre Miller
bullets: NEW (10/16): led New Orleans' Week 5 backfield with 10 carries and a rushing TD (10/12) while Alvin Kamara was limited in practice this week with a back issue (see Kamara's note). TheFantasyFootballers flags Miller as the likely early-down beneficiary again Sunday at the Giants (10/18) if Kamara's back lingers.

Patriots D/ST.name: Patriots D/ST
bullets: Top-10 fantasy finish in 2025, but that leaned on a soft schedule; added Dre'Mont Jones, Kevin Byard, and a 2nd-round pick. Real talent additions, but a much tougher 2026 slate makes them a regression candidate off last year's ranking.

Javonte Williams.name: Javonte Williams
bullets: New 3-yr/$24M deal after a career year: 252 att, 1,201 yds, 11 TD.
Backups Davis, Blue, and Mafah are unproven; Dallas' history of a 2-RB rotation still leaves him high touch security.

Ladd McConkey.name: Ladd McConkey
bullets: Played through the Week 1 rib injury (suffered on a hit from Mack Wilson vs. Arizona) in Sunday's Week 2 win over the Raiders, wearing a flak jacket for protection — caught 4 of 6 targets for 39 yards and a TD in the 31-14 win.
No setback or re-aggravation reported; the rib did not limit his workload and he remains the Chargers' clear top target earner.

NEW (9/30): the earlier rib injury is long resolved (he was fully cleared off the injury report for Week 3), but McConkey popped up on the Week 4 injury report with a separate, new foot injury — limited in Wednesday's practice. No MRI, surgery, or multi-week timeline has been reported yet; beat coverage (Chargers.com, NBC Sports, ClutchPoints) frames Thursday/Friday practice as the deciding factor for Sunday's game at Seattle, with nothing suggesting a severe issue (9/30).

WORSENED (10/4-5): did play Week 4 at Seattle, but the foot injury flared up in the first half and he was downgraded from "questionable to return" to officially out, finishing with 0 catches on 2 targets (NBC Sports, 10/4). HC Jim Harbaugh called him "week-to-week" with the same foot injury in Monday's presser (RotoWire, CBS Sports, FantasyFootballers, 10/5) -- the SAME foot issue first flagged 9/30, not a new injury, but clearly worse than last week's minor framing. No Wednesday practice report yet as of today; bumping tag from Health Watch to Injury given the real doubt now attached to his Week 5 availability.

UPDATE (10/10): remains in the Chargers' Week 5 injury mix with the lingering foot injury first flagged 9/30 and worsened in Week 4; HC Jim Harbaugh's "week-to-week" framing from Monday had not been updated with a firm practice report via search as of Friday. Teammate Quentin Johnston was confirmed OUT for Sunday's game vs. Denver (see his note), which would put extra pressure on McConkey's snaps if he plays through it.

Week 5 final (10/11-12): technically active but played zero offensive snaps in the Chargers' 23-17 loss to Denver, with the lingering foot injury clearly still a real limiter despite no official game-day inactive designation. HC Jim Harbaugh said Monday (10/12) McConkey will keep working into practice ahead of Week 6 vs. Kansas City (Sun 10/18); no firmer return signal beyond that has surfaced yet. Keeping the standard Injury tier.

UPDATE (10/16): limited in practice both Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the foot injury -- a step up from the zero offensive snaps he played in Week 5 (active but essentially an emergency-only option). HC Jim Harbaugh said early in the week it was only "possible" he returns to full practice; trending toward another Questionable tag for Sunday vs. Kansas City (10/18), with no official Friday grade confirmed yet.

CLEARED (10/18): ESPN's Adam Schefter reported McConkey has no injury designation for Sunday night's Week 6 game vs. Kansas City, and our roster tracker confirms ACTIVE -- a real step up after he played zero offensive snaps in Week 5 despite being active. The recurring foot injury had him limited in practice through Wednesday/Thursday this week per HC Jim Harbaugh, so treat his workload as worth confirming early in the game rather than assuming an immediate return to full volume. Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch.

NEW INJURY -- CONCUSSION (10/18): a different issue from the foot problem that dogged him in recent weeks -- ruled out early in the 2nd quarter of a 22-6 loss at Kansas City after his head hit the turf on a tackle, finishing with just 1 catch for 17 yards (ESPN, Yahoo Sports, 10/18). Concussion-protocol timelines are inherently unpredictable and no return estimate has been reported, but the Chargers are on their Week 7 bye (next game Nov. 1 at the Rams), which gives him a real runway to clear protocol before it costs him a game. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the new, distinct injury and genuine uncertainty; Quentin Johnston and KeAndre Lambert-Smith are the top receiving options in LA's banged-up WR room if he's still out Week 8.

Keaton Mitchell.name: Keaton Mitchell
bullets: Explosive change-of-pace back for the Chargers, but Omarion Hampton is the clear RB1 on the current depth chart; Mitchell has a slight edge over Kimani Vidal for the No. 2 job behind him, per Chargers.com and Yahoo Sports.
Weak as a receiver out of the backfield, which caps his standalone fantasy value to a change-of-pace/big-play role in a Hampton-led committee rather than a real workload threat.

NEW (9/30): limited in Wednesday's Week 4 practice with an ankle injury and was seen afterward in a walking boot, though he told reporters he was "ok." Beat/fantasy coverage frames logging a limited Wednesday session as a good sign he's trending toward playing Sunday at Seattle, with two more practice windows to upgrade; no structural diagnosis reported. Kimani Vidal would be next man up behind Omarion Hampton if Mitchell can't go (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, DraftSharks, 9/30).

CLEARED (10/3): the ankle issue resolved without a setback -- logged full practice sessions after Wednesday's limited session and carries no designation into Sunday's game at Seattle. Removing Health Watch tag; still a change-of-pace role behind Omarion Hampton with Kimani Vidal as the other depth option.

Christian McCaffrey.name: Christian McCaffrey
bullets: Full workhorse usage in the opener with no ill effects from the calf scare: 10 carries for 68 yards plus 5 catches for 20 yards in the win over the Rams.
Held out of the end zone, but the touch volume is exactly what you want to see after last year's injury history.

HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed this week the Week 1 split with rookie Kaelon Black (who out-carried him 14-10, 44% of snaps) was a deliberate plan to lighten McCaffrey's load: "That was the goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more... love taking some off Christian." Total touches were even (15-15), but expect Black to keep chipping into the carry share.

A.J. Brown.name: A.J. Brown
bullets: Left his Patriots debut early in the 3rd quarter of the Sept 9 NFL Kickoff Game (a 13-10 loss to Seattle) with a right ankle injury after Seahawks CB Nehemiah Pritchett's knee landed on his ankle; had 3 catches for 26 yds on 4 targets before exiting.

Thursday's (Sept 10) MRI confirmed a high-ankle sprain (Tuesday-night X-rays had been negative). Confirmed Sept 11 (AP): Patriots are placing him on injured reserve, officially ruling him out a minimum of four games under IR roster rules — New England is also signing DT DaQuan Jones as a separate roster move. Treat him as unplayable through at least Week 4.

Arrived via trade from PHI (Patriots sent Philadelphia a 2028 1st-round pick and a 2027 5th-round pick); signed for up to $112.75M with $32.75M guaranteed. Was stepping into a wide-open target share atop New England's WR room before the injury.

ACTIVATED AND RETURNED (10/18): activated off injured reserve and made his Patriots home debut in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets, ending a 4-game absence with the high-ankle sprain suffered in his Sept. 9 Patriots debut. The return was rusty -- just 3 catches for 27 yards on 9 targets with multiple drops, plus a muffed-onside-kick mishap his teammates covered for (Boston Globe, NESN, 10/18-19). Drake Maye (3 TD passes, 0 INT) carried New England's offense in the win; expect Brown's role/rapport to build gradually. Downgrading tag from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch now that he's actually back on the field.

MANAGED, NOT A SETBACK (10/20-21): limited at Monday's walkthrough and Tuesday's practice with the same high-ankle sprain he returned from last week, but this reads as short-week load management rather than a new issue -- Brown told reporters he's "absolutely" ready for Thursday night's Week 7 game at the Bears, and HC Mike Vrabel and Brown himself both describe the ankle as not a lingering concern (ESPN's Mike Reiss, Heavy.com, Athlon, 10/20). Keeping Health Watch; today's QUESTIONABLE game-status flip is expected to clear by Thursday's kickoff.

Derrick Henry.name: Derrick Henry
bullets: Turns 32; 2025 was still elite (1,595 yds / 16 TD) with no decline signs yet, but a new play-caller and remade O-line add real variance this year.

Showed zero decline signs in the Week 1 opener vs. Indianapolis: 24 carries for 144 yards and 3 rushing TDs (35.3 fantasy pts) as Baltimore's clear lead back, with only Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali behind him on the depth chart.

Week 2 usage raised a flag: 16 carries for 68 yards and a TD plus 3 catches for 19 yards in the loss to New Orleans, but no explosive runs (long of 8 yards) and he was "puzzlingly" limited to just 5 carries in the second half even while Baltimore led — worth monitoring, not yet a confirmed workload cut (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Baltimore Beatdown).

UPDATE: bounced back from the Week 2 workload dip — went for 89 yards and 2 TD on the ground in Baltimore's wild 34-31 win over Dallas in Brazil (Week 3, 9/27), reaffirming the workhorse role with no lingering effects from the light second-half usage two weeks ago.

Week 4 (10/4): Baltimore beat Tennessee 24-18, but Henry was reportedly held in check by the Titans' run defense per a CBS Sports recap headline ("Derrick Henry shut down") -- the exact carry/yardage total could not be independently confirmed via box score due to source access limits, so treat this as a quiet, below-his-standard game rather than a new injury or role concern. Worth a follow-up once a clean box score is available.

Zay Flowers.name: Zay Flowers
bullets: Missed Week 2 vs. New Orleans with the recurring hamstring injury (first tweaked in a Week 1 TD catch-and-run, aggravated further in that same game).

CLEARED AND DELIVERED: active and effective in Sunday's Week 3 win over Dallas in Rio — 5 catches on 6 targets for 84 yards plus a 20-yard carry, turning half his touches into 20+ yard gains, including a 27-yard catch with time expiring that set up the game-winning field goal (NBC Sports, 9/27).
No re-aggravation reported; the hamstring concern appears fully resolved with a full workload back in hand — Flowers projects back into his lead-receiver role for Baltimore.

NEW (9/30): flipped back to a game-status designation (limited practice) as Baltimore continues managing the same hamstring that had him on a "pitch count" through Week 3's 5-catch, 84-yard game. HC Jesse Minter said Monday he expects Flowers to carry a full workload Week 4 vs. Tennessee; FantasyPros projects him roughly 79% likely to play with no new setback reported (NBC Sports, RotoWire, FantasyPros, 9/29-30).

CLEARED (10/1-2): upgraded from limited to a full practice participant Thursday, officially shaking the hamstring designation ahead of Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Tennessee — full workload expected as Baltimore's lead receiver (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, 10/1-2).

NEW DESIGNATION (10/2-3): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag again this week, but this reads as routine hamstring management rather than a new setback -- HC Jesse Minter said Flowers is "coming out of this thing really ready to push to be back in there closer to full time," and multiple outlets (RotoBaller, FantasyPros) are calling him a must-start WR1 Sunday vs. the 0-3 Titans if there's no in-week change. Watch Friday's final report, but treat this as a likely-to-play Questionable, not a real doubt.

Entered Week 4 off a full Thursday practice with no setback, and OC/staff expected him to carry a full workload vs. Tennessee after Baltimore's win (team reports, 10/1). No new injury or designation has surfaced since; treating the hamstring issue as resolved and upgrading tag to Healthy as Baltimore's lead receiver. (Exact Week 4 box-score line could not be independently confirmed via search -- sourcing on the Ravens-Titans final was inconsistent.)

UPDATE (10/8): the recurring hamstring issue produced another QUESTIONABLE tag -- Flowers was downgraded in Baltimore's final Week 4 injury report (questionable vs. Tennessee) and now carries the same designation into Sunday's Week 5 game at Atlanta as the team continues managing his workload week to week. No new injury or setback reported, just the same ongoing hamstring maintenance pattern.

UPDATE (10/13): flipped from QUESTIONABLE back to ACTIVE. Pregame reporting had him questionable with a foot issue (distinct wording from the recurring hamstring, possibly just reporting inconsistency) but ESPN's Adam Schefter said he was expected to play Sunday night at Atlanta; Lamar Jackson (ankle) was out for that game with Tyler Huntley starting (see Jackson's note). Could not independently confirm the final score or Flowers' box-score line for that game via search as of this update -- treating today's ACTIVE flip as a likely no-new-designation reset for Week 6 rather than confirmed proof the hamstring is fully behind him. Recheck next cycle for the actual Week 5 result.

Week 5 final (10/11): quiet by his standards but heavy volume -- 8 catches on 9 targets for 53 yards plus a 13-yard carry in Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win over Atlanta (Tyler Huntley started for the injured Lamar Jackson and scored the winning TD). No touchdown, and his longest catch went for just 12 yards -- a 26-yard grab on the late game-tying drive was wiped out by a defensive pass-interference penalty drawn in his favor. No new injury reported.

NEW (10/15-16): added to Baltimore's Week 6 injury report with a toe injury, limited in both Thursday and Friday practice -- but no game designation on the final report, so he's good to play Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. Cleveland (10/18) per NBC Sports (10/16). Lamar Jackson's ankle (see his note) remains the bigger question mark for the Baltimore offense.
