CONFIRMED (10/18): today's QUESTIONABLE-to-ACTIVE flip matches what was already being reported -- the toe injury produced no game designation on Baltimore's final Week 6 report (NBC Sports, 10/16), so he's playing Sunday's home game vs. Cleveland at full workload as Baltimore's lead receiver. Lamar Jackson (ankle) is the bigger question for the passing game, now officially OUT (see his note) with Tyler Huntley starting.

DJ Moore.name: DJ Moore
bullets: Confirmed trade (official March 11, 2026, roster move finalized Aug 17): Bears sent Moore plus a 2026 5th-round pick to Buffalo for a 2026 2nd-round pick. Bills guaranteed $15.5M of his 2028 salary, and the trade also guaranteed his 2027 salary — reshapes the WR room alongside Shakir.
Followed a strong Week 1 (21.0 fantasy pts) with a scary exit from Thursday night's Week 2 win over Detroit (AC joint sprain), but the injury turned out to be minor.

CLEARED: active for Sunday's Week 3 win over the Chargers and led Buffalo in targets, catches and receiving yards (6 catches on 10 targets for 67 yards) with no setback reported (NBC Sports, 9/27) — the shoulder is fully behind him.

NEW (9/30): back on a game-status designation (limited, worked in a non-contact jersey) as Buffalo continues managing the same AC joint/shoulder sprain from Week 2 — not a new injury or setback. Reporting across RotoWire/CBS/Yahoo frames it as ongoing rest/management; he's expected to play Week 4 vs. New England (9/30).

CLEARED (10/3): the AC-joint/shoulder sprain is fully behind him -- back to a full practice week with no setback, and expected to play Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. New England. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

NEW DESIGNATION (10/5): back to QUESTIONABLE today after being cleared to Healthy on 10/3. No new injury mechanism or beat-writer report has surfaced tying this to a specific in-game exit from Sunday's Week 4 game vs. New England -- stating that plainly rather than guessing. Given his recurring AC-joint/shoulder history, treat this as probable continued precautionary management rather than a new, more serious issue until further reporting clarifies it. Downgrading tag from Healthy back to Health Watch.

WORSENED (10/16): did not practice the estimated Wednesday report or Thursday's walkthrough with the AC joint/shoulder sprain (originally a Week 2 injury that's been re-aggravated multiple times) -- multiple outlets (WGRZ, Heavy.com) now say he's unlikely to play Sunday vs. the Raiders (10/18) and could instead use Buffalo's Week 7 bye to fully heal. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the real absence risk.

CONFIRMED OUT (10/18): officially inactive for Buffalo's 33-30 win at Las Vegas with the recurring AC-joint/shoulder sprain, missing his second game in three weeks; Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir absorbed the added target share. Buffalo now has its Week 7 bye before a Nov. 1 game vs. Baltimore, giving Moore roughly two extra weeks to heal with no specific new timeline reported -- keeping the standard Injury tier given the recurring nature of this shoulder issue, but the bye materially helps his odds of a clean return.

BYE-WEEK RESET (10/22): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip is procedural, not a recovery signal -- Buffalo is on its Week 7 bye (confirmed via NFL.com/Fox Sports bye lists), so there's no game this week for any designation to attach to. The recurring AC-joint/shoulder sprain hasn't been given any new timeline by the team; next game is Nov. 1 vs. Baltimore, giving Moore the full two-week bye window to heal.

Kyle Pitts Sr..name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
bullets: Finished 2025 as the No. 2 fantasy TE in PPR and was projected top-5 again in 2026 as one of Penix's top two targets alongside London, but the profile hasn't shown up in the box score through 3 games.

NEW: just 1 catch on 2 targets for 5 yards in Thursday night's Week 3 win over Green Bay (35-14) — his line through 3 games is now just 2 catches for 20 yards on 6 targets. QB Michael Penix Jr. is clearly funneling the passing game elsewhere (London had a 9/194 day the same game); worth downgrading expectations until target share shows up (RotoWire/NBC Sports, 9/24).

Parker Washington.name: Parker Washington
bullets: Stepped up in practice reps amid Thomas/Meyers injuries in one of the league's deepest WR rooms, alongside Travis Hunter.

George Kittle.name: George Kittle
bullets: Played in the opener as expected off Achilles recovery, but usage was light (2 catches, 12 yards on 5 targets, 46.2% of snaps) — matches Shanahan's stated plan to manage his snap count.

The Achilles maintenance plan wrapped up clean — upgraded to a full practice Friday (9/18) and removed from the injury report entirely, with no designation for Sunday vs. Miami; Wed/Thu limited reps were confirmed as planned workload management, not a new setback (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, 9/18).

DK Metcalf.name: DK Metcalf
bullets: Played through the previously undisclosed issue with no setback and led Pittsburgh's offense with 10 targets, turning them into 4 catches for 40 yards in the opener vs. Atlanta — the target volume was there even if the per-catch efficiency wasn't.
Traded from Seattle to Pittsburgh in 2025 (Steelers sent a 2nd- and 7th-rounder, got back a 6th) and signed a 5-year, $150M extension there.
UPDATE: named Steelers' Player of the Week after his Week 4 performance, remaining Pittsburgh's clear top target earner (Steelers.com, early week of 10/5).

NEW (10/18): added to Pittsburgh's injury report Friday with an illness (not an injury) after missing practice -- RotoBaller reports he wasn't on the Wednesday/Thursday report, suggesting he started feeling sick late in the week. Steelers' WR room is thin behind him (Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek both out), so Germie Bernard would see a bigger role if Metcalf can't go Sunday vs. Tampa Bay. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch given the swift, late-week designation; illness-driven Questionable tags often clear on gameday, so recheck the final inactive list.

CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/18): removed from Pittsburgh's injury report Saturday, ending the late-week illness scare, then delivered a big game in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over Tampa Bay -- 11 catches for 93 yards, tied with Germie Bernard (also 11 catches) for Pittsburgh's team high in receptions (Yahoo Sports, Behind the Steel Curtain, 10/18-19). Teammate Pat Freiermuth (calf) also carried a late QUESTIONABLE tag into the same game -- see his note. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean, productive game.

Brock Purdy.name: Brock Purdy
bullets: Signed a massive 5-yr/$265M extension; finished as a QB1-range fantasy scorer in every full season as a starter, behind a receiving corps upgraded with Mike Evans and Christian Kirk.

Ja'Kobi Lane.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
bullets: Fractured his left wrist coming down awkwardly after a Lamar Jackson end-zone target during Sunday's win over Indianapolis; finished with 1 catch for 11 yards before exiting in the 2nd quarter.

Surgery on the wrist was performed Wednesday morning (Sept 16) and reported successful; Baltimore officially placed him on injured reserve the same day. The NFL's mandatory 4-game minimum rules him out through Week 5 (Saints, Cowboys, Titans, Falcons), with HC Jesse Minter saying he has "a really good chance of coming back here pretty quick" once eligible — Week 6 vs. Cleveland is the target, not yet guaranteed.
Ravens promoted WR Chris Moore from the practice squad to fill the roster spot. Puts his WR2-behind-Flowers breakout runway on hold for at least a month.

ACTIVATED (10/17): designated for return and logged a full practice before being activated off injured reserve ahead of Sunday's Week 6 game at Cleveland, ending the 4-game-minimum absence from his Week 1 wrist fracture/surgery (Baltimore Ravens official site, NBC Sports Fantasy, 10/14-17). His specific snap count/target share in Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns could not be confirmed via search as of this update -- Baltimore's passing game ran through backup Tyler Huntley (19-of-31, 165 yds, 1 TD) with Lamar Jackson out again (ankle, see his note), so expect a gradual route back to volume rather than an immediate workload. Softening tag from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch now that he's actually back and eligible.

WEEK 6 ACTUAL (10/18): active for his first game off IR, as expected, in Baltimore's 13-10 loss at Cleveland; his specific snap count/target share could not be confirmed via search as of this update, with Baltimore's passing game going through backup QB Tyler Huntley (Lamar Jackson out again, ankle -- see his note). Keeping Health Watch pending a clearer read on his workload next week.

Woody Marks.name: Woody Marks
bullets: Was Houston's clear passing-down/receiving-work back behind David Montgomery through the first several weeks, holding real standalone value even in a committee.

NEW (10/13): took over as Houston's lead back after David Montgomery exited Sunday's Week 5 win over Tennessee (26-3) with a groin injury -- finished with a season-high 15 carries for 62 yards plus 4 catches, reportedly logging roughly 85% of the Texans' backfield snaps once Montgomery left (FantasyPros, Athlon Sports, SI/OnSI, 10/12). With Montgomery now DOUBTFUL/week-to-week (see his note), Marks projects as Houston's clear lead back for as long as that lasts.

UPDATE (10/13): confirmed to keep the expanded lead-back role for Week 6 in Montgomery's continued absence, replicating his Week 5 workload (15 carries/62 yards, 4 catches) -- per FantasyFootballers and CBS Sports (~10/13). Jawhar Jordan and practice-squad RB Deuce Vaughn are the depth pieces behind him if needed.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
bullets: Opened 2026 with 8 catches for 122 yds and the game-winning 45-yard TD (41 YAC) on 4th-and-1 in the 4th quarter of Seattle's 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game win over New England — early sign the regression fears may be overblown.

Backup QB Drew Lock (18/22, 187 yds) finished that game after starter Sam Darnold left with a hip injury on the opening drive; Darnold's Thursday (Sept 10) MRI showed no major structural damage ("dodged a bullet," per the team), but he's still expected to miss Week 2 at Arizona with Lock confirmed as the Week 2 starter — worth tracking since it affects who's throwing Smith-Njigba the ball.
Led all NFL WRs with 1,793 yds/10 TD in 2025 and won Offensive Player of the Year; now the highest-paid WR in history (4yr/$168.6M).
Top-5 overall fantasy asset — the question is regression off a historic year, not upside.

NEW (10/14): picked up a minor ankle injury on a 16-yard lateral run in the second quarter of Seattle's 32-29 Week 5 loss at San Francisco (10/11) -- it didn't meaningfully slow him down; he still topped 100 receiving yards for the 5th straight game, pushing his NFL-leading total to 583 yards and 7 TDs through 5 games. The Seattle Times' Bob Condotta reported he was a limited practice participant Monday (10/12) ahead of a short week (Seahawks play Thursday 10/15 at Denver), with reporting suggesting he should play Thursday without real restriction. Tagging Health Watch given the minor/day-to-day framing -- not a real absence risk at this point.

UPDATE (10/15): no official designation beyond Monday's (10/12) limited-practice estimate has surfaced ahead of tonight's Thursday Night Football game at Denver -- RotoBaller's analysis expects him to play without real restriction on the short week, but that's analyst opinion, not a confirmed team designation. Check Seattle's pregame inactive list for final confirmation.

RESOLVED (10/16): the minor ankle tweak was a non-issue -- played every snap of Thursday night's 17-14 OT loss at Denver (10/15) with no in-game setback, posting 12 catches on 16 targets for 134 yards (season now 49 catches, 717 yards, 7 TD through 6 games). Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; today's ACTIVE flip reflects a clean bill of health, not a new designation.

Jeremiyah Love.name: Jeremiyah Love
bullets: Played through the high-ankle sprain that had him Questionable and delivered his first extended workload: 11 carries for 41 yards and a TD plus 2 catches for 9 yards in Sunday's game vs. the Chargers.
No setback reported after the game — the ankle no longer looks like a Week 2 concern with a full game under his belt.

NEW (10/5-6): tweaked his OTHER ankle (not the preseason high-ankle sprain) late in Sunday's Week 4 loss at the Giants, finishing with 14 carries for 63 yards plus a target that went for -8 yards. HC Mike LaFleur described it Monday as "a management-type thing... he tweaks it and then he feels fine," and Love himself called this shaping up as the "longest year" of his career (NBC Sports, RotoBaller, Heavy.com, SI.com, 10/4-5). No practice report yet as of today (Week 5 practice starts Wednesday); downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending Wednesday's designation.

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Detroit -- HC Mike LaFleur had already downplayed the tweaked ankle as a "management-type thing," and that held up with no setback reported heading into Friday. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

NEW, SEPARATE INJURY (10/16): dealing with a different left-ankle issue (not the preseason high-ankle sprain or the earlier "management-type" tweak) -- did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (10/14-10/15). HC Mike LaFleur's language shifted more cautious, saying the staff wants to "get this ankle right and do it the right way," which beat writers (Arizona Sports, Yahoo Sports) read as a real threat to his Sunday availability vs. the Rams (10/18) even though Love reportedly wants to play through it. Tyler Allgeier would start if he sits. Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier given the genuine uncertainty.

CONFIRMED (10/18): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. the Rams -- HC Jonathan Gannon's staff (via AP) confirmed the lingering left ankle injury (aggravated in Week 4 at the Giants) kept him out of practice all week. No IR conversations have taken place per the team, so this reads as a short-term absence rather than a long one. Tyler Allgeier (newly added to this roster, see his note) and Bam Knight are set to handle Arizona's backfield work Sunday. Keeping the standard Injury tier given the no-IR signal, though recheck next week for an actual return target.

UPDATE (10/22): did not practice Wednesday (10/21) with the ankle injury -- HC Mike LaFleur said rest is "vital" for him right now, and NBC Sports frames the DNP as putting him "on the wrong side of questionable" for Sunday's Week 7 game vs. Denver. He has a chance to return to practice Thursday/Friday; if he sits, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would again handle Arizona's backfield work. Keeping the standard Injury tier pending the rest of the week's reports.

Rashee Rice.name: Rashee Rice
bullets: Made his long-awaited return from suspension and offseason knee cleanup in Kansas City's Week 1 win over Denver, playing through it cleanly — 2 catches for 19 yards and a TD on just 2 targets as the offense eased him back in behind Kenneth Walker III's big rushing day.

UPDATE: usage has climbed hard each week since — 2 targets (Wk1) to 6 (Wk2) to 9 in Week 3 (7 catches, 88 yards) in a 49-play win over Miami where Mahomes only threw 24 times — a clear signal Rice is rounding back into the true WR1 role (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, RotoWire, 9/27).

NEW INJURY, CONFIRMED (10/4-5): suffered a non-contact hamstring injury early in Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Raiders -- pulled up lame grabbing his leg after a short catch, was downgraded to doubtful, and did not return (SI, KCTV5, NBC Sports, ClutchPoints, AtoZ Sports, DraftKings Network, 10/4). IMPORTANT: search results for Rice are heavily cross-contaminated with his unrelated, much more serious September 2024 knee injury (LCL/hamstring-tendon surgery after a Mahomes collision, which was feared to be an ACL tear at the time) -- that 2024 story is NOT this year's news and should not be merged with it. This week's hamstring strain is a new, separate, and so far lower-severity issue. Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier pending a firmer timeline; keeping Elite Starter since the role/talent profile is unaffected when he's healthy.

UPDATE (10/16): a second straight full DNP Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the hamstring/knee injury; HC Andy Reid declined to commit to him practicing the rest of the week or playing Sunday, saying of hamstrings, "it could be a week, it could be two weeks, you don't know" (Arrowhead Pride). Trending toward sitting out Sunday's Week 6 game vs. the Chargers (10/18) rather than a continuation of last week's progress.

CONFIRMED (10/18): HC Andy Reid ruled Rice out for Sunday's Week 6 game vs. the Chargers after a third straight full DNP week with the hamstring strain suffered in Week 4 vs. the Raiders. Reid declined a firm number but said hamstring injuries typically cost players '1 to 2 weeks' and called him 'a pretty fast healer,' with Kansas City's primetime Week 7 game at Seattle floated as a realistic return target (Field Level Media, KCTV5, 10/16). Revising tag from the standard Injury tier to Short-Term Injury given that fairly firm 1-2 week framing.

UPDATE (10/22): did not practice Wednesday (10/21) with the hamstring -- HC Andy Reid confirmed the sit-out but said Rice "is improving," without predicting whether that's enough for Sunday Night Football at Seattle (10/25, 8:20pm ET, NBC). He needs to mix into practice Thursday/Friday for a real shot to play; keeping the Short-Term Injury tier given last week's firm 1-2-week framing from Reid is still the operative timeline.

Quinshon Judkins.name: Quinshon Judkins
bullets: Moved to the unambiguous RB1 spot on Cleveland's depth chart, ahead of Sampson and Sanders.
Battling a minor "nagging" injury that cost him two camp practices, but coaches aren't concerned — remains Cleveland's clear lead back over Dylan Sampson, Raheim Sanders, and Ahmani Marshall.
2025 2nd-round pick (36th overall, Ohio State), acquired via a Day 1 trade with Jacksonville.

Handled 12 of Cleveland's 15 RB carries plus 5 catches (17 touches, 48 total yards) in the Week 2 win over Tampa Bay, confirming him as the clear #1 back even in a tough matchup (CBS Sports, RotoWire).

NEW (10/13): picked up a new right ankle "tweak" in Sunday's Week 5 loss to the Jets (10/11); HC Kevin Stefanski called it day-to-day and said he'll "have a chance to play" Week 6 vs. Baltimore (RotoWire, NBC Sports, 10/12). Worth watching closely -- it's the same ankle/fibula area he surgically repaired after a dislocation/fracture last season, which has some beat writers flagging it even though team language is cautiously optimistic (Yahoo Sports/Heavy, Dawg Pound Daily, 10/12). No official Wed/Thu/Fri practice grade confirmed yet -- recheck before Week 6. If he sits, Raheim Sanders would be next in line, though Sanders himself left the same game with a hip injury and his own availability is a wrinkle (ESPN).

UPDATE (10/14): did NOT practice Wednesday with the ankle, per NBC Sports/RotoWire -- he was seen in the locker room without the walking boot he'd worn postgame Sunday, a mildly positive visual sign, but no Thursday/Friday practice grade had posted as of this update; his Week 6 call vs. Baltimore still hinges on the rest of the week's practice participation. Correction: the "day-to-day, has a chance to play" comment is attributed by multiple outlets to OC Todd Monken, not HC Kevin Stefanski as previously framed -- flagging since the original Stefanski attribution could not be verified. Separately, backup Raheim Sanders (hip, same Week 5 game) was placed on IR Tuesday (10/13), so he will NOT be available if Judkins sits -- Cleveland signed RB Audric Estime off Minnesota's practice squad as added depth, with Jaleel McLaughlin also in the mix. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty and Wednesday DNP.

UPDATE (10/16): did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the ankle, though he was seen without his walking boot. Beat writers still frame him as "day-to-day" without a firm ruling, but Cleveland signed RB Audric Estime off Minnesota's practice squad this week as insurance, and Dawg Pound Daily reports the trend points toward Jaleel McLaughlin as Sunday's lead back vs. Baltimore (10/18) if Judkins sits.

CONFIRMED OUT (10/18): did not play in Cleveland's 13-10 win over Baltimore -- tested in pregame warmups on the ankle he tweaked in Week 5 (the same surgically-repaired ankle/fibula from last season) before being held out (USA Today/Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 10/18). Jaleel McLaughlin (9 carries/41 yards) and Audric Estime (9 carries/19 yards, including the game-tying 2-yard TD) split the backfield work in his absence. No firm return timeline has been reported yet for Week 7; recheck Wednesday's practice report. Keeping the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty and the injury's proximity to last year's more serious ankle/fibula fracture.

UPDATE (10/22): upgraded to a LIMITED practice participant Wednesday (10/21) -- a real step up from last week's DNP -- with Dylan Sampson also absent from Cleveland's non-participant list, per the Akron Beacon Journal's Chris Easterling. OC Todd Monken said he's "optimistic" about Judkins' availability for Sunday's Week 7 game vs. Tennessee but stopped short of guaranteeing it. Trending positive; keeping the standard Injury tier until he logs a full practice or a firmer designation posts.

TreVeyon Henderson.name: TreVeyon Henderson
bullets: Missed the Week 1 loss to Seattle (ruled out Sept 8) after not practicing all week with an ankle injury; Rhamondre Stevenson started in his place.
Returned to practice Sept 14 and was a full participant that week, officially cleared to Active for Week 2.

UPDATE (9/30): clearly took over New England's lead-back role in Week 3's 35-6 loss at Jacksonville — 8 carries for 23 yards plus a target, compared to just 1 carry for Stevenson. Small sample in a blowout script, but the snap/touch distribution points to Henderson as the ascending back; worth tracking whether it holds up in a more competitive game script (RotoWire, dknetwork, 9/27-28).

NEW (10/13): suffered a new ankle injury in New England's 45-17 Week 5 win over Las Vegas (10/11) -- first questionable to return, then ruled out, finishing with just 4 carries for 22 yards and 1 catch for 16 yards. Sent for testing Monday (10/12); HC Mike Vrabel said he'd be evaluated (Patriots Communications, DraftSharks, PatsPulpit, 10/11-12). No official Week 6 designation confirmed yet. With Henderson banged up, Rhamondre Stevenson (see his note) is expected to see the bulk of the carries, a reversal of the recent Henderson-as-lead-back trend, with rookie Corey Kiner as the likely change-of-pace option (Yahoo Sports).

WORSENED (10/14): status flipped from QUESTIONABLE to DOUBTFUL for Week 6 (home vs. the Jets, Sun 10/18). HC Mike Vrabel confirmed Henderson got an MRI on the ankle Monday (10/12) and said he'd be evaluated, but no diagnosis or specific return timeline has been reported by Patriots beat writers as of this update -- treat the DOUBTFUL tag as a real escalation given the MRI, even though it's not yet matched by a published diagnosis. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the genuine uncertainty. Rhamondre Stevenson (see his note) is expected to handle the bulk of New England's backfield work if Henderson can't go, with rookie Corey Kiner as change-of-pace.

UPDATE (10/14): listed as a LIMITED practice participant Wednesday with the ankle (NBC Sports/RotoWire, CBS Sports, Yahoo) -- a step up from a full DNP, but multiple outlets report the Patriots are expected to officially rule him out Friday for Sunday's game vs. the Jets, though that's not yet guaranteed. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported, following Monday's MRI, that it's a high right ankle sprain, no surgery needed, but likely multiple weeks out -- the first real diagnosis/timeline attached to this injury.

UPDATE (10/16): a meaningfully better trend than last week's fear of a multi-week absence -- practiced in a non-contact jersey as a LIMITED participant both Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15), the first real practice reps since Monday's ankle MRI, and was seen running and cutting on video Thursday. SI's Patriots Country and DraftSharks now frame him as a plausible Sunday option vs. the Jets (10/18), matching today's status flip from DOUBTFUL back to QUESTIONABLE -- though a full Friday practice is still needed to shed the tag entirely.

PLAYED ON PITCH COUNT (10/18): active and started but clearly managed coming off the ankle sprain -- 7 carries for 31 yards plus 1 catch for 9 yards in the 26-19 win over the Jets, and lost his first fumble of the season in the 3rd quarter (forced by Jets rookie David Bailey), which the Jets converted into points (ESPN, CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 10/18). Rookie Corey Kiner reportedly out-touched him on early downs in one beat writer's count (11 carries/57 yards per a Patriots Notebook recap), suggesting a timeshare while Henderson continues to work back to full speed. Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Health Watch now that he's active and playing, but worth monitoring his snap share closely next week given the apparent load management.

Harold Fannin Jr..name: Harold Fannin Jr.
bullets: Led the Browns in receiving as a rookie (72/731/6); with Njoku gone he's the unquestioned TE1 under new OC Todd Monken, who developed Andrews and Likely.

Jameson Williams.name: Jameson Williams
bullets: Coming off a big season but genuinely boom/bust (WR41 pace Weeks 1-10 vs. WR13 pace Weeks 11-18) — more of a WR3 with real week-winning upside than a lineup lock.

Aaron Jones Sr..name: Aaron Jones Sr.
bullets: Was co-starter on paper with Jordan Mason — but Mason's Sept 16 thumb-fracture surgery and IR placement (out a mandatory 4 games minimum, through at least Week 5) handed Jones the clear lead-back role in Minnesota for at least a month. Depth behind him is thin (DeeJay Dallas up from the practice squad).

CLEARED: the knee tweak from Minnesota's Week 2 win was removed from the injury report after a full Friday practice — Jones carries no designation into Sunday's game vs. Tampa Bay (NBC Sports, FantasyPros, Vikings.com, 9/25).

RJ Harvey.name: RJ Harvey
bullets: CLEARED off the hamstring that cost him Week 2: returned to action in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Rams (30-26), tying for the team lead in targets — 2 carries for 6 yards plus 6 catches on 7 targets for 41 yards (CBS Sports, 9/27).

NEW: was evaluated for a concussion in the second half of Sunday's game, but cleared and stayed in — logged just one touch afterward, more a game-flow note than a lingering health concern, though worth a light watch into Week 4.

J.K. Dobbins led Denver's backfield in carries Sunday (17 att/49 yds, still without a rushing TD this year) but Harvey's role as the clear passing-down/receiving back is intact; Jonah Coleman remains on IR (high ankle sprain, out at least through Week 6).

Week 6 TNF (10/15): scored his first rushing TD of the season (1-yard) in Denver's 17-14 OT win over Seattle, finishing with 6 carries for 25 yards plus 3 catches on 4 targets for 31 yards -- led Denver in receiving. J.K. Dobbins also scored on the ground (see his note); Denver's backfield split continues with no clear lead-back resolution.

Matthew Stafford.name: Matthew Stafford
bullets: Reigning NFL MVP — led the league in passing yards (4,707) and TD passes (46) in 2025; real regression risk since his 2025 leaned on unsustainable red-zone efficiency.
Went 22-of-31 for 327 yards, 4 TD, 1 INT in Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants; his 426th career passing touchdown moved him past Philip Rivers into 6th all-time (NFL.com, Yahoo Sports).

Eddy Pineiro.name: Eddy Pineiro
bullets: San Francisco's starting kicker behind a run-heavy, red-zone-efficient offense under Kyle Shanahan.

Missed all three practices last week (Wed-Fri, 9/16-18) sick, drawing a Questionable tag for Week 2 vs. Miami with the 49ers carrying no other kicker on the roster or practice squad. The 49ers worked out veteran kickers Greg Joseph and Younghoe Koo Saturday (9/19) but signed neither — a strong signal the team expects Pineiro to be active and play Sunday (NBC Sports Bay Area, 9/19-20).

Tucker Kraft.name: Tucker Kraft
bullets: Confirmed "full-go" for Week 1 vs. Minnesota after full-contact clearance and full participation in a joint practice vs. Arizona — a clean upgrade off the torn ACL, though still his first year back.

Ollie Gordon II.name: Ollie Gordon II
bullets: Stepped in after De'Von Achane tore his ACL in Week 3 vs. Kansas City (season-ending) — 17 carries for 41 yards and a TD, plus 3 catches for 14 yards on 3 targets in relief (Yahoo Sports, Bleacher Report, 9/27-28).

Miami's backfield is now a committee with Jaylen Wright (trending back healthy for Week 4) — analysts project roughly a 60/40 split favoring Wright, with Gordon getting goal-line/early-down work. One of the top Week 4 waiver adds league-wide given the timeshare upside (SI/OnSI, Yahoo Sports).

Week 4 final (10/4): dominated the Miami backfield in the 15-10 loss to Minnesota -- 9 carries for 100 yards and a TD plus 2 targets on 22 snaps, clearly outplaying Jaylen Wright (5 carries/7 yards, 12 snaps -- see his note). With De'Von Achane out for the season, Gordon now looks like the favorite for lead-back work in Miami's backfield heading into Week 5, not just a 50/50 committee piece (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Heavy.com, 10/4).

George Pickens.name: George Pickens
bullets: Franchise-tagged ($27.3M) after a 2025 breakout — 93 rec/1,429 yds/9 TD, top-6 PPR WR despite sharing targets with Lamb.

Bijan Robinson.name: Bijan Robinson
bullets: Widely projected as the 2026 fantasy #1 overall pick — back-to-back 1,400+ rush-yard seasons plus 60+ catches gives him a McCaffrey-type dual-threat ceiling.
The camp hold-in is fully resolved: signed a 3-year, $75M extension ($51M guaranteed) with Atlanta in early August 2026, ending the contract-driven absence before the season started (NFL.com).

Backed up the elite billing with a dominant Thursday-night Week 3 performance in the 35-14 win over Green Bay: 29 carries for 194 yards and 2 rushing TDs, plus 2 catches for 19 yards — 213 total yards from scrimmage (CBS Sports, 9/24).

Josh Allen.name: Josh Allen
bullets: Locked in as the top overall fantasy QB — top-9 in passing yards 5 of the last 6 years, top-7 in passing TDs every year, with real rushing/scramble equity on top.

Historic Week 2 Thursday-night performance in a 41-31 win over Detroit: 317 total yards and 5 total TDs (3 pass, 2 rush), over 40 fantasy points — per ESPN, only the 3rd player in NFL history with 9 total TDs and 0 turnovers through a team's first 2 games (Mahomes 2018, Manning 2013 the others).

NEW: banged up late in Week 3's win over the Chargers — took a helmet to the outside of his left knee in the 4th quarter and was seen favoring the leg postgame. No formal diagnosis announced, but medical analysts (Dr. David Chao) describe him as "more hurt than injured," floating a possible grade 1-2 MCL sprain that could range from full Week 4 availability to a 1-3 week absence (Buffalo Rumblings, SI, Yahoo Sports, 9/28-29). Officially Questionable entering Week 4 vs. New England and likely limited in practice early in the week — worth checking the Friday injury report before locking him in.

UPDATE (9/30): the left knee scare from Week 3 is a non-issue — Allen practiced in full Wednesday with no brace or visible limitation, and HC Joe Brady said "I'm not concerned with Josh." He is NOT listed on the Week 4 injury report at all ahead of Sunday's game vs. New England (Buffalo Rumblings, CBS Sports, RotoWire, 9/30).

Week 4 final (10/4): the knee was a total non-issue, but Buffalo lost its first game of the season, 29-26 at home to New England (fell to 3-1). Allen went 23/33 for 253 yards and 1 passing TD (34-yd to Keon Coleman) plus 5 carries for 4 yards and a rushing TD -- but threw a game-sealing INT with 1:14 left. He also became Buffalo's all-time TD leader on the score. No health concerns entering Week 5 (ESPN, Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 10/4).

Brock Bowers.name: Brock Bowers
bullets: Missed Week 1 (meniscus trim surgery in early September) and Week 2 at the Chargers, then came down to a Sunday game-time call for Week 3 vs. New Orleans.

CLEARED AND DELIVERED: officially active roughly 2 hours before kickoff and made a monstrous 2026 season debut in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Saints — 10 catches on 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown (CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 9/27), instantly re-establishing himself as Las Vegas' clear top receiving option.
No re-aggravation reported after the workload; Michael Mayer moves back to a clear TE2 role now that Bowers has cleared and produced in the same game.

UPDATE (10/8): Bowers has carried a QUESTIONABLE tag in each of the last two weeks -- an illness (not his earlier knee issue) was the reported cause ahead of Week 4 vs. Kansas City, and the Raiders expected him to play (ESPN's Adam Schefter, 10/4); he's QUESTIONABLE again for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. New England, though the specific reason behind this week's tag hadn't been reported by beat writers as of Wednesday.

CLEARED (10/8): upgraded from limited to a full practice participant Thursday on the knee, trending toward playing Sunday's Week 5 game vs. New England -- no setback reported from the illness-related QUESTIONABLE tag he carried into Week 4 (Yahoo Sports/Raiders beat, 10/8).

NEW DESIGNATION (10/16): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag for the first time this week, but it's the same knee the Raiders have been proactively managing in practice all season, not a new injury -- limited Wednesday, upgraded to a full practice Thursday (10/14-10/15). FantasyPros projects him at 94% to play Sunday vs. Buffalo (10/18); this matches his standard early-week rest pattern rather than a real setback.

CLEARED (10/17): logged back-to-back full practices Thursday and Friday and carries NO injury designation into Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Buffalo -- officially off the injury report entirely (NBC Sports, 10/16). Remains the overall TE1 play this week.

David Montgomery.name: David Montgomery
bullets: Trade acquisition from DET leads the Houston backfield, and Joe Mixon's release clears out the only other real competition — but Woody Marks still holds real passing-down/receiving touches, so it remains a genuine committee, not a clear lead back.

NEW (10/13): suffered a groin injury early in the 2nd quarter of Sunday's Week 5 win over Tennessee (26-3), exiting after just 5 carries for 11 yards (Houston Chronicle, RotoWire, ESPN, 10/11-12). HC DeMeco Ryans called it "week-to-week" Monday with no hard return date, matching today's flip to DOUBTFUL -- picking the standard Injury tier given the genuinely uncertain timeline. Woody Marks (see his note) took over as the lead back the rest of the game and is confirmed to handle the workload if Montgomery sits further; Ryans said Marks "will carry the load for us."

UPDATE (10/15): no fresher practice-report confirmation found beyond HC DeMeco Ryans' Monday (10/12) "week-to-week" comments -- no official Wed/Thu Week 6 designation located via search yet. 4for4's analysis says he's "very likely" to miss Week 6, and flags that Houston's upcoming bye week could extend the absence further before a firm return estimate emerges. Woody Marks (see his note) is confirmed as the Week 6 lead back regardless.

CONFIRMED OUT (10/16): officially ruled out for Sunday's Week 6 game at Jacksonville in London (10/18) with the groin injury suffered late in the Week 5 win over Tennessee, after zero practice reps Wednesday or Thursday. HC DeMeco Ryans calls it "week-to-week," with reporting (NBC Sports, National Football Post) pointing to a Week 7 vs. the Giants target return -- Houston's bye isn't until Week 8, so there's no extra cushion this week. Upgrading tag to Short-Term Injury given the firm ~1-week target; Woody Marks remains the clear lead back in the meantime.

UPDATE (10/22): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip lines up with the new Week 7 practice-report cycle (Houston hosts the Giants Sun 10/25), but no independent beat reporting confirming his actual Wednesday practice participation was found as of this update -- one outlet speculates he could target a Week 7 return but explicitly flags that as unconfirmed, not an official report. Keeping the Short-Term Injury tier from last week's ~1-week target rather than overclaiming a confirmed recovery; recheck Thursday/Friday's report. Woody Marks remains the lead back in the meantime.

Luther Burden III.name: Luther Burden III

UPDATE: caught an 8-yard TD from Case Keenum in Chicago's 27-7 Week 3 upset of Philadelphia (Monday Night, 9/28) — his first score of the season, with Keenum starting in place of the injured Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent.

Delivered as the Packers' clear outside WR1 in the Week 1 win at Minnesota: 6 catches for 147 yards and 2 TDs on 8 targets, well ahead of Matthew Golden in target share.

Kept it up in Thursday night's Week 3 loss at Atlanta (35-14): led the team with 7 catches on 10 targets for 96 yards and a TD (4-yard grab that opened the scoring) — remains Green Bay's clear top target earner even in a blowout loss (RotoWire/CBS Sports, 9/24).

Jacory Croskey-Merritt.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt

NEW (10/8): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag in this week's injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants; specific injury type was not confirmed by beat writers as of Wednesday -- recheck once Washington's Thursday/Friday reports post. Still working as part of a 2-man committee with Rachaad White.

Dropping the Health Watch tag now that he's cleared.

NEW (10/15-16): a groin injury (recurring from Week 5) kept him off the practice field entirely both Thursday and Friday ahead of Monday night's Week 6 game at San Francisco (10/19) -- ESPN's John Keim flagged the Thursday absence as a real watch item. Re-adding the Health Watch tag given the back-to-back DNPs; no severity or ruled-out/doubtful designation confirmed yet, recheck Saturday's report. Rachaad White would see the bulk of the backfield work if he sits.

CONFIRMED OUT (10/18, final): HC Dan Quinn confirmed Saturday that Croskey-Merritt is out for tonight's Monday Night Football Week 6 game at San Francisco (10/19) with the same recurring groin injury -- he did not practice at all this week (SI/Yahoo Sports Commanders injury reports, 10/17-18). Across 5 games this season he had 67 carries for 239 yards and 2 TDs in a committee with Rachaad White. Washington's backfield now projects as a White/Austin Ekeler/Jeremy McNichols (activated off IR Monday) committee in his absence. Upgrading tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury given the official IR move and the ~4-game minimum absence.

Tyreek Hill.name: Tyreek Hill

Not rostered by any NFL team — unplayable/bench for now; monitor for a signing or workout announcement.

UPDATE (10/13): still unsigned -- agent Drew Rosenhaus called the free-agency situation "fluid," telling reporters "I think a deal could happen anytime" and naming the Chiefs as a plausible contender fit given Hill's stated preference to sign only with a Super Bowl-caliber team needing WR help (RotoBaller, CBS Sports, 10/13). No team has signed him as of this update. Today's in-system flip from OUT to QUESTIONABLE does not correspond to any real NFL game-status designation since he isn't on any team's roster -- treat it as a data artifact, not real news. Remains unplayable/bench.

Chase Brown.name: Chase Brown
bullets: Top-5, arguably top-3 PPR RB potential — posted 7 top-12 weekly finishes even through Burrow's 2025 absence; Samaje Perine remains mild committee/handcuff risk.

Backed up a strong Week 1 with 20 carries for 80 yards plus 3 catches on 5 targets in Cincinnati's 20-6 win over Houston in Week 2 — 42-of-60 snaps, 36 carries and 11 targets through two games confirms bell-cow usage (Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports).

Braelon Allen.name: Braelon Allen
bullets: Clear backup, not a starter — Breece Hall re-signed and remains the workhorse; Allen competes with Isaiah Davis for change-of-pace touches.

Treat as the clear lead-back option for as long as Hall is out (CBS Sports, NBC Sports, SI/OnSI, 9/28).

Week 4 final (10/4): took every single Jets RB carry in the 23-12 loss to Chicago -- 14 carries for 59 yards (4.2 YPC) plus 2 catches for 8 yards. Volume was capped by the Jets' anemic 32 offensive plays, not a snap-share concern. With Breece Hall still out (see his note, remains week-to-week with no firm return date), Allen looks like the clear every-down back rather than a committee piece -- upgrading tag from Depth Chart Battle to Depth Chart Secured (NBC Sports, NYJets.com, CBS Sports, 10/4-5).

Week 5 final (10/11): career-best game with Breece Hall again out -- 24 carries for 116 yards (4.8 YPC) and the game-winning 22-yard TD run on 3rd down in a 17-12 win over Cleveland, playing 60 of 70 snaps (85.7%). Added 1 catch on 4 targets for 0 yards. Remains the clear lead back as long as Hall is out.

Jalen Coker.name: Jalen Coker
bullets: Caught 8-of-9 targets in EACH of Carolina's first two games (Week 1: 8/138 yds/2 TD vs. Chicago; Week 2: 8/66 yds vs. Atlanta) with Bryce Young — became just the 3rd undrafted player since 1967 to reach 15+ catches, 200+ receiving yards and 2+ TDs through a team's first two games (Yahoo Sports/Heavy, 9/23). No longer just a presumptive WR2 behind McMillan — now viewed as a legitimate 1A/1B.

UPDATE: played through the ankle issue that had triggered a Week 3 Questionable tag, but exited Sunday's 21-18 loss to Cleveland early with a new quad strain, finishing limited to 2 catches for 18 yards.

Monday follow-up tests found nothing overly significant on the quad — described as a relatively minor strain. He's Questionable for Week 4 vs. Detroit, with his Wednesday-Friday practice activity set to determine availability (SI/OnSI, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 9/28-29). Downgrading tag from a standalone injury tier to Health Watch given the "relatively minor" framing and no ruled-out signal yet.

WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/5): downgraded from QUESTIONABLE to OUT today -- the quad strain suffered vs. Cleveland in Week 3 (originally called "relatively minor" by Ian Rapoport) has not resolved on the Wed-Fri practice ramp-up as hoped. No multi-week timeline has been disclosed, but Carolina has an IR transaction history on this same quad earlier in the season, raising some risk the team manages it conservatively. Bumping tag from Health Watch to standard Injury given the confirmed missed game and recurrence on the same body part.

REVISED TO LONG-TERM, CORRECTED (10/7): Carolina placed Coker on IR, and ESPN's David Newton reported an expected 4-to-6 game absence -- HC Dave Canales called it a "serious quad strain," a firmer and worse timeline than the earlier "relatively minor" read. Revising tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury given the confirmed 4+ game IR window. IMPORTANT CONTEXT: the Panthers are on their Week 5 BYE, so there is no Week 5 game/opponent for him either way -- today's QUESTIONABLE roster status is a placeholder, not a game-week designation. He's now inside his 21-day practice window (eligible to return from IR) but has not yet been designated to return; realistic target is Week 6 or later, post-bye.

CLEARED (10/16): practiced in full Wednesday (10/14) with no designation on Carolina's injury report, ending the IR stint -- HC Dave Canales called him "on track" to play Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Philadelphia (10/18) (NBC Sports/Sharp Football, 10/13-14). Softening tag from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch; expect his workload eased in his first game back before he reclaims a full target share.

Amon-Ra St. Brown.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
bullets: Top-5 fantasy WR three years running (WR4 in PPG each of the last 3 seasons) — high floor, high ceiling, first-round caliber.
Answered a quiet first half with 9 catches, 142 yards and 2 TDs in Thursday night's loss to Buffalo — his usual bell-cow target share showing up even in a losing effort.

CeeDee Lamb.name: CeeDee Lamb
bullets: Coming off a down 2025 (75/1,077/3, worst yardage since his rookie year) but still a Round 2 pick — expected bounce-back with Pickens locked in alongside him.

NEW (10/8): left Thursday night's Week 5 loss to Tampa Bay in the 4th quarter with a quad/thigh injury -- a recurrence of the thigh issue first flagged during the Week 3 win at Houston. Finished with a season-low 2 catches for 9 yards on 5 targets (coming off a 17-catch, 189-yard, career-high 21-target Week 4) as Dallas fell to the previously winless Buccaneers (DallasNews, NBC Sports, RotoBaller, 10/8). No Week 6 return timeline confirmed yet; George Pickens would be in line for a bigger target share if Lamb sits vs. Green Bay.

UPDATE (10/15): no official Wednesday designation found yet for Sunday Night Football at Green Bay (10/18, Lambeau) -- but team sentiment remains optimistic: EVP Stephen Jones said Friday (10/10) he expects Lamb "all ready to go," and Ian Rapoport has characterized the quad injury as a bruise that's "not considered serious." Recheck Friday's final report for official confirmation.

CLEARED (10/16): flipped from QUESTIONABLE back to ACTIVE -- the quad/thigh issue was confirmed as a bruise, not a strain, by NFL Network's Ian Rapoport ("not a major injury"), and Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones said Thursday he expects Lamb "all ready to go" for Sunday Night Football at Green Bay (10/18). Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

Week 6 final (10/18): played through the cleared quad bruise with no setback in Sunday Night Football's 23-13 loss at Green Bay -- drew a team-high 18 targets but converted them to just 9 catches for 70 yards, including a costly slipped route on a slant that Packers rookie Brandon Cisse intercepted. Dallas fell behind 17-0 at halftime and dropped to 2-4, its second straight loss; Dak Prescott threw 2 INTs on 34-of-54 passing. No new injury reported -- the quad is confirmed fully behind him; this was a low-efficiency game, not a health setback.

Breece Hall.name: Breece Hall
bullets: Groin was a non-issue in Week 1 — ran for 102 yards and a TD on 22 carries plus 2 catches for 16 yards in the opener vs. Tennessee, his best workload in well over a year.
Exited Sunday's Week 3 loss to Detroit in the second half with a quad/thigh injury after being tackled near the sideline (13 carries/32 yards, 3 catches/23 yards before leaving) — did not return.

NEW: Monday's MRI (9/28) came back better than initially feared — the Jets and multiple reports now describe Hall as "week-to-week" rather than facing a long absence, with hope it's a couple of weeks rather than a month-plus. CONFIRMED (10/10): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 5 game in London vs. Jacksonville with the hamstring injury -- missed back-to-back Wednesday/Thursday practices, and Ian Rapoport reported him not expected to play (10/8). Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce are set to handle the Eagles' backfield work in London (see Shipley's note).

Week 5 final (10/11): missed a second straight game as Jacksonville beat Philadelphia 19-17 in London on a last-second Cam Little field goal. Will Shipley and newly-activated Dameon Pierce (making his 2026 debut) handled the Eagles' backfield work in his absence; fellow absentee Tank Bigsby (abdomen) also sat out.

UPDATE (10/14): real positive signal for Week 6 vs. Carolina (Sun 10/18, home) -- RotoBaller reported (10/12) Barkley "has a chance to return," with Ian Rapoport earlier characterizing the hamstring injury as "not believed serious." No Wednesday practice report confirming actual participation had posted as of this update; keeping the standard Injury tier until that's confirmed.

SETBACK (10/14): also did NOT practice Wednesday -- the Eagles' team injury report listed him remaining sidelined even as other players returned from IR (Heavy.com/Yahoo; one Yahoo headline said "limited" but the fuller team-report language points to DNP). A real step back from the "has a chance to return" framing from earlier in the week for Sunday's game vs. Carolina; recheck Friday before trusting the more optimistic read.

UPDATE (10/16): a worse trend than teammate DeVonta Smith -- officially a non-participant in both Wednesday and Thursday practice (10/14-10/15), a second straight full DNP, and hasn't played since the Week 4 hamstring injury. Dameon Pierce would start Sunday vs. Carolina (10/18) if Barkley sits, with Carson Steele as backup; Friday's practice is the real swing factor.

CONFIRMED (10/18): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. Carolina after missing every practice this week with the hamstring injury -- a second straight full missed game (NBC Sports Philadelphia injury reports, 10/13-10/17). QB Jalen Hurts is also out (blood clot in his calf), with Tanner McKee starting; Dameon Pierce is set to lead Philadelphia's backfield Sunday with Carson Steele as backup.

UPDATE (10/22): Philadelphia is NOT on a bye this week -- they host Dallas on Monday Night Football (10/26). Per Bleacher Report (citing Ian Rapoport/Adam Schefter), the Eagles "believe" there's a "realistic" chance Barkley returns for that game, but no official Wednesday practice-report grade confirming actual participation was found as of this update -- treat as optimistic-but-unconfirmed, not a practice confirmation. Keeping the standard Injury tier; Dameon Pierce remains the lead back in the meantime.

Drake London.name: Drake London
bullets: Clear WR1 with essentially no target competition (~30% target share); should produce top-10 WR numbers, with QB play the main swing factor rather than his role.

Delivered a massive game in Thursday night's Week 3 win over Green Bay (35-14): 9 catches for 194 yards (including gains of 68 and 40 yards), tied to Michael Penix Jr.'s efficient return under center (18/25, 256 yards, 1 TD) (CBS Sports, 9/24).

NEW (10/13): QB Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury on a late sack in Atlanta's 30-23 overtime loss to Baltimore (10/12) and did not return to that game; Ian Rapoport reported it's not believed serious, and Penix said he expects to play Week 6 vs. Chicago, but the team was still evaluating him in practice as of midweek. Worth checking Friday's injury report before trusting London's volume outlook -- a limited or sidelined Penix would be a real dent in his target efficiency.

Kyren Williams.name: Kyren Williams
bullets: Remains the lead back in a McVay-preferred ~65:35 split with Blake Corum — not under real threat, but not a bell-cow either.

Split carries close to even with Blake Corum in Monday night's win over the Giants (12-85-0 rush plus a receiving TD for Williams), and lost a fumble at his own 11 late in the first half — worth tracking whether the committee trends more even going forward (CBS Sports/RotoWire).

UPDATE (10/13): scored the game-tying touchdown late in Monday night's 37-34 OT loss to Buffalo (10/12) but was otherwise inefficient per fantasy outlets. The loss was partly due to K Harrison Mevis missing two field goals, including a potential OT game-winner (see his note) -- worth monitoring whether kicking struggles start costing the Rams short-field/red-zone possessions that would otherwise run through Williams.

Davante Adams.name: Davante Adams
bullets: Turns 33; 2025 TD rate was unsustainable (49% of his fantasy points came via red-zone scores vs. a 14.5% NFL average) and his catch rate hit a career-low 53%.
No longer the clear #1 target with Nacua sharing the offense — real regression risk.

Answered the regression question emphatically in Monday night's 28-6 rout of the Giants: 8 catches for 195 yards and 2 TDs, Stafford's clear top target with Nacua (hip) inactive (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports).

OUT 6-10 WEEKS (10/19-21): suffered a non-contact injury on the Rams' penultimate offensive snap of Sunday's 18-16 loss to Arizona, pulling up in the end zone and hobbling to the sideline. HC Sean McVay said Monday it's a ruptured semitendinosus (hamstring tendon), with a 6-10 week recovery expected (AP/Field Level Media, 4for4, TSN, 10/19-20). Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and 4 TDs this season; Puka Nacua remains LA's clear top receiver in his absence, and the Rams are expected to look at adding WR depth. Upgrading tag from Aging Watch to Long-Term Injury given the confirmed multi-week (likely IR-eligible) timeline.

CONFIRMED (10/22): the Rams formally placed Adams on injured reserve Tuesday, Oct. 20, for the ruptured hamstring tendon (semitendinosus) suffered in Week 6 vs. Arizona -- locking him out a minimum of 4 games, consistent with HC Sean McVay's original 6-10 week recovery estimate (CBS Sports, RotoWire). Puka Nacua remains L.A.'s clear WR1; Konata Mumpfield is now in line for a bigger WR2-type role, with Jordan Whittington also in the mix.

Tyler Warren.name: Tyler Warren
bullets: The groin injury fully resolved — played through the Week 1 loss to Baltimore with no setback, catching 3 of 5 targets for 13 yards and a receiving TD.

NEW (10/18): added to Indianapolis' injury report Friday as a limited participant with a groin injury, drawing a QUESTIONABLE tag for Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Tennessee -- he dealt with a groin issue back in August, so this could be a recurrence rather than a fresh injury, though that hasn't been confirmed (4for4, The Fantasy Footballers, 10/16). Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending the final gameday call.

CONFIRMED OUT (10/18): officially inactive for Indianapolis' Week 6 game vs. Tennessee with the groin injury that popped up on Friday's practice report -- likely a recurrence of the same groin issue from August camp rather than a brand-new injury, though that hasn't been formally confirmed (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, StampedeBlue, 10/17-18). No return timeline reported yet. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier now that it has actually cost him a game.

UPDATE (10/22): did not practice Wednesday (10/21) with the groin injury, per the Colts' official report -- HC Shane Steichen called him "progressing really well" but deferred to the injury report rather than guaranteeing Sunday's availability. Indianapolis' Week 7 opponent is Minnesota (not a repeat of last week's Tennessee game). No Thursday/Friday grade or official designation confirmed yet as of this update; keeping the standard Injury tier.

Drake Maye.name: Drake Maye
bullets: Rough Week 1 debut of the new-weapons era: 23/33 for 178 yds, 1 TD, but 3 INTs — all in the 4th quarter, including a game-sealing pick in the end zone — in a 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game loss to Seattle. Added 47 rush yds. Called the turnovers "unacceptable" postgame; also lost top target A.J. Brown to an ankle injury mid-game.
Coming off a QB2-overall 2025 (20.7 PPG); Patriots traded for A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs, giving him real weapons — widely projected top-5 fantasy QB before Week 1's opener.

Tony Pollard.name: Tony Pollard
bullets: Entrenched starter chasing a 5th straight 1,000-yard season — hit 1,000 rushing yards in each of the past 4 years.
CLEARED: returned to a full practice Friday (9/25) and is off the final Week 3 injury report entirely — no designation for Sunday vs. the Giants (RotoWire, FantasyPros, NBC Sports, 9/25).

Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (ankle) remains Questionable — if Spears is limited or sits, Pollard is positioned for an even bigger workload bump on top of his already-larger carry share (53.4% snap share to Spears' 42.7% through two weeks, with roughly double Spears' carries).

NEW (9/30): a new foot injury (distinct from the ankle issue referenced earlier) — Pollard was a non-participant in Wednesday's Week 4 practice. HC Mike Vrabel's staff said they are "not overly concerned about Sunday" for Pollard and don't believe it will affect his Week 4 availability vs. Baltimore; backfield mate Tyjae Spears also sat out Wednesday with an ankle issue (CBS Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, Newsweek, 9/30).

CLEARED (10/1-2): the foot issue that held him out of Wednesday's practice did not linger — Pollard returned to a full practice Thursday and carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Baltimore. Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (ankle) remains limited/Questionable, keeping Pollard's bell-cow workload intact (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 10/1-2).

Week 4 final (10/4): the foot issue was a non-factor -- went for 16 carries, 48 yards and a 3-yard rushing TD plus 2 catches for 2 yards in a 24-18 loss to Baltimore that dropped Tennessee to 0-4. Backfield mate Tyjae Spears was marginal (2 carries, 7 yards), confirming Pollard as the clear lead back even in a lost season. Worth watching: with Tennessee winless, ESPN's Adam Schefter floated Pollard as a potential trade-deadline candidate -- no deal reported yet, just speculation (NBC Sports, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports, 10/4).

NEW (10/8): did not practice Wednesday with a foot injury and is QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Houston; beat coverage describes it as a possible maintenance/veteran rest day rather than a new injury, consistent with how Tennessee has handled him in past weeks (10/7).

CLEARED (10/8): back to a full practice participant Thursday after sitting out Wednesday with the foot issue -- on track to play Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Houston, continuing the pattern of maintenance-related absences that haven't cost him game time all season (Yahoo Sports/Titans beat, 10/8).

Week 5 final (10/13): the foot was a non-issue and he played the full workload, but the game itself was ugly -- Houston routed Tennessee 26-3 (ESPN gameId 401872984, Titans.com, PFF), dropping the Titans to 0-5 (not 0-4 as noted last week; the winless streak continued, it did not end). Pollard carried 14 times for 52 yards with no catches or TDs reported (Yahoo Sports, RotoWire, FantasyPros). No new injury flagged out of the game; still Tennessee's clear lead back on a team now shopping for answers at 0-5.

Courtland Sutton.name: Courtland Sutton
bullets: Likely slides to a true WR2 role now that Waddle is in town — real target competition caps his ceiling versus prior seasons.

Week 6 TNF (10/15): held under 50 receiving yards for a 5th straight week -- just 2 catches on 3 targets for 19 yards in Denver's 17-14 OT win over Seattle (season: 13-123-1 through 6 games). NBC Sports' recap framed QB Bo Nix as not looking his way; adding Regression Watch given the sustained low-volume stretch.

Chuba Hubbard.name: Chuba Hubbard
bullets: The camp hamstring issue was fully behind him for the opener — played through it and led Carolina's backfield in the Week 1 loss to Chicago: 10 carries for 49 yards and a rush TD plus 3 catches for 38 yards and a receiving TD (23.7 fantasy pts).

NEW: with Jonathon Brooks now on injured reserve (core-muscle surgery, minimum 6 weeks) as of 9/23, the earlier 1A/1B timeshare is over — Hubbard is Carolina's undisputed lead back, with AJ Dillon next man up in a diminished RB2/short-yardage role.

Chris Godwin Jr..name: Chris Godwin Jr.
bullets: The ankle rehab and conflicting reports resolved in his favor for Week 1 — played and produced in Tampa Bay's opener vs. Dallas, catching 4 targets for 40 yards plus a 3-yard carry, confirming the WR2/target-lead role behind Emeka Egbuka now that Mike Evans is gone.

But he left that game with a hamstring injury, missed practice all week (Sept 16-17), and has been confirmed ruled OUT for Week 2 vs. Cleveland (correcting the opponent — not New Orleans). Reporting indicates the strain isn't believed to be severe, but no return timeline beyond Week 2 has been confirmed yet.

CORRECTION/UPDATE (9/30): the hamstring issue referenced above resolved weeks ago and is no longer current. Godwin's active situation is a new ankle injury — he was a full non-participant in Wednesday's Week 4 practice (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, Bucs Nation, 9/30); severity has not yet been disclosed, with Thursday's practice participation flagged as the key signal. Separately, with Mike Evans now gone (signed with San Francisco in free agency), Godwin is "ticketed for a bigger role" in Tampa Bay's slot — 10 catches for 111 yards through 3 games (Buccaneers.com, 10/1). Tampa is thin at WR with Jalen McMillan on IR, raising the stakes on his Week 4 availability vs. Green Bay.

CLEARED (10/1-2): the ankle issue that held him out of Wednesday's practice resolved quickly — Godwin was back to a full practice participant Thursday and is expected to play Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Green Bay, continuing his expanded target-lead role in Tampa Bay's thin receiving corps with Mike Evans gone and Jalen McMillan on IR (NBC Sports, Buccaneers.com, 10/1-2).

Week 4 final (10/4): torched Green Bay for 10 catches (11 targets) for 155 yards as Tampa Bay won 34-20 at Lambeau, its third straight win, with Baker Mayfield posting a perfect 158.3 rating (CBS Sports, SI.com Buccaneers). No injury designation came out of the game -- fully healthy and Tampa Bay's clear lead receiver entering Week 5. Upgrading tag to Healthy.

NEW INJURY, RULED OUT (10/9-10): suffered a fibula injury (a different spot than last year's season-ending ankle dislocation/fracture) and was ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 6 game vs. San Francisco; HC Todd Bowles called it week-to-week with no IR move planned as of this report (NFL.com, CBS Sports, RotoBaller, 10/9-10). Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier pending a firmer return timeline.

Rachaad White.name: Rachaad White
bullets: Bounced back with the clearer role in Week 2 vs. Dallas (37-20 loss, 9/20): out-snapped Croskey-Merritt 36-23, leaned on heavily as a receiver in catch-up mode — 7 carries/43 yards + 6 catches/40 yards (83 total). A real 2-man committee, and he may now have the passing-down edge.
Signed a one-year, $2M free-agent deal with Washington after his rookie contract with Tampa Bay expired — reunites him with Arizona State teammate Jayden Daniels.

NEW (9/30): the shoulder injury from Week 3 (suffered late in the 2nd quarter vs. Seattle, returned and finished the game) has worsened in practice standing — White was the ONLY Commanders player who traveled to London and did not practice Wednesday, getting treatment instead. Multiple outlets (Hogs Haven, RotoWire, FantasyPros, NBC Sports, 9/30) now say he looks likely to sit out Week 4 vs. the Colts, which would open work for Jacory Croskey-Merritt and rookie Kaytron Allen. No games-missed count has been reported yet, so treat as a real but not-yet-confirmed short absence.

WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Colts in London -- the shoulder injury from Week 3 kept him from practicing at all this week even after traveling with the team, and multiple outlets now have him sitting out entirely rather than just banged up. Jacory Croskey-Merritt and rookie Kaytron Allen are set to pick up the work in his absence (Hogs Haven, RotoWire, Newsweek, 10/1-3).

UPDATE (10/5): the shoulder injury that kept him out of practice all week before London was not fully confirmed via search as an official inactive, but days of zero practice participation strongly indicate he sat out Week 4 vs. the Colts. The outlook is favorable, though -- reporting characterizes this as a short absence, with White "should be ready to go Week 5 against the Giants" (Newsweek/NBC Sports). Washington's recent addition of Austin Ekeler would handle passing-down work in any continued absence. Upgrading tag from standard Injury to Short-Term Injury given the fairly firm one-week runway reported.

MIXED SIGNALS (10/7): one Commanders Wednesday practice-report source lists White (shoulder) as a non-participant again ahead of Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants, while other beat reporting from earlier this week (RotoBaller, ~10/5) had the team believing he'd practice and "should be ready to go." Treat his exact Wednesday participation as unconfirmed pending Washington's official posted report; keeping the Short-Term Injury tag given the generally positive one-week-absence framing from multiple outlets.

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants -- back to practicing in full after missing last week's game in London with the shoulder injury, confirming the short-absence framing from last week's reporting. Downgrading tag from Short-Term Injury to Healthy now that he's resolved it.

NEW DESIGNATION (10/18): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag for Sunday's Week 6 game -- the specific injury behind it could not be confirmed via search as of this update (older shoulder and hamstring issues from Weeks 3-5 had already resolved, per prior notes). Flagging this as a real but not-yet-explained designation rather than assuming it's a repeat of the earlier shoulder trouble; Jacory Croskey-Merritt would see a bigger role if White sits. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch out of caution.

CLEARED FOR TONIGHT (10/17-18): full Thursday, then limited Friday and Saturday with the shoulder issue, but cleared to play tonight's Monday Night Football Week 6 game at San Francisco (10/19) alongside fellow cleared RB Austin Ekeler (chest) -- Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is out for the same game, so White projects for a bigger workload (SI/Yahoo Sports Commanders injury reports, 10/17-18). Keeping Health Watch given how often his ailments have recurred this season, though there's no game-status concern tonight.

Steelers D/ST.name: Steelers D/ST
bullets: DST5 in points per game in 2025 (7.8 PPG) even with T.J. Watt missing three games, powered by 27 forced turnovers and 48 sacks. Secondary got shredded at times — free agents Jamel Dean and Jaquan Brisker were brought in to fix that, but this remains one of the league's oldest defensive units.

Kyler Murray.name: Kyler Murray
bullets: Cleared the NFL's concussion protocol on Monday 9/21 (suffered the concussion in Week 1 vs. Green Bay on a hit from S Javon Bullard); missed Week 2 vs. Chicago, which Carson Wentz started and won 9-3.
Confirmed by HC Kevin O'Connell as the Week 3 starter at Tampa Bay (Sun 9/27) — no lingering designation, fully back atop the depth chart.

Note: Murray was released by Arizona in March 2026 and signed with Minnesota as a free agent (Arizona still covering most of his prior extension salary) — his Minnesota team tag is accurate, not a data error. Vikings are 2-0 to start the season.

Matt Gay.name: Matt Gay
bullets: Signed by Las Vegas as a free agent in March 2026 after previously kicking for the Colts and Rams; locked in as the Raiders' K1 after winning the camp competition over Kansei Matsuzawa.

NEW (10/17): added off waivers this week by a fantasy manager -- no new on-field news beyond his standard role as Las Vegas' placekicker behind an offense that leans heavily on Brock Bowers (see his note) in the passing game.
